title: Kubelet sets incorrect ownerReference apiVersion "core/v1" on PodCertificateRequest, breaking garbage collection
body:
### What happened?

When the kubelet creates a `PodCertificateRequest` (KEP-4317, `certificates.k8s.io/v1alpha1`), it sets the owning Pod's `ownerReference.apiVersion` to `"core/v1"` instead of the correct `"v1"`. The Kubernetes garbage collector cannot resolve `"core/v1"` as a valid API group/version for Pods — Pods belong to the legacy core API group, which has no group prefix, so the correct `apiVersion` is simply `"v1"`.

This causes the GC controller in controller-manager to log errors like:

```
error syncing item" err="unable to get REST mapping for core/v1/Pod."
```

When a Pod is deleted, its associated `PodCertificateRequest` objects are never garbage collected.

### What did you expect to happen?

The `ownerReference` on `PodCertificateRequest` objects should use `apiVersion: "v1"` for Pod references, consistent with how all other core-group resources are referenced throughout Kubernetes. The garbage collector should be able to resolve the owner, and when a Pod is deleted, its `PodCertificateRequest` objects should be automatically cleaned up.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Enable the `PodCertificateRequest` feature gate (KEP-4317) on the kubelet and kube-apiserver.
2. Deploy a Pod that triggers creation of a `PodCertificateRequest` (e.g., a Pod configured to use pod-identity certificates).
3. Inspect the resulting `PodCertificateRequest` object:
   ```bash
   kubectl get podcertificaterequest -o json | jq '.items[].metadata.ownerReferences'
   ```
4. Observe that `apiVersion` is set to `"core/v1"` instead of `"v1"`.
5. Delete the owning Pod.
6. Observe that the `PodCertificateRequest` is **not** garbage collected.
7. Check the kube-controller-manager logs for GC errors:
   ```
   error syncing item" err="unable to get REST mapping for core/v1/Pod."
   ```

### Anything else we need to know?

**Workaround:** A external signer controller can patch the owner reference from `"core/v1"` to `"v1"` on every `PodCertificateRequest` it reconciles. This restores proper garbage collection behavior.

First bug report, not sure if this should be opened here or commented on https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/4317

I am happy to submit the patch for this myself, after I figure out the contrib process. :) 

### Kubernetes version

Affects all versions implementing KEP-4317 (`PodCertificateRequest` / `certificates.k8s.io/v1alpha1` / `certificates.k8s.io/v1beta1`).

title: kubelet restart during intermittent network issues unmounts volumes of running pods
body:
### What happened?

During kubelet startup, it checks all volumes against the desired state (`desired_state_of_world_populator.go`). One of these steps is a `Get` request [on the PVC](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.28.0/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/populator/desired_state_of_world_populator.go#L487C21-L487C21). If that API call fails due to an intermittent network issue between kubelet and the API server(s), the pod is not considered to be in the list of pods to mount, leading to the [`operationExecutor` to call `UnmountVolume`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.28.0/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconciler_common.go#L166) in case of CSI-attached volumes. Although the volume will be mounted again as soon as the network issues resolves, the unmount/mount action leaves the bind mount in a broken and unrecoverable state depending on the CSI implementation (e.g. iscsi device name changed). To the user, nothing appears to be wrong as the pod is still in `Running` state. Only a manual deletion of the pod will fix it again.

We have observed this in production especially during maintenance where control-plane nodes are replaced and kubelet might not always be able to connect to the API server.

### What did you expect to happen?

I think kubelet should never call `UnmountVolume` on a running pod as it will leave the mounts in an unrecoverable state that is also not really visible to the user. The `desired_state_of_world_populator` should probably retry if it can't populate the desired state due to API server issues as it seems to make assumptions about the actual state which might be different.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

This is quite the edge-case and requires a perfect storm of a somewhat, but not completely broken connection, between kubelet and the API server plus a badly-timed restart of kubelet. If the connection to the API server is fully gone, kubelet won't get into the `desired_state_of_world_populator` routine during startup and all is fine. So naturally, it's hard to reproduce the issue. I was able to reprocuce it with a lot of luck and inserting some well timed iptables rules just after restarting kubelet but this is far from consistent. So instead I have created a small proxy with which it can be consistently reproduced and put it into [this reproducer repo](https://github.com/ctrox/kubelet-unmount-reproducer) with all the required files and steps.

1. Clone the reproducer
    ```bash
    git clone https://github.com/ctrox/kubelet-unmount-reproducer.git
    cd kubelet-unmount-reproducer
    ```
1. Create a kind cluster (`v0.20.0` with the node image `1.27.3` was used in my case)

    ```bash
    kind create cluster
    ```

1. Install a CSI driver like [`csi-driver-host-path`](https://github.com/kubernetes-csi/csi-driver-host-path/blob/master/docs/deploy-1.17-and-later.md)

    ```bash
    kubectl apply -f csi/
    ```

1. Create a PVC and a Pod that mounts it

    ```bash
    kubectl apply -f sts.yaml
    ```

1. Build, copy and run the `pvcfailproxy`

    ```bash
    GOOS=linux go build -o pvcfailproxy
    docker cp pvcfailproxy kind-control-plane:/usr/bin/
    docker exec -ti kind-control-plane pvcfailproxy
    ```

1. Modify `/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf` to use the `pvcfailproxy` and restart kubelet

    ```bash
    # in another terminal
    docker exec -ti kind-control-plane sed -i 's/kind-control-plane:6443/kind-control-plane:8443/g' /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf
    docker exec -ti kind-control-plane systemctl restart kubelet
    ```

1. Observe the kubelet log if it contains the expected error and unmount operation

    ```bash
    docker exec -ti kind-control-plane journalctl -fu kubelet
    ```

    ```bash
    desired_state_of_world_populator.go:295] "Error processing volume" err="error processing PVC default/data-web-0: failed to fetch PV pvc-8308a5fc-c8b2-42c2-8f1c-c0183ea2bce5 from API server ...
    reconciler_common.go:172] "operationExecutor.UnmountVolume started for volume \"pvc-8308a5fc-c8b2-42c2-8f1c-c0183ea2bce5\"
    ```

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

The issue was reproduced on a number of kubelet versions up to `1.28.0`. The API server version does not seem to be relevant.

title: PodLevelResources + DRA discovery
body:
As the [KEP for PodLevelResources](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/2837) evolved, it included accomodation for how its forward-looking API and behaviors will integrate with the existing container-specific resources APIs and behaviors (e.g., determining that pod-level resources take precedence; ref: https://github.com/ndixita/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-node/2837-pod-level-resource-spec/README.md#podspec-validation-rules).

Now that DRA is GA, and PodLevelResources are slated for beta in 1.34, we should fully flesh out the cooperative story here between the two. We can start with simply "what do we do when a pod spec includes both a pod-level resource configuration, and includes resource claims for one or more of its containers?".

It will probably make sense to update https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/2837 with our conclusions, and prioritize any needed implementation work, to optimize for a smooth graduation of PodLevelResources to GA.

title: [PodLevelResources] Inconcistency in computing QOSClass
body:
Almost everywhere we check whether a pod has pod level resources (PLRs) we don't differentiate between nil and empty PLRs. For example:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/3ec72e2e973664a0690bc7122c9cd291702b5f36/staging/src/k8s.io/component-helpers/resource/helpers.go#L73-L82

However, in `ComputePodQOS` we don't make this distinction:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/3ec72e2e973664a0690bc7122c9cd291702b5f36/pkg/apis/core/v1/helper/qos/qos.go#L96-L111

This could lead to some weird situations where you have a best-effort pod running with resources specified. For example:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name:      pause-plr
spec:
  resources: {}
  containers:
    - name:    pause
      image: registry.k8s.io/pause:latest
      resources:
        requests:
          cpu:    100m
          memory: 50Mi
        limits:
          cpu:    100m
          memory: 50Mi
```

I'm not sure exactly what the implications of this are, but since it breaks some fundamental assumptions, it's probably not good.

What was the reason for ignoring empty pod level resources?

We'll need to be careful about backwards compatibility when fixing this.

/assign @ndixita

title: Inability for Kubelet to clean a large number of containers during GC cycle
body:
### What happened?

In environments which use a significant amount of short-living pods (batch jobs, CI, etc.), kubelet is unable to clean containers with the GRPC error:
```
E1021 14:00:00.850972    2333 log.go:32] "ListContainers with filter from runtime service failed" err="rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = grpc: trying to send message larger than max (16795768 vs. 16777216)" filter="&ContainerFilter{Id:,State:nil,PodSandboxId:,LabelSelector:map[string]string{},}"
```

The problem here is that after the deprecation of the `--maximum-dead-containers` option, there are no ways left to force `kubelet` to clean the containers before the number of containers and the size of the response go up enough to make it impossible because of the message size, which means the node is always failing in this use case.

I am able to reproduce this behavior with ~18.5k containers (based on the value of `kubelet_running_containers{container_state="exited"}` metric) on the `containerd` runtime. 

### What did you expect to happen?

Container GC should or work out of the box with any number of containers, or it should have a tuning option to set a number of containers on which GC will be forcibly triggered.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Spawn on the node a large amount of short living containers. Target number is ~20k finished containers.
2. Wait until the GC will be triggered.
3. Inspect Kubelet logs and it's status. Node should be marked "NotReady" and GRPC errors should exist in logs.

Note: Better to use long names (40+ symbols) to make the reproduction faster.

### Anything else we need to know?

title: Support spec.MaxUnavailable=0  to use PDB with Jobs and prevent disruptions during node upgrades
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Add support to the `spec.MaxUnavailable` setting when set to 0 (zero) for PDBs used in combination with jobs. 

### **Context**
Currently, the [documentation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/run-application/configure-pdb/#arbitrary-controllers-and-selectors) states that `spec.MaxUnavailable` should not be used for resources that do not support the scale subresource, and when deployed,  the PDB shows this warning:  

> Warning  CalculateExpectedPodCountFailed  75s  controllermanager  Failed to calculate the number of expected pods: jobs.batch does not implement the scale subresource

However, by setting `spec.MaxUnavailable=0` in the PDB and use it in combination with a selector label to point the PDB to the Scaled Jobs, our testing has confirmed that it effectively prevents disruptions of Keda Scaled Jobs during node upgrades. 

**The reasoning is that when `spec.MaxUnavailable` is set to 0, there is not need to know the number of Pods running at a given moment.** 

Behavior observed during testing:

1. Node is cordoned 
2. Kubernetes attempts to evict pods running a job, and eviction is prevented by the PDB.
3. Kubernetes keeps attempting to evict the pods.
4. Jobs finish execution.
5. Kubernetes evicts the pods.
6. The upgrade can proceed.

**Example PDB Used** 
```
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: agent-scaledjob-pdb
spec:
  maxUnavailable: 0
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: agent-scaledjobs
```
 The selector label is also included in the ScaledJob
```
..
spec:
  jobTargetRef:
    activeDeadlineSeconds: 1500
    template:
      metadata:
        name: agent-scaledjob
        labels:
          app: agent-scaledjobs
..
```

### Why is this needed?

To avoid disruptions of jobs during node image or Kubernetes upgrades

title: kube-proxy fails to sync in nftables mode when newer nftables sets exist
body:
### What happened?

kube-proxy crashes repeatedly, causing the container network to not function.
```
E0205 20:24:21.385767       1 proxier.go:1217] "Failed to list existing sets" err="failed to run nft: signal: segmentation fault (core dumped)" ipFamily="IPv4"
E0205 20:24:22.721950       1 proxier.go:1788] "nftables sync failed" err="signal: segmentation fault (core dumped)" ipFamily="IPv4"
I0205 20:24:22.723136       1 proxier.go:1143] "Sync failed" ipFamily="IPv4" retryingTime="30s"
E0205 20:24:23.698591       1 proxier.go:1217] "Failed to list existing sets" err="failed to run nft: signal: segmentation fault (core dumped)" ipFamily="IPv6"
E0205 20:24:24.761438       1 proxier.go:1788] "nftables sync failed" err="signal: segmentation fault (core dumped)" ipFamily="IPv6"
I0205 20:24:24.761928       1 proxier.go:1143] "Sync failed" ipFamily="IPv6" retryingTime="30s"
```

### What did you expect to happen?

kube-proxy should correctly setup nftables rules.


### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Run a container in the host namespace with a newer version of nftables (1.1.3+), for example Fedora 43. Add a nft set in the container:
```
nft add table test_table
nft add set test_table test_set '{ type ifname; elements = { "test" } }'
```

Then delete the kube-proxy pod on the host, and example the logs on the new pod.


### Anything else we need to know?

kube-proxy in nftables mode crashes repeatedly on hosts where newer versions of nftables (eg 1.1.3) have created sets in the same network namespace.

I found a fix for the crash in newer nftables here (it appears to be related to udata being present on newer nft sets):
https://git.netfilter.org/nftables/commit/?id=be737a1986bfee0ddea4bee7863dca0123a2bcbc

It's probably a good idea to build kube-proxy with a patched version of nftables to avoid the crash, but not use anything newer than nftables 1.1.1 as it could then potentially break other unpatched nftables in CNIs etc.

title: Pod-level limits defaults not set when all containers have limits set and pod-level request is set
body:
As per the requirements listed in the KEP, pod-level limits are set to aggregated container limits if all containers have limits set. Please check rows 10, 12 from the table in the KEP:

https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/d57336d85b8673959916529873e71010a5d2a4fd/keps/sig-node/2837-pod-level-resource-spec/README.md?plain=1#L503-L507

The implementation is setting only pod-level requests defaults as per different scenarios. 
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/98e6935d436d5068b3549e651e629f76ec96e3f7/pkg/apis/core/v1/defaults.go#L198

The bug fix involves adding the defaulting logic for pod-level limits such that when pod-level requests are set, and pod-level limits are unset and "all containers"  have limits set then pod-level limits should be defaulted to aggregated container limits.

Instead of adding to the existing in defaults.go, it is recommended to limit this change to  podStrategy#PrepareForCreate and podResizeStrategy#PrepareForUpdate and also guard the implementation behind a feature gate - PodLevelResourcesFixUpdateDefaulting

title: RFE: Kubectl wait for multiple conditions
body:
**What would you like to be added**:
I'd like `kubectl wait` to support multiple wait conditions at once so these are evaluated on the resource with the same ResourceVersion. Like:
```
kubectl wait <resource> --for='condition=Available=True' --for='condition=Progressing=False' --for='condition=Degraded=False
```

**Why is this needed**:
The current workaround
```
kubectl wait <resource> --for='condition=Available=True' && \
kubectl wait <resource> --for='condition=Progressing=False' && \
kubectl wait <resource> --for='condition=Degraded=False'
```
isn't atomic and the first condition can change before it evaluates the next one. It's also slower and uses more calls to the apiserver.

/sig cli
fyi @soltysh

title: image pull credential verification doesn't work
body:
### What happened?

I wanted to use a recently introduced feature called "image pull credential verification". It has been described at:

1. https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/images/#ensureimagepullcredentialverification
2. https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/2535-ensure-secret-pulled-images
3. https://kubernetes.io/blog/2025/05/12/kubernetes-v1-33-ensure-secret-pulled-images-alpha/

I execute scenario with following conditions:

1. registry always requires authentication for the image in question
2. two sample pods are created which use the same image
3. pod definition requests to be scheduled to a specific node and it is always started there
4. the node does not have the image locally initially

The scenario:

1. pod A is started in namespace A without specifying service account or image secrets
2. default service account in ns A has a secret attached for the registry in question
3. kubelet pulls the image successfully
4. pod B is started in namespace B, the default service account has no secrets attached
5. pod B is successfully started but it should fail, this is the problem of this issue

This is what I observe. When the second pod is created an event is generated:

> $ k get events | grep 'already present' | tail -n1
> 42m         Normal    Pulled                 pod/sample-pod   Container image "zot.kube01.pemlab.net:5001/docker-io/rockylinux/rockylinux:10" already present on machine and can be accessed by the pod

This means the verification passed by it should not.

I have a standard configuration of kubelet with imagePullCredentialsVerificationPolicy set to NeverVerifyPreloadedImages. When this setting is changed to AlwaysVerify the attempt fails properly with message about missing credentials.

i did some digging in the source code to find the cause of it. On the second pod the kubelet thinks the image was not pulled by kubelet so it is treated like a preloaded image. After the first pod is created I see this:

```
$ jq . /var/lib/kubelet/image_manager/pulled/sha256-dd81f502dc5e7f8b60445496abe590916d606411d7c474a2e18e4a42e4e82151
{
  "kind": "ImagePulledRecord",
  "apiVersion": "kubelet.config.k8s.io/v1beta1",
  "lastUpdatedTime": "2026-02-14T09:41:58Z",
  "imageRef": "zot.kube01.pemlab.net:5001/docker-io/rockylinux/rockylinux@sha256:b86cb4305db4c29abb1e3a1257fefccc184b5e4a94378e02844b340845ef9460",
  "credentialMapping": {
    "zot.kube01.pemlab.net:5001/docker-io/rockylinux/rockylinux": {
      "kubernetesSecrets": [
        {
          "uid": "eeb25318-beff-46d0-bb24-f0c871a11e25",
          "namespace": "kube-system",
          "name": "zot",
          "credentialHash": "0bd56ac49132f1c4ffbf88affd024c6888e40d35fb6c9e10fef0e0b19a09fb06"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

The ns A is the kube-system in this case. Note the imageRef as it will be used below. It has a proper sha for rockylinux:10 for linux/amd64 platform at the time this issue is created. zot registry is being used and the /docker-io/** path needs authentication.

The message is generated from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.35/pkg/kubelet/images/image_manager.go#L257. The function receives argument of requestedImage with value "zot.kube01.pemlab.net:5001/docker-io/rockylinux/rockylinux:10". In imagePullPrecheck it uses imageService to resolve the image to an imageRef and it receives a value of "812a83d5aec123cbd962ba7cd1e22266db0fe2b3a0b49cb4e9aa521d13ad214f". It matches:
```
$ crictl inspecti zot.kube01.pemlab.net:5001/docker-io/rockylinux/rockylinux:10 | yq .status.id
812a83d5aec123cbd962ba7cd1e22266db0fe2b3a0b49cb4e9aa521d13ad214f
```

The call in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.35/pkg/kubelet/images/image_manager.go#L253 uses the requestedImage and imageRef to decide if the image needs to be pulled or not. The MustAttemptImagePull contains a lot of conditionals and yet it doesn't have any debug logging. I had to modify the source code and add print statements everywhere to understand what is going on. The https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.35/pkg/kubelet/images/pullmanager/image_pull_manager.go#L211 tries to find by imageRef and returns nil, false, nil. There are no intents at this time so imagePulledByKubelet stays with false value. This in turn is processed by the policy and we have the decision.

Now I wondered why the find failed. The records are stored in memory. The lookup in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.35/pkg/kubelet/images/pullmanager/mem_pullrecords.go#L197 uses the imageRef into a map. The key isn't there. So I made an investigation when keys are added and the added key was: 

```
zot.kube01.pemlab.net:5001/docker-io/rockylinux/rockylinux@sha256:b86cb4305db4c29abb1e3a1257fefccc184b5e4a94378e02844b340845ef9460
```

and this is what is read from /var/lib/kubelet/image_manager/pulled.

I tested this with cri-o and containerd. There is no difference. I wonder how this verification can ever work if there is always mismatch is inserted and lookedup keys ?

I have tested this with the directory clean and a fresh start of kubelet and the directory populated with files and the result is the same. The cache is populated with very long keys yet lookups are done with short imageID as reported by crictl.

### What did you expect to happen?

I expect the kubelet to verify the credentials again but it doesn't do it.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Scenario in the issue description.

title: Add support for tracing in scheduler
body:
### What would you like to be added?

The scheduler should generate an OTEL trace for a single scheduling attempt of a pod.

### Why is this needed?

We've observed slow scheduling attempts for pods which can be cumbersome to investigate with multiple scheduling plugins enabled. It would be very useful to have a trace for a single pod scheduling attempt. The trace context could also be propagated to custom scheduler plugins. 

One benefit of this over the existing log-based `utiltrace` is downstream clients that have already instrumented OTEL tracing (ie. http clients) could now be visualised in the context of a scheduling attempt.

The existing `utiltrace` is quite useful, but is k8s specific. Given [other k8s components](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/cluster-administration/system-traces/#component-traces) standardising around OTEL traces, feels appropriate for the scheduler to as well.

title: Service controller memory leak:  `lastSyncedNodes` entries not cleared when Services are deleted
body:
### What happened?

**What happened?**

 `kube-controller-manager` / cloud-provider Service controller shows problematic memory behavior around `lastSyncedNodes`, including:

- **(1) Stale retention / steady-state memory pressure** due to intentionally storing per-Service node slices.
- **(2) A real leak / unbounded growth bug** because `lastSyncedNodes` entries are not cleared when a Service is deleted.

In `staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go`, the controller stores (per Service key) a slice of `*v1.Node` pointers (from the node informer lister) in `lastSyncedNodes`. When the Service is deleted and the load balancer deletion path runs, the controller currently does **not** delete the corresponding `lastSyncedNodes[key]` entry.

As a result, repeated create/delete cycles of Services (especially when Service names are continuously new/unique, e.g. hashed) cause `lastSyncedNodes` to grow unbounded and retain node slices indefinitely, resulting in steadily increasing memory usage over time.

**Two related issues**
1) **Stale retention / memory pressure (even without Service deletion):**  
   `lastSyncedNodes` intentionally retains a per-Service `[]*v1.Node`. In large clusters (many Nodes, large Node objects), this can significantly increase steady-state memory usage because the controller holds strong references to large Node objects across sync cycles.

2) **Leak / unbounded growth under Service churn (bug):**  
   When a Service is deleted, its `lastSyncedNodes` entry is not removed. If Services are repeatedly created and deleted with unique names (e.g., hashed), the map grows without bound and can additionally retain multiple generations of `*v1.Node` instances (Nodes update frequently), causing continued memory growth over time.


**Additional context**

Nodes are updated frequently (e.g., NodeStatus updates and/or node lease heartbeats), producing continuous watch `MODIFIED` events. The node informer updates its store/indexer accordingly, and listers return the latest versions of `*v1.Node` objects.

Therefore, over time the controller may observe new `*v1.Node` instances (i.e., different Go object pointers) for the same logical Node names.

**Why the churn case can become unbounded**

`lastSyncedNodes` is keyed by Service. If Service keys are not removed on deletion, every create/delete cycle with a new (unique) Service name leaves behind an additional map entry. Each entry retains a `[]*v1.Node` obtained from the node lister at that time.

Because Nodes are frequently updated (status/lease), lister results across time may contain different `*v1.Node` object instances (different pointers) even for the same logical Nodes. Therefore, stale map entries can retain multiple generations of Node objects, causing cumulative and potentially unbounded memory growth.


### What did you expect to happen?

For (2) the leak bug: when a Service is deleted (and/or load balancer deletion is processed), the controller should remove the corresponding entry from `lastSyncedNodes` so the stored node slice (and referenced objects) can be garbage-collected.

(1) is mentioned as impact/pressure; (2) is the primary correctness bug in this issue.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

One possible reproducer:
1. Run cloud-controller-manager (or the relevant controller-manager binary enabling this Service controller) with a cluster that has N Nodes.
2. Repeatedly create and delete Services of type `LoadBalancer` (generate unique names, e.g. hashed names).
3. Observe process RSS/heap growing steadily over time.
4. Heap profiles show growth dominated by retained `[]*v1.Node` reachable from `Controller.lastSyncedNodes`.

### Anything else we need to know?

additional notes:

- `lastSyncedNodes` is keyed by Service. If Service keys are not removed on deletion, every create/delete cycle with a new (unique) Service name leaves behind an additional map entry. Each entry retains a `[]*v1.Node` obtained from the node lister at that time.

- Because Nodes are frequently updated (status/lease), lister results across time may contain different `*v1.Node` object instances (different pointers) even for the same logical Nodes. Therefore, stale map entries can retain multiple generations of Node objects, causing cumulative and potentially unbounded memory growth.

title: kube-apiserver fails to start because start-service-ip-repair-controllers PostStartHook fails
body:
### What happened?

When upgrading a Kubernetes cluster from v1.32 to v1.33 by creating new control plane nodes with v1.33 manifests, the kube-apiserver fails to start with admission errors. 
```
0115 20:56:16.106534   # log start
...
E0115 20:56:24.741991       1 repairip.go:372] "Unhandled Error" err="the ClusterIP [IPv4]: 10.211.95.185 for Service <namespace foo>/<service bar>is not allocated; repairing" logger="UnhandledError"
...
Trace[295533714]: ---"Write to database call failed" len:247,err:ipaddresses.networking.k8s.io "10.211.95.185" is forbidden: not yet ready to handle request 10000ms (20:56:34.744)
Trace[295533714]: [10.000527316s] [10.000527316s] END
E0115 20:56:34.745027       1 repairip.go:235] "Unhandled Error" err="ipaddresses.networking.k8s.io \"10.211.95.185\" is forbidden: not yet ready to handle request" logger="UnhandledError"
I0115 20:56:34.746095       1 repairip.go:236] Shutting down ipallocator-repair-controller
I0115 20:56:34.834949       1 healthz.go:280] informer-sync,poststarthook/start-service-ip-repair-controllers check failed: readyz
[-]informer-sync failed: 4 informers not started yet: [*v1.Pod *v1.ServiceAccount *v1.Secret *v1.Namespace]
[-]poststarthook/start-service-ip-repair-controllers failed: not finished
...
I0115 20:57:06.335471       1 healthz.go:280] informer-sync,poststarthook/start-service-ip-repair-controllers check failed: readyz
[-]informer-sync failed: 1 informers not started yet: [*v1.Secret] # v1.Namespace informer is ready  
[-]poststarthook/start-service-ip-repair-controllers failed: not finished
...
F0115 20:57:18.630248       1 hooks.go:204] PostStartHook "start-service-ip-repair-controllers" failed: unable to perform initial IP and Port allocation check

```

We think this is a race condition introduced by new code path when `MultiCIDRServiceAllocator` is enabled by default in v1.33.  
`start-service-ip-repair-controllers` reads clusterIPs from all `Services` objects and creates `IPAddresses` objects if they are not found from cache. Since we are upgrading from v1.32, where `MultiCIDRServiceAllocator` is disabled, ETCD does not contain any `IPAddresses` objects. 
`start-service-ip-repair-controllers` therefore does not read any existing `IPAddresses` objects from cache and attempts to create them. However, at this point, the `ipaddresses.networking.k8s.io` API is not yet ready. As a result, `start-service-ip-repair-controllers` failes and the kube-apiserver never becomes ready.

Because we have a large number of namespaces, `v1.Namespace` informer takes more time to become ready, which increases the likelihood of this issue occurring in our cluster.
In v1.32 `MultiCIDRServiceAllocator` is disabled. The `start-service-ip-repair-controllers`  implementation only invokes the internal `RangeRegistry` API, which is initialized earlier, so this issue did not exist.



### What did you expect to happen?

The kube-apiserver should start successfully and the repair controller should create missing `IPAddress` objects for existing `Services`, either by:
1. Waiting for admission plugins to be ready before attempting writes
2. Deferring repair work until after startup completes
3. Retrying failed operations instead of terminating

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Prerequisites:
- Cluster with large number of `Namespaces` and `Services` 
- `MultiCIDRServiceAllocator` feature gate previously disabled

Steps:
1. Prepare v1.33 kube-apiserver manifests with `MultiCIDRServiceAllocator` enabled by default
2. Start kube-apiserver
3. Observe API server fails to start

title: Feature Request: Generate a Kubernetes Release Artifact On Releases That Lists Feature Gate Default Enalbed/Disabled status
body:
### What would you like to be added?

This issue requests adding a new release artifact that lists the feature gates in a release and whether they are enabled / disabled by default.

If we had this, it would help k/website code verify that the machine readable feature gate metadata are correct - see https://github.com/kubernetes/website/tree/main/content/en/docs/reference/command-line-tools-reference/feature-gates.

Additionally a release artifact that is properly the "source of truth" for what feature gates in a release are enabled /disabled could additionally be used for Kubernetes feature: Compatibility Versions related testing (ex: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/127947)

Related comment: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128138#issuecomment-2423882866

### Why is this needed?

A release artifact that lists the feature gates in a release and whether they are enabled / disabled by default is needed because currently the k/website which tracks what feature gates are enabled at each version is updated in a bespoke manual way and could use a published release artifact for correctness validation.  The current approach can lead to deltas and missed updates if things are changed but not updated pre/post release.  Here is an issue for example that notes some feature gates deltas from k8s releases vs k/website:
https://github.com/kubernetes/website/issues/47996

By creating a release artifact for each version, the k/website could use this artifact to verify and ensure correctness

/cc @sftim 
/assign @aaron-prindle

title: [EventedPLEG] EventedPLEG should detect resize completion rapidly
body:
### What would you like to be added?

EventedPLEG should detect completion of pod resizing in the runtime as rapidly as GenericPLEG.

Since v1.32 (#128518), GenericPLEG polls container resources in the runtime at resizing a pod so that it detects resize completion rapidly. This poll is actuated when GenericPLEG relists pods regularly:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d36322f8d76c8e2a456e381bcc6bb43e4bbe602c/pkg/kubelet/pleg/generic.go#L314-L327

EventedPLEG depends on GenericPLEG for this polling:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d36322f8d76c8e2a456e381bcc6bb43e4bbe602c/pkg/kubelet/pleg/evented.go#L430-L432

When EventedPLEG is enabled, GenericPLEG relists pods every five minutes:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d36322f8d76c8e2a456e381bcc6bb43e4bbe602c/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L197

Then, it takes at most five minutes till pod resize appears to be completed in the API.


### Why is this needed?

Pod resize should complete as quickly as if EventedPLEG is not enabled.

Considering maturity of features, I don’t think this issue blocks promotion of InPlacePodVerticalScaling. This issue should be solved for promoting EventedPLEG.

title: Some crashed or OOMKilled containers fail to restart in v1.35
body:
### What happened?

After upgrading Kubernetes from v1.34.2 to v1.35.0, we observed a scenario where a pod with multiple containers does not restart a crashed application container, leaving the pod in an Error state indefinitely.

This behavior was not observed on v1.34.2. Reverting the kubelet back to v1.34.2 causes the issue to disappear.

**Observed Behavior:**
The main container terminates but never restarts:
```
State:          Terminated
  Reason:       Error
  Exit Code:    2
  Started:      Tue, 27 Jan 2026 16:11:01 +0000
  Finished:     Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:08:55 +0000
Ready:          False
Restart Count:  0
```

The sidecar container continues to run normally:
```
State:          Running
Started:        Tue, 27 Jan 2026 16:10:54 +0000
Ready:          True
Restart Count:  0
```

Pod conditions show:
```
Conditions:
  Type                        Status
  PodReadyToStartContainers   True
  Initialized                 True
  Ready                       False
  ContainersReady             False
  PodScheduled                True
```

No useful logs or errors appear in `kubectl describe pod` output, events, or `kubelet` logs.

**Notes:**
- This issue seems to only affect pods with more than one container
- We are unsure whether it's just pods with an `initContainer` or does it also apply to `container` sidecars
- Manually killing the process in the sidecar container or deleting the pod helps getting it back to working state
- `RestartAllContainersOnContainerExits` is not enabled

**Possibly related?**
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134345

### What did you expect to happen?

Containers should reliably restart every time they crash.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

The best way we found to reproduce this is by running a pod with 2 containers: an initContainer with `restartPolicy: Always` and an application container that we manually crash with `kill 1` command.
It might not work right first time, but we managed to reproduce this multiple times getting pods stuck in Error state that they never recover from automatically.

title: Interning for API Server and controller memory reduction
body:
### What would you like to be added? I propose implementing object interning (deduplication) techniques in the Kubernetes API Server and control plane components to significantly reduce memory usage. Specifically, this proposal suggests: * **String Interning:** Modifying protobuf deserialization to intern strings during decoding. [PoC](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/c8ff1377dcebe18effe75166507bf624afbe008e) * **ManagedFields Deduplication:** Implementing custom deserialization for FieldsV1 (Server-Side Apply metadata) to reuse existing objects. [PoC](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/627898045327206f37b347c65ba84d0fdb69b361) * **JSON Optimization:** Evaluating a migration to json/v2 for built-in interning support. Work related to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/134375 ### Why is this needed? As Kubernetes adoption grows, particularly with the rise of AI/ML workloads, cluster scales are pushing beyond traditional limits. * **High Replication & Redundancy:** We are increasingly seeing Jobs, Deployments, and StatefulSets scaling to 10,000+ replicas. In these highly replicated workloads, the PodSpec is largely identical across replicas, leading to massive redundancy in memory. Etcd already started getting feature request to handle it better [etcd-io/etcd#21305](https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/issues/21305), * **Memory Bottlenecks:** The API server consumes approximately 10x the raw resource size in memory to maintaining latest state and history in watch cache and latest state in informer. With the increase in replication and resource complexity, memory overhead becomes the primary limiting factor for horizontal scaling. * **ManagedFields Overhead:** By design, Server-Side Apply (SSA) metadata accounts for >50% of the stored resource size[KEP-555](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-api-machinery/555-server-side-apply#scalability). Since this data is highly repetitive, it is a prime candidate for deduplication. ### Alternatives Considered * **Reflect-based interning:** Using reflection to intern strings after deserialization was rejected because it incurred a 2.5x CPU overhead and increased allocations by 25%. * **Full PodSpec interning:** Caching and reusing the entire PodSpec struct was explored but deemed too risky. Initial implementations caused API server crashes due to concurrent map writes, and while deep-copying mitigated this, the approach remains fragile due to hidden mutations (e.g., defaulting, admission). * **Dropping unused Informer fields:** We considered dropping unused fields from the API Server's internal informers. However, this provided only marginal benefits (~5% memory reduction) restricted to the API server, without addressing the broader KCP memory footprint. ### Analysis & Results We evaluated these techniques using a synthetic benchmark with a realistic workload. 1. **Optimistic microbenchmark Results (per object)** 13 pod manifests decoded 10,000 times. | Technique | Decode time [µs] | KBs retained per object | KBs allocated per object | Allocations per object | | ---------------------------------------- | ---------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------- | | Base | 29.33 | 24.15 | 29.13 | 346.0 | | ReflectStrings | 87.63 (+198.8%) | 19.07 (-21.0%) | 34.34 (+17.9%) | 433.0 (+25.1%) | | DecodeString | 35.01 (+19.3%) | 19.07 (-21.1%) | 24.17 (-17.0%) | 154.0 (-55.5%) | | ManagedFields | 27.19 (~) | 19.10 (-20.9%) | 24.20 (-16.9%) | 343.0 (-0.9%) | | DecodeString
ManagedFields | 33.51 (~) | 14.02 (-42.0%) | 19.24 (-34.0%) | 151.0 (-56.4%) | | PodSpec | 12.29 (-58.1%) | 13.29 (-45.0%) | 14.10 (-51.6%) | 115.0 (-66.8%) | | DecodeString
ManagedFields
PodSpec | 11.11 (-62.1%) | 6.98 (-71.1%) | 7.93 (-72.8%) | 56.0 (-83.8%) | 2. **Pessimistic microbenchmark Results (per object)** 13 unique pod manifests decoded 10 times (expected times a healthy pod is written in deployment cycle) | Technique | Decode time [µs] | KBs retained per object | KBs allocated per object | Allocations per object | | ---------------------------------------- | ---------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------- | | Base | 45.60 | 24.15 | 29.13 | 346.0 | | ReflectStrings | 148.65 (+226.0%) | 19.84 (-17.9%) | 37.75 (+29.6%) | 541.0 (+56.4%) | | DecodeString | 75.57 (+65.7%) | 19.56 (-19.0%) | 26.35 (-9.5%) | 222.0 (-35.8%) | | ManagedFields | 41.25 (-9.5%) | 19.96 (-17.4%) | 25.89 (-11.1%) | 344.0 (-0.6%) | | DecodeString

title: DeepDerivative silently ignores trailing slice item removals
body:
## What happened?

`equality.Semantic.DeepDerivative()` in `k8s.io/apimachinery` does not detect when items are removed from the end of a slice. It only compares up to `len(a)` items (the "desired" side), so any extra trailing items in `b` (the "existing" side) are silently ignored.

This means if a controller uses `DeepDerivative` to determine whether an object needs updating, removing items from the end of a slice (e.g., container args, env vars, volume mounts) will never trigger an update.

## What did you expect to happen?

`DeepDerivative(a, b)` should return `false` when `a` has fewer slice items than `b`, since the desired state differs from the existing state.

## How to reproduce

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/equality"
)

func main() {
	desired := []string{"--foo", "--bar"}
	existing := []string{"--foo", "--bar", "--baz"}

	// Returns true — the removal of "--baz" is NOT detected
	fmt.Println(equality.Semantic.DeepDerivative(desired, existing)) // true
}
```

## Root cause

In `staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/conversion/equalities.go`, the `deepDerivative` method has this logic for slices:

```go
for i := range a { // iterates only up to len(a)
    if !e.deepDerivative(a[i], b[i]) {
        return false
    }
}
return true
```

It iterates only over the indices of \`a\` (desired). If \`a\` has 2 items and \`b\` has 3, the third item in \`b\` is never examined.

## Impact

This affects any controller that relies on \`DeepDerivative\` to detect spec changes for reconciliation. Specific real-world impact:

- **[OCPBUGS-65879](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-65879)**: In OpenShift HyperShift, removing \`--image-overrides\` arguments from a container's args list was not detected, leaving stale configuration on cluster objects indefinitely.

## Additional context

The trailing slice behavior is **not** documented and appears to be unintentional. 

/sig api-machinery
/kind bug
/area apiserver

kubectl get <category> should filter out 403 errors from non authorized types
body:
### What happened?

The categories field within CRDs allows users to discover crds, see https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/extend-kubernetes/custom-resources/custom-resource-definitions/#categories
> Categories is a list of grouped resources the custom resource belongs to (eg. all). You can use kubectl get <category-name> to list the resources belonging to the category.

Underneath kubectl is leveraging the k8s api discovery endpoint documented at https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/kubernetes-api/#unaggregated-discovery e.g. /apis/mycorp.com/v1 to discover all resources including their categories and then query all resources matching the required category (e.g. "claim")

However, the discovery api is not filtering the types against lack of authorization, aka the discovery api is returning types that the requester may not have any authorization.

As a result, `kubectl get <category>` displays errors from non-authorized resources.

Let's take the example of the crossplane library which uses the following categories to support discovering the following type of resources dynamically loaded into a cluster
* `claim`: crossplane claims (platform user) 
* `composite` : crossplane XRs (platform engineer)
* `composition`: crossplane compositions (platform engineer)
* `managed`: crossplane managed resources (platform engineer)
* `xrd`: crossplane composite resource definitions

Each category is used by many CRDs targetting different roles in a k8s multi tenant cluster.

`kubectl get claim` will return authorized CRs along with errors for unauthorized CRs such as the following

`Error from server (Forbidden): mariadatabasebackups.mycorp.org forbidden: User "xxx" cannot list resource "mariadatabasebackups" in API group "mycorp.org" in the namespace "my-namespace"`

The current kubectl user has to explicitly filter out errors from stderr and fix the unreliable exit status

### What did you expect to happen?

 `kubectl get <category>`  should offer a flag to only return resources from authorized resources types,  filtering out 403 errors from non authorized resources 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

* deploy crd1 and crd2 referencing category "mycategory"
* grant service account permission to list/get crd1 but not crd2
* type `kubectl get mycategory`

### Anything else we need to know?

There are related documented decisions to not support acl-filtered list operations on resources:
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/112686#issuecomment-1260952844
* https://github.com/kubernetes/community/issues/1486#issuecomment-350741039
> What you are describing is acl-filtered list, which is desired, but not able to be implemented without breaking watch semantics. If the content of a list call depends on two dimensions (actual resources present AND current state of ACL), a single resourceVersion will not represent the results correctly.
> 
> Additionally, if the API server does not have a way to know when ACLs have changed, it does not know when to react by sending add events for newly granted resources or remove events for newly denied resources)

But I did not see related discussion/decisions to acl-filterered operations on types (what does `kubectl get <category>` or `kubectl api-resources`). Also `kubectl get <category>`  does not support --watch

```
kubectl get claim --watch
error: you may only specify a single resource type
```

Service Controller Does Not Reconcile When LoadBalancer Status is Cleared
body:
### What happened?

The cloud-provider service controller doesn't trigger reconciliation when a LoadBalancer Service's status is cleared by external controllers like GitOps tools. This happens when the Service spec includes `loadBalancerIP` and the GitOps tool updates the Service, clearing the status field. Even though the cloud load balancer continues to function normally, the Service shows a pending status indefinitely because the controller only detects changes to the Service spec, not the status.

### What did you expect to happen?

When a LoadBalancer Service's status is cleared during a resource update, the service controller should detect this change and reconcile by querying the cloud provider to restore the correct LoadBalancer ingress information.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a LoadBalancer Service with `loadBalancerIP` specified in the spec:
   ```yaml
   apiVersion: v1
   kind: Service
   metadata:
     name: test-service
   spec:
     type: LoadBalancer
     loadBalancerIP: 10.50.71.131
     ports:
     - port: 80
   ```
2. Verify the Service has `Status.LoadBalancer.Ingress` populated with the LB IP
3. Apply the same Service YAML using a GitOps tool or kubectl, which clears the status field
4. Observe the Service status remains empty/pending even though the cloud load balancer exists and functions correctly

### Anything else we need to know?

The `needsUpdate()` function in `staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go` (lines 557-616) only checks `Service.Spec` fields like ports, annotations, and IPs. It doesn't check if `Service.Status.LoadBalancer.Ingress` has been cleared.

### What would you like to be added?

Request : Expose the source IP address in the AdmissionReview Object.

Context :

We would like to have Admission Controller make decisions on a particular exec/attach request depending upon where the request originated from i.e the client source IP address.

The source IP address is not available in the AdmissionReview object so it is currently not possible to do validation on IP address at Admission Control.

Due to a security policy, we want users to interact (exec, attach) with their K8S workloads only from certain machines and dis-allow all interactions from all other machines.

title: DRA: kubelet: Allow option to skip plugin calls and/or NodeUnprepareResources specifically if noop
body:
Pods with ResourceClaims will be stuck in Terminating for as long as NodeUnprepareResources has not been called (which is WAI per discussion in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/129402), as kubelet blocks on a successful NodeUnprepareResourcesResponse. In cases where a given plugin's NodeUnprepareResources would be a no-op, this unnecessarily introduces the potential for a faulty plugin to needlessly block node or driver upgrades when the drain cannot be completed. At an even more extreme end, even NodePrepareResources may be a no-op, unnecessarily introducing delays in pod startup on the node to contact the driver and recieve the response from the no-op prepare call. This issue seeks to make one, or both of these, more forgiving by one of two methods of softening kubelet's expectations regarding plugin prepare/unprepare calls:

1. Allow kubelet to recognize certain devices and/or device classes as no-op for node local preparation

* Kubelet assumes it must contact a DRA driver matching a Pod’s claim’s deviceclass when asked to run a Pod with a claim ([ref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.35/pkg/kubelet/cm/dra/manager.go#L318)) to perform node local operations
* That DRA driver is implemented as a kubelet plugin ([ref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.35/pkg/kubelet/cm/dra/plugin/dra_plugin_manager.go#L49)) of a specific interface (namely, has the NodePrepareResources and NodeUnprepareResources functions) and must return a valid NodePrepareResource response when preparing a claim ([ref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.35/pkg/kubelet/cm/dra/manager.go#L397))
* Some device classes do not require any node local operations
* Today, such device classes would still be required to stand up a driver matching the kubelet plugin interface; otherwise scheduled Pods will not run and do not know to be rescheduled
* In these cases, Kubelet should instead allow configured device classes not to require calls to their associated driver’s PrepareResources and UnprepareResources functions

2. Allow kubelet to recognize certain devices and/or device classes as kubeletplugin-less

* Device classes as described above may also implement their ResourceSlice publication off the node (such as in the case of multi-node logical devices), removing the need for any node local driver component at all
* Maintainers for such devices should not need to provide a completely no op driver, nor should cluster operators be forced to deploy and maintain such drivers, just to satisfy Kubelet’s interface requirements
* Kubelet should instead allow configured deviceclasses not to require a handle to a kubeletplugin driver at all

title: Add additional test coverage for HPA External Metrics framework
body:
We recently introduced a new testing framework in #136799 that enables testing HPA behavior using an External Metrics mock server.

Currently, the framework includes only a single test case (basic scale up and scale down), which is not sufficient to fully validate HPA behavior. We should expand the test coverage to ensure the framework works reliably across more realistic scenarios.

We propose adding the following test cases:

- [ ] Multiple Metrics: Verify that a single HPA can correctly handle two or more external metrics simultaneously.
- [ ] Stabilization Window: Ensure that the HPA does not scale too aggressively when metric values fluctuate rapidly, respecting the configured stabilization window.
- [ ] Scaling Limits: Validate that the configured scaling limits (behavior.scaleUp and behavior.scaleDown) are enforced correctly.

title: Tracking: Enable Kube-API-Linter rules
body:
This is issue is to help track the various Kube API Linter rules that have been implemented, and whether they are ready to be integrated into K/K. I've assessed each rule, including those in open issues that I think will be implemented and divided into categories

## When taking on an issue below

Start by commenting on this issue to say that you're going to take a particular issue. We want to make sure we don't duplicate work with multiple PRs for the same work.

Checkout the latest master branch and enable your chosen rule (or remove part of an exclusion if that's appropriate) in the  `hack/kube-api-linter/kube-api-linter.yaml` file. Run `hack/update-golangci-lint-config.sh` to update the config and then `hack/verify-golangci-lint.sh staging/src/k8s.io/api` to run the linter. This should only report newly found issues for your linter.

Assess existing issues, should they be excepted, or can they be fixed in a non-breaking way. If you are unsure, post on this thread for help on making that decision. In general, most issues reported by the linter **should not** be fixed by changing the existing Go types.

For linters with hundreds of violationsTake a look at how I've handled `optionalorrequired`, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134675. In this case we've built up a table of how many issues exist per API group and have decided to tackle each API group 1 by 1. We don't expect this to be the norm, but in some cases we do genuinely have hundreds of issues to trawl through to determine whether or not they can be fixed and how they can be fixed.

| dependenttags | N | N | Y | N | | Needs to be implemented in KAL [tracker](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kube-api-linter/issues/146). Would be used to enforce relationships like unionMember fields must be optional |
| markerscope | N | N | Y | N | | Needs to be implemented in KAL [tracker](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kube-api-linter/issues/148). Would ensure that tags are applied to the right scope, e.g. field vs object vs array vs map. Will need knowledge of DV markers |
| preferredmarkers | N | N | Y | N | | Needs to be implemented in KAL [tracker](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kube-api-linter/issues/139). Will be used to ensure usage of newer versions of markers, e.g. when we have taught everything about `+k8s:optional`, this will move usage of `+optional` to the new marker and prevent new usage of the old marker |
| defaultorrequired | N | N | Y | N | | Needs to be implemented in KAL [tracker](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kube-api-linter/issues/136). Prevent usage of default tags with required fields (configuration of conflictingmarkers already covers this). |
| minlength | N | N | Y | N | | [WIP PR in KAL](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kube-api-linter/pull/149). Will then need DV marker knowledge. Requires authors to think about the minimum length of strings/arrays/maps/structs. |
| references | N | N | Y | N | | Needs to be implemented in KAL [tracker](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kube-api-linter/issues/25). Ensure Ref/Refs is preferred over Reference/References. Is a naming convention configuration. |
| defaults | N | N | Y | N | | Needs to be implemented in KAL [tracker](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kube-api-linter/issues/22). Ensure we only use the default marker and no variation of it, both built-ins and CRDs share the same marker. |
| numericbounds | N | N | Y | N | | Needs to be implemented in KAL [tracker](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kube-api-linter/issues/18). Ensure all integer values set a minimum and maximum bound |
| enums | N | N | Y | N | | Needs to be implemented in KAL [tracker](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kube-api-linter/issues/17). Ensure enums are PascalCase, apart from specific exceptions that can be configured where this rule doesn't make sense. |

## Open questions

| - | - | - | - | - | - | - |

title: Liveness probe with an error doesn't trigger container restart
body:
### What happened?

We have a specific case when a health check would error out with `500 INTERNAL SERVER ERROR`. In this particular scenario, the readiness probe will correctly mark pod unready but the liveness probe does not trigger a container restart.

Here are some more details:
1. Kubernetes Server Version: v1.24.16.
2. An application pod is running a single container.
3. Both readiness and liveness probes are `httpGet` and are hitting the same `/healthcheck` endpoint.
4. Healthcheck endpoint is responding with `500 INTERNAL SERVER ERROR`.
5. The readiness probe does mark the container as "unready" as expected.
6. The liveness probe does not trigger a container restart, even after the multiple consecutive failures.

I confirmed that `restartPolicy: Always` and when I exec into the container and run curl, I do get the 500 INTERNAL SERVER ERROR, the same as what I see in the application logs. As per documentation, a failing liveness probe should be triggering a restart but it is not happening.

Here's the log from kubelet:
```
Jan 03 17:34:20 ip-1-1-1-1 kubelet[5845]: E0103 17:34:20.352585    5845 prober.go:118] "Probe errored" err="unexpected EOF" probeType="Liveness" pod="mynamespace/application-abc
```

Also, looking at the code [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.24/pkg/kubelet/prober/prober.go#L115-L124) the error does seem to be captured correctly by the probe but restart is not initiated.

Somehow the error is not being handled gracefully I assume. If I change it to an invalid port and cause a timeout the container gets restarted as expected. Also, switching from `httpGet` to `exec` type of healthcheck and running `curl http://localhost:8000/healthcheck` does trigger a restart so I suspect there is some bug with the httpGet probe itself.

This is what I see in the events:
```
Liveness probe errored: unexpected EOF
Readiness probe errored: unexpected EOF
```

### What did you expect to happen?

A failing healthcheck in a liveness probe would trigger a container restart.

```
containerMessage="Container abc  failed liveness probe, will be restarted"
```

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a deployment with an app that is crashing and returns 500

Configure healthceck like so:
```
    livenessProbe:
      failureThreshold: 3
      httpGet:
        path: /healthcheck
        port: healthcheck
        scheme: HTTP
      initialDelaySeconds: 3
      periodSeconds: 10
      successThreshold: 1
      timeoutSeconds: 3
    name: abc
    ports:
    - containerPort: 8000
      name: healthcheck
      protocol: TCP
    readinessProbe:
      failureThreshold: 3
      httpGet:
        path: /healthcheck
        port: healthcheck
        scheme: HTTP
      initialDelaySeconds: 3
      periodSeconds: 10
      successThreshold: 1
      timeoutSeconds: 3
```

title: KMS v2 add a DEK cache timeout option
body:
<!-- /sig sig-security -->

Hi everyone,

In [KMS v2](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/3299), the Data Encryption Key Seed (DEK Seed) lives in the k8s API server cache indefinitely until a k8s node stops or restarts.

Reason behind is to be more efficient with less calls to the KMS plugin.

But for some usecases, one might want to set a _DEK cache timeout_. After the amount of time of the _DEK cache timeout_, the DEK is cleared (erased) from the cache. And k8s will need to send a KMS v2 [DecryptRequest](https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/kms/apis/v2#DecryptRequest) in order to "revive" the DEK in the cache.

Default value should be an infinite cache timeout to stay in line with current KMSv2.

The configuration file could look like this.

```yaml
---
apiVersion: apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1
kind: EncryptionConfiguration
resources:
  - resources:
      - secrets
    providers:
      - kms:
          apiVersion: v2
          name: kms-server
          endpoint: unix:///run/user/1000/k8s-kms-plugin.sock
          timeout: 3s
          dekCacheTimeout: 0   # default value infinite cache timeout
          dekCacheTimeout: 30s # DEK is cleared from cache after 30 secondes
          dekCacheTimeout: 10m # DEK is cleared from cache after 10 minutes
          dekCacheTimeout: 1h  # DEK is cleared from cache after 1 hour
          dekCacheTimeout: 2d  # DEK is cleared from cache after 2 days
          dekCacheTimeout: 3w  # DEK is cleared from cache after 3 weeks
      - identity: {}
```

What is you opinion with this idea?

cc @IceManGreen

# KMS

https://github.com/kubernetes/kms/tree/master/apis/v2

/sig sig-security

title: reclaimPolicy: retainWithoutUuid
body:
# Context
I'm deploying an application through Pulumi (but a Helm Chart would be the same). This application deploys a PVC, bound to a PV with `persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain`.

When I `pulumi down` then `pulumi up`, the PVC doesn't bind to the same PV, it recreates a new one because the new PVC has a different `metadata.uid`

# Request

Would it be possible to have a `reclaimPolicy` that retains the volume, but removes `claimRef.uuid` (and maybe `claimRef.resourceVersion`) ?

# Purpose

This would allow attaching a PVC with the same claim (namespace, kind, name), but with a different UUID because it was recreated.

# Use Case

Phoenix pattern : destroying and rebuilding your infrastructure regularly
Facilitates development : during development, destroying and rebuilding is regular
Error restoration : should the PVC be destroyed accidentaly, and new one with the same spec can just be created

# Other mentions of this idea

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/65581#issuecomment-436550574
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/78997730/how-to-remove-claim-from-a-persistent-volume-when-it-was-released

title: add and use alternative APIs which support contextual logging
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Several staging repos, for example client-go, only have APIs which don't support contextual logging. Changing those APIs is typically not desirable because it can break large parts of the downstream ecosystem. Instead, we need to add alternative APIs (usually called `<something>WithContext`) which accept a context.

Such a context can replace an existing stop channel, add cancellation when there was no such stop channel, and last but not least be used to retrieve a logger for contextual logging. When using `context.WithCancelCause` in the caller and `context.Cause(ctx)` in the callee, additional information about the reason for canceling can be passed down, thus avoiding the uninformative "context canceled" messages.

The process for adding such alternatives is 

- Add an alternative `<something>WithContext` API to some package in staging
- Mark the original API with `// Contextual logging: <something>WithContext should be used instead of <something> in code which supports contextual logging.`
- Review that change with maintainers and merge it
- Temporarily replace `// Contextual logging: ...` with `//logcheck:context // ...`:

      sed -i -e 's;// *Contextual logging: ;//logcheck:context // ;' -e 's/Handle\(Error\|Crash\)WithContext should be used instead of/Handle\1WithContext or Handle\1WithLogger should be used instead of/'  $(git grep -l "// *Contextual logging: ")

- Run `hack/verify-golang-lint.sh` to find code which is supposed to support contextual logging and now needs to be updated to use `<something>WithContext` or (where available and applicable) `<something>WithLogger`
- Sometimes tests can or even should (for example, in the package itself) continue to use the function that got replaced. Use common sense to decide and `//nolint:logcheck // Intentionally using original function.` to suppress such warnings.
- Fix relevant issues, submit in one or more PRs:
  - try to align with OWNERS files so that a single approver is sufficient for a PR
  - reference `https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/126379` in the issue section of the PR description
- Once all of those PRs are merged, submit a PR which replaces the `// Contextual logging:  ...` with `//logcheck:context // ...`

This issue will be kept open and (if needed) reopened as long as there is work remaining, which can be checked with:
```
git grep  -e '// Contextual logging:'
```

### Special notes for contributors:

Please reach out on [Slack in the #wg-structured-logging channel](https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C020CCMUEAX) if there are questions.

Use `/wg structured-logging` to label PRs.

### Why is this needed?

Several of our binaries (e.g. kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler) have been converted to structured, contextual logging. However, they still emit unstructured, context-unaware log output because of the helper packages that they use.

- https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/1602
- https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/3077

title: APIService remains unhealthy due to kube-apiserver reusing connection to incorrect endpoint and not verifying server certificate
body:
### What happened?

When kube-apiserver is deployed on a new control-plane node before kube-proxy is running, the AvailableConditionController, which checks the availability of registered APIServices, may connect to the Service’s ClusterIP before it is proxied by kube-proxy. As a result, the connection can be routed to an external server that happens to be listening on the same IP, causing the APIService to be reported as unhealthy due to unexpected responses.

However, even after the kube-proxy runs and proxys the ClusterIP, because of transport-layer connection caching and the fact that kube-apiserver is hard-coded to skip server certificate validation (even when the APIService’s `insecureSkipTLSVerify` is set to false), the APIService can remain unhealthy until the kube-apiserver is restarted:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5151f58ef08d9fb26931019d6d844292aeb57637/staging/src/k8s.io/kube-aggregator/pkg/controllers/status/remote/remote_available_controller.go#L179-L184



### What did you expect to happen?

kube-apiserver should be able to recover from corner cases where it mistakenly establishes a connection to an incorrect server that never returns the expected response during APIService availability checks. It can be addressed either by verifying the server’s certificate when the APIService’s caBundle is provided, or by avoiding reuse of cached connections when the server returns an unexpected response.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Install an APIService with a caBundle configured and backed by a ClusterIP Service.
2. Run an HTTPS API server outside the cluster that listens to the ClusterIP and is routable from the cluster and returns 404 for unknown paths.
3. Add a new control-plane node where kube-apiserver starts before kube-proxy is scheduled on the node.
4. Check the kube-apiserver logs: the APIService continues to be reported as unhealthy due to 404 status code even after kube-proxy is running on the node.

body:
### What would you like to be added?

As of now, Kubernetes api server provides a mechanism to push events to a separate etcd cluster using the --etcd-servers-overrides="/events#" flag. This issue is to request similar mechanism for sending CRDs to separate etcd cluster.


### Why is this needed?

Primary motivation is to keep the main etcd cluster performant.

* CRD listing - Some workloads use their CRDs for events (example argo). These events cause issues similar to the Kubernetes native events - they have spiky writes and they keep getting LIST calls typically from monitoring tools. The motivation for moving these out of main etcd cluster is similar to the reasoning for moving Kubernetes events out of main etcd cluster.

* CRD count - Some CRDs produce millions of objects and affect the performance of main etcd cluster.

title: Pods with zero terminationGracePeriod are force-deleted
body:
### What happened?

This is spin-off from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/119273.

When a pod with `spec.terminationGracePeriod: 0` is deleted without force, it's force-deleted from the API server, without kubelet killing its containers and unmounting its volumes first.

This can be dangerous for StatefulSets. They should guarantee that only a single replica of a Pod runs, but KCM will start a new replica while the old replica is still running, because kubelet did not have enough time to kill it and unmount its volumes. This can be further emphasized when kubelet is not able to talk to the API server e.g. due to network partition or any other error. The old Pod can run for quite some time until its kubelet reconnects to the API server and realizes it should be killed, while the new Pod is running on another node. These two pods are sharing the same volume and may corrupt data of each other.

Surprisingly, `terminationGracePeriod: 1` is enough to prevent this behavior. The old Pod will be Terminating without any timeout (i.e. forver) until kubelet confirms the Pod is dead and its volumes unmounted.

### What did you expect to happen?

Pods should be deleted from the API server only after their containers are killed and their volumes unmounted.

Unless `--force` is used, but then user must deal with the consequences - pod volumes can get corrupted, as they may be used by multiple pods.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Run a StatefulSet with a single replica with `terminationGracePeriod: 0`.
2. Stop kubelet on the node where the replica starts .
3. After 5-6 minutes, node controller deletes the pod (without force), but the pod gets deleted from the API server because of `terminationGracePeriod: 0`.
4. Observe that a new replica starts, while the old replica is still running on the "problematic" node.

Check the same with `terminationGracePeriod: 1` - the old pod is *not* force-deleted and StatefulSet ensures that only a single replica runs. The Pod will be Terminating forever, or until the node reconnects to the cluster and kubelet kills the pod containers + unmounts its volumes.

### Anything else we need to know?

### Which tests are flaking?

k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/cache.cache 
* TestStressExpiringCache

### Since when has it been flaking?

[Triage](https://storage.googleapis.com/k8s-triage/index.html?test=k8s.io%2Fapimachinery%2Fpkg%2Futil%2Fcache.cache)

### Testgrid link

https://testgrid.k8s.io/ibm-ppc64le-periodics#ci-kubernetes-unit-ppc64le-master

### Reason for failure (if possible)

This flake is observed in architectures that follow [Weak Memory Model](https://preshing.com/20120930/weak-vs-strong-memory-models/) such as `ppc64le`. Unlike architectures with a strong memory mode, like the `amd64`, the PowerPC CPU does not strictly guarantee that memory writes happen in the order as they appear in code.

In this scenario, the CPU likely updated the Map Pointer before it finished writing the data itself. A reader thread sees the valid pointer, accessed the memory location, but found incomplete or "stale" data inside. This inconsistency caused the Go runtime to panic with `fatal error: concurrent map read and map write`

### Anything else we need to know?

Migrating the `ExpiringCache` test logic to use `sync.Map` resolves the high-concurrency flakes observed on `ppc64le`. This will ensure the test runs reliably across all architectures by using `sync.Map`'s native safety against weak memory model race conditions.

title: wrong container_memory_working_set_bytes for DinD container on cgroupv2 only nodes
body:
### What happened?

Let's assume you have: 
- cgroupv2 only OS (e.g. Ubuntu 22.04 (Azure AKS) or [gardenlinux 934.7](https://github.com/gardenlinux/gardenlinux/releases/tag/934.7), see below)
- A running Kubernetes cluster on that OS (e.g. K8s  v1.26.5 or 1.27.3)
- Create a DinD pod with memory limits (e.g. [docker:24.0.5-dind-alpine3.18](https://hub.docker.com/layers/library/docker/24.0.5-dind-alpine3.18/images/sha256-fe74d395f3a15eb2233848d2ac47fd076aa6fe7c17dd9b4ca13145116893f2f5?context=explore))

Then start some container inside the dind pod and consume e.g. 400 MB memory:
```
kubectl exec -it dind -- sh
docker run -it ubuntu bash
cat /dev/zero | head -c 400000000 | tail
```

Wait 5 minutes and then check k9s. Then the 400 MB memory consumption is not visible. 
Same is true for `kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/NODE_NAME/proxy/metrics/resource"`

### What did you expect to happen?

container_memory_working_set_bytes{container="dind",namespace="default",pod="dind"} should show the 400 MB
Metrics server gets the right values, which is shown in `top` or in `docker stats`:
![image](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/metrics-server/assets/70013998/aa6a7a07-5986-4f69-8fc2-8cde4abcd9d0)

on cgroupv1 enabled OS the CPU/memory are shown correctly (e.g. Ubuntu 20.xx or gardenlinux 5xx.yy)

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

cgroupv2 only node OS, can be checked via 
``` 
mount | grep cgroup2
```
should return on the node: `cgroup2 on /sys/fs/cgroup type cgroup2 (rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime)`


example  DinD-pod.yaml:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
    name: dind
spec:
    containers:
      - name: dind
        image: docker:dind
        resources:
            requests:
                cpu: 10m
                memory: 700Mi
            limits:
                cpu: 2
                memory: 700Mi
        securityContext:
            privileged: true
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: true
        volumeMounts:
          - name: docker-graph-storage
            mountPath: /var/lib/docker
    volumes:
      - name: docker-graph-storage
        emptyDir: {}     
```

### Anything else we need to know?

https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/metrics-server/issues/1301 brings me here.

This DinD setup is used in Github Runners: https://github.com/actions/actions-runner-controller/issues/2284

See also https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/45378
