title: Migrate Kubelet codebase to contextual logging
body:
### **What would you like to to?**

Support contextual logging in Kubelet.

### **Why is this needed?**

To implement https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-instrumentation/3077-contextual-logging

### **How to do it?**

General instructions can be found here: https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-instrumentation/migration-to-structured-logging.md

The approach I'd like to propose for `Kubelet` is to do it directory by directory, making as little changes as possible to other components.  If the first level directory requires a lot of changes, consider migrating its subdirectories in a separate PRs, e.g. instead of migrating `pkg/kubelet/cm` at once, consider migrating `pkg/kubelet/cm/cpumanager`, `pkg/kubelet/cm/containermap`, etc.

Use `context.TODO()` to create context that should be passed as an argument in future to avoid massive changes in other components. Add a comment explaining that this is a temporary solution and when it needs to be replaced by the direct context usage.

Look at the existing `context.TODO()` and `context.Background()` calls in the directory. Replace them by the ctx usage if possible. Replace `context.Background()` with `context.TODO()` if ctx is not yet accessible there.

After all source files in the directory are migrated, add the directory path to the `./hack/logcheck.conf` and run `hack/update-golangci-lint-config.sh` to generate `hack/golangci*.yaml` configs. This will prevent usage of non-contextual logging for the directory.

Last step of this migration is to migrate `pkg/kubelet/*.go`, add `pkg/kubelet` to the `./hack/logcheck.conf`, remove all its subdirectories from there and regenerate `golangci` configs.

title: Reject requests with unsupported options
body:
Today, the apiserver accepts requests with options that are unknown to the server, we just throw those options away and continue with the request as if they hadn't been specified.

I think this decision made some sense, as we don't necessarily want to reject a request asking for pagination made to an old server that doesn't support pagination, but it has also caused issues for us when we wanted to add features like server-side dry-run, and when discussing the possibility of adding a precondition to delete options.

The way we dealt with this for dry-run was to make the api-server reject requests with that field for a few versions, which was safe, but also unnecessarily delayed the feature's release.

**What would you like to be added**:
I think the server should ideally reject all requests with options they don't understand and return some kind of structured/machine-readable error which explains which options are causing the failure. Then clients could use this list to determine whether or not any of these options are critical to the request (like dry-run or a precondition). If any of the unsupported are critical, the client should not retry, and just return the error. If none of the unsupported options are critical, the client should retry the request automatically without those options specified. The client is the only one guaranteed to have the knowledge of whether or not an option is critical, since the apiserver could be from an older version.

This change would be backward compatible as long as no one relies on sending the server options that aren't in any version of k8s (which might not be completely true), and would allow us to safely add both critical and uncritical options in the future without having to worry about the same version skew issue we keep running into.

/kind design
/area apiserver
/sig api-machinery
/priority important-longterm
cc @lavalamp

title: [KEP-2400] [Swap]: Verify memory pressure behavior with swap enabled
body:
### What would you like to be added?

A replacement for https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/105023

The issue is for addressing problems related to node pressures and swap.

In short, the problem is that the kernel would try to avoid/defer swapping as much as possible. Therefore, swap generally kicks in when the node is already pressured. On the other hand, kubelet configures node-eviction thresholds so it would be able to reclaim memory before the kernel starts doing so (e.g. with OOM kills).

So, now the flow is as follows:
* Kubelet threshold is exceeded => kubelet reclaims memory by killing pods.
* Swap kicks in.
* Kernel starts reclaiming space (e.g. by OOMing processes).

With this flow, swap does not have the opportunity to free memory space because kubelet starts evicting before it kicks in.

The desired flow is (same as above with different order):
* Swap kicks in.
* Kubelet threshold is exceeded => kubelet reclaims memory by killing pods.
* Kernel starts reclaiming space (e.g. by OOMing processes).

Important pointers:
- See [this comment](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/2400#issuecomment-1693451128).
- Current [discussion in Slack](https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C02UCH9N02J/p1695207853069709).

### Why is this needed?

KEP https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/2400-node-swap

title: DRA: integration-test: cannot set PreAlpha feature gate at emulated version 1.33 but no allocator available for feature set (stable allocator)
body:
### What happened?

In `scheduler_perf/dra` of integration-test,
we enable each allocator for testing and now override the beta feature = false when allocator is stable and in the test, there is a case that version 1.33 needs to be emulated.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ec2c7739bc3ccc602f7af67b096d44a9f446122a/test/integration/scheduler_perf/dra/dra_test.go#L60-L65

However, for some beta features including DRAConsumableCapacity, it is PreAlpha in 1.33. Adding the override there cause the following error.

> scheduler_perf.go:1160: failed to set versions (emu=1.33, min=1.32) during test: cannot set feature gate DRAConsumableCapacity to false, feature is PreAlpha at emulated version 1.33, min compatibility version 1.32

from

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ec2c7739bc3ccc602f7af67b096d44a9f446122a/test/integration/scheduler_perf/scheduler_perf.go#L1156

Meanwhile, not adding that also cause the following error.

> 2026-02-13T00:51:17.1666700Z E0213 00:41:32.160846   27097 schedule_one.go:163] "Error selecting node for pod" err="running PreFilter plugin \"DynamicResources\": internal error: no allocator available for feature set {AdminAccess:false ConsumableCapacity:true DeviceBindingAndStatus:false DeviceTaints:false PartitionableDevices:false PrioritizedList:false}, enabled allocators: stable" pod="test/test-drarhn2d"

from

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ec2c7739bc3ccc602f7af67b096d44a9f446122a/staging/src/k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/structured/allocator.go#L171

The workaround that I did in my PR to have the test pass is to export allocatorEnabled function and add a similar logic to disable beta feature when allocator is`stable` and version >= 1.34 after emulation set.

```diff
@@ -1160,6 +1161,15 @@ func setupTestCase(t testing.TB, tc *testCase, featureGates map[featuregate.Feat
                }
                featureGates[features.OpportunisticBatching] = false
        }
+
+       // Disable DRAConsumableCapacity for the stable allocator when emulating v1.34+.
+       // At v1.33, the feature doesn't exist (PreAlpha) so we can't set it, but it's
+       // effectively disabled, which is what the stable allocator expects.
+       if structured.AllocatorEnabled("stable") &&
+               utilfeature.DefaultFeatureGate.(featuregate.MutableVersionedFeatureGate).EmulationVersion().AtLeast(version.MustParse("1.34")) {
+               featuregatetesting.SetFeatureGateDuringTest(t, utilfeature.DefaultFeatureGate, features.DRAConsumableCapacity, false)
+       }
+
        featuregatetesting.SetFeatureGatesDuringTest(t, utilfeature.DefaultFeatureGate, featureGates)
```
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136611/changes#diff-a09bf733e7a7273560beb3d657d078a3bec7ba83baa4c5b89cbc6990976aad30

Test passes.

title: Consider CSIStorageCapacity when scheduling pods with already-bound PVCs
body:
Is it possible to extend `CSIStorageCapacity` tracking so that the scheduler also considers it when scheduling pods whose PVCs are already bound?

When a node hosting a pod is drained (for example, during maintenance or upgrades), the pod needs to be rescheduled. Currently, the scheduler does not use `CSIStorageCapacity` information for pods with bound PVCs. For storage backends that support volume rebuild or migration, it would be useful if the scheduler could prefer nodes with sufficient available storage capacity, so that the new node can accommodate the original volume and keep the pod and volume co-located for better I/O performance. At the moment, this is not supported, and pods can occasionally be scheduled onto nodes where volumes cannot be rebuilt.

Do you think this should be addressed on the Kubernetes side, or does it need to be handled by the storage backend? If on the Kubernetes side, this could potentially be implemented by adding a new field to StorageClass.

/sig storage
/sig scheduling

title: client-go: Replace deprecated BackoffManager with DelayFunc in Reflector
body:
## Why is this needed?

The `Reflector` in `client-go/tools/cache` uses `wait.NewExponentialBackoffManager()` which is deprecated. The deprecation notice recommends using `wait.Backoff{}.DelayWithReset()` instead.

Related issues #117829 and #118638 noted that the deprecation documentation is incomplete - it suggests using `delayFn.Timer()` with `BackoffUntil`, but this doesn't compile because `Timer` doesn't implement `BackoffManager`. 

This issue proposes:
1. Replace `NewExponentialBackoffManager` with `Backoff{}.DelayWithReset()` in the Reflector
2. Use `DelayFunc.Until()` as the loop mechanism (which does work, unlike the documented suggestion)
3. Optionally expose `Backoff` configuration in `ReflectorOptions` for customization

## Benefits
- Removes usage of deprecated API
- Enables context-aware cancellation (BackoffManager doesn't respect context)
- Allows optional customization of backoff strategy when constructing Reflectors

/sig api-machinery
/kind cleanup
/priority backlog

title: Kubectl Namespace defaulting logic is inconsistent
body:
This is effectively a re-open of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/99884, but I think its slightly different. Basically my concern is the mixing of disparate kinds of clusters.  If you don't agree feel free to close - we have worked around it so this is more to avoid future users issues; it took us _3 years_ to figure it out (obviously not fully time :slightly_smiling_face: )

Kubectl has some namespace defaulting logic:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/cea1d4e20b4a7886d8ff65f34c6d4f95efcb4742/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/clientcmd/client_config.go#L593-L599 and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8bf42039e62d001f5d0331753bd99790b70d51eb/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/clientcmd/merged_client_builder.go#L120

This generally works fine. 

I get if we are "in cluster" we use in cluster config, and if KUBECONFIG is specified we use that. But we are currently mixing the two, which IMO is wrong.

For example, run a pod in namespace "A", then in the pod
```
$ gcloud cluster get-credentials ...
$ kubectl get pods
// Will use namespace "A" instead of default
```

My concern here is that we are mixing two disparate cluster configurations. The configuration for "in cluster" and for "external cluster" should not be mixed, they are configured two completely different things. To me, this is not so different from having a KUBECONFIG with 2 clusters and merging bits of the two together -- they should remain separate.

---

note for folks seeing this issue, the fix is to either set the namespace explicitly or `automountServiceAccountToken: false`

/sig cli

title: kubelet does not restart static pods when apiserver is down
body:
HandlePodCleanups is responsible for restarting static pods, but handle pod cleanups will not run until the apiserver reports in.  If the apiserver or any components it depends on is running as a static pod, it is possible for the static pod to never restart.

Reproduce:

1. Start a cluster
2. Run a static pod with a static UID on a node
3. Terminate the apiservers
4. Restart the kubelet of the node with the static pod
5. Change the configuration of the static pod on disk

Expect: static pod with static uid should restart

HandlePodCleanups should be able to SyncKnownPods to pod worker and restart static pods independent of whether the apiserver is running.

We are missing e2e tests that simulate down apiserver and stress static pods, which could have caught this.

title: MutatingAdmissonPolicy: Validation fails at first attempt when a policy with a matchCondition and a mutation with variables
body:
### What happened?

Validation error occurs when a following policy applied at first, but next try does not cause validation error.

```
$ cat map.yaml
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: MutatingAdmissionPolicy
metadata:
  name: policy
spec:
  matchConstraints:
    matchPolicy: "Equivalent"
    namespaceSelector: {}
    objectSelector: {}
    resourceRules:
    - apiGroups: ["*"]
      apiVersions: ["v1"]
      operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
      resources: ["deployments"]
  failurePolicy: Fail
  reinvocationPolicy: IfNeeded
  variables:
  - name: maxReplicas
    expression: "int(5)"
  matchConditions:
  - name: always-matched
    expression: "true" 
  mutations:
  - patchType: ApplyConfiguration
    applyConfiguration:
      expression: >-
        Object{
          spec: Object.spec {
            replicas: variables.maxReplicas
          }
        }

$ kubectl apply -f map.yaml 
The MutatingAdmissionPolicy "policy" is invalid: spec.mutations[0].applyConfiguration.expression: Invalid value: "Object{\n  spec: Object.spec {\n    replicas: variables.maxReplicas\n  }\n}": compilation failed: ERROR: <input>:3:24: unexpected failed resolution of 'kubernetes.variables'
 |     replicas: variables.maxReplicas
 | .......................^

$ kubectl apply -f map.yaml 
mutatingadmissionpolicy.admissionregistration.k8s.io/policy created
```

### What did you expect to happen?

Validation error does not occur.

title: Clarify ContainerStatus.Started null value and initialize the value for Init containers
body:
This issue is to discuss whether we can change the `Started` field of `ContainerStatus` from pointer to non-pointer bool value. The pointer type is inconsistent with other field `Ready`. The semantic of `Started` being `null` is undefined and it is not ideal if users will use `Started` field `null` value as indication of a spacial condition beyond what `false` indicates. So if there is a process of making field non-pointer after skew period has passed, it would be great to follow it.

The field was introduced as a pointer following [this suggestions](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/77807#discussion_r289542539:): 

> If this is optional, it needs to be a pointer. We can't add non-optional fields, ergo this should be a pointer. Otherwise an old client will not set it and it will be false, which is super confusing.

The field long passed it's skew inconsistency period.

The field is set by prober_manager: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0e3818e02760afa8ed0bea74c6973f605ca4683c/pkg/kubelet/prober/prober_manager.go#L270

## Current behavior

The PR: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/115463 improves the documentation for the `Started` field of `ContainerStatus`. We never declared when `null` value means for the `ContainerStatus`.

For regular container:
- Field is `null` before the `prober_manager` starts.
- Field is `false` once `prober_manager` started.
- Field is `true` when no startup probes defined or once startup probe succeeded.

For Init and ephemeral containers:
- Field is always `null` as those do not start the `prober_manager`.

`StartedAt` field of `Status` type is always populated for both - regular and Init containers. It is populated earlier than `Started` will be set by `prober_manager`. So there is period of time when `StartedAt` has a date and `Started` is `null`.

There is also `Ready` field on `ContainerStatus` that is not a pointer. It will be `false` from the Pod creation and will change to `true` while readiness probes succeed.

## Changes for sidecar containers

The question about this field came up because we plan to use it for https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/753. Also resolving this would clarify the field that needs to be added as part of that same KEP.

We need a signal for sidecar containers KEP to indicate that the sidecar container started and other containers initialization can proceed. We believe that relying on `Started` field would be the best option. So we will initialize the `Started` field for sidecar containers and there will be logic relying on it.

## Proposal

- Change `Started` type from `*bool` to `bool`.
- This changes behavior for Init Containers and Pods before they received by the kubelet - value will be `false` instead of `null`
- Clearly document the difference between `ContainerStatus.Started` and `ContainerStatus.State.StartedAt` fields.
- For sidecar container KEP use the `Started` field as a signal that sidecar container started and ready to proceed with other containers initialization.


/sig architecture
/sig node
/label api-review
//cc @matthyx @dims 

Discussion in Slack: https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/CJUQN3E4T/p1675467718491919

title: Unblock enablement of the ConcurrentWatchObjectDecode by default (to fix scale issues for CRDs)
body:
### What would you like to be added?

[ConcurrentWatchObjectDecode](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/features/kube_features.go#L1955C18-L1957) is currently Beta, but disabled by default.

**I would like to identify or understand the blockers for graduation (if any) so that this can be moved forward.**

This feature gate looks very promising for handling CRD objects with high cardinality, like Workload objects in [Kueue](https://kueue.sigs.k8s.io/). Without this feature gate migration between versions like `v1beta1` to `v1beta2` is risky at scale.

We would love to have this improved before migrating Kueue v1beta2 -> v1.

### Why is this needed?

In Kueue 0.15 we introduced v1beta2 for serving, while keeping v1beta1 for storage. Which was dictated by the needs of downgrading to 0.14 in case something "goes wrong".

However, this caused issues on high scale clusters (small clusters <10k work fine).

My understanding of the problem:
1. when Kueue is starting up then controller-runtime tries to establish the WATCH on the Workload object in v1beta2
2. If the API server does not have a "warm" cache for the Workloads, then it requests ETCD for the list of Workloads in v1beta1
3. API server receives the workloads list, but before returning to Kueue it tries to convert them sequentially to v1beta2. 

**Issue**: for some larger clusters it was estimated to take around 8min, but this exceeds some timeouts in ETCD to serve the request, and the API server fails with 500 in the meanwhile.

There is a good chance that enabling parallel requests would save the request.

**Mitigation**: we recommend users to move from Kueue 0.15 to 0.16 (which is using v1beta2 for storage and serving) which mitigates the problem, but the situation is not ideal, because 0.15 remains affected.

Related issues in Kueue:

title: improved preemption logic for the kubernetes scheduler
body:
### What would you like to be added?

I'd like to expand the kubernetes scheduler so that multiple pods together can share the resources of a preempted pod

### Why is this needed?

According to my understanding, when a pod is preempted there can only be one pod that replaces this pod immediately (a.k.a one pod that'll get a `nominatedNode`), this can delay scheduling of other pods if a relatively big pod is preempted by a relatively small pod.

usually this wouldn't be much of a problem since other small pods will just take a bit longer to schedule, but this has risen from an [issue](https://github.com/kubernetes/autoscaler/issues/7683) in kubernetes/autoscaler, where this might cause unnecessary scale ups in cluster autoscaler.

title: Deduplicate Sync type delta in DeltaFIFO
body:
### What would you like to be added?

# purpose
Currently, there is only deletions will be deduplicated in DeltaFIFO.

Here, we propose that `sync deltas` should also be deduplicated in DeltaFIFO. 

Following is the example of current & desired impl:

# current impl
In DeltaFIFO Items, for ObjA, there are two scenarios (suppose that there is no Delata with ObjA in Items before)：
1. if `Update delta` arrived after resync process finished, then:
```
Items
key: objA-key | Deltas: <Sync, objA1>,<Updated,objA2>
```
2. but if `Update delta` arrived just before resync process, then there is:
```
Items
key: objA-key | Deltas: <Updated,objA2>
```
Since, if there is already corresponding Obj in DeltaFIFO(Items), then during this resync process, the <Sync,Obj> Delta will not be put into Deltas.

# Desired impl
For above two scenarios, no matter that `Updated Delta` is arrived before or after `Sync Delta`, as long as the two deltas are adjacent, the final processing result should be:
 ```
Items
key: objA-key | Deltas: <Updated,objA2>
```

# All the case
For following cases, the sync delta will be deduplicated.
```
Items
1. key: objA-key | Deltas: <Sync, objA1>,<Updated,objA2>
2. key: objA-key | Deltas: <Sync, objA1>,<Deleted,objA2>
3. key: objA-key | Deltas: <Sync, objA1>,<Replaced,objA2>
4. key: objA-key | Deltas: <Sync, objA1>,<Sync,objA2>
```
above cases will be deduplicated like:
 ```
Items
key: objA-key | Deltas: <Updated,objA2>
key: objA-key | Deltas: <Deleted,objA2>
key: objA-key | Deltas: <Replaced,objA2>
key: objA-key | Deltas: <Sync,objA2>
```

Note: 
1. there is no chance that `Added Delta` shows just after `Sync Delta`, if it is, then there must be a `Deleted Delta` between them 
2. There are two `Sync Delta` adjacent, since maybe the process of relist happened right after resync process.  

### Why is this needed?

The goal why we propose this idea is reducing the meaningless delta in DeltaFIFO, which could reduce the times that `HandleDeltas` propagates the delta to all the listeners.

title: PV Controller Serial Processing Bottleneck Causes Massive Pod Scheduling Delays in Large-Scale StatefulSet Scenarios
body:
### What happened?

In large-scale StatefulSet scenarios where each pod is bound to a PVC using volumeTemplate, we observe that a large number of pods remain in the Pending state. The root cause is that the PVCs of these pods are not bound to PVs. The fundamental issue is that the PV controller processes PVCs serially. Each PVC requires at least two rounds of processing by the PV controller to reach the Bound state: the first round triggers PV creation, and the second round triggers the binding of the PV to the PVC. Moreover, after a PV is created, it is stored in the PV controller's cache (persistentVolumeOrderedIndex) only after the PV controller processes the PV. Then, during the second round of processing the PVC, the PV controller can find the PV from the cache (via findBestMatchForClaim) and bind them. This multiple-step processing can take a significant amount of time. In our tests with 50,000 PVCs, it took up to 20 minutes for a pod to be scheduled (the scheduler waits for the PVC to be bound).


### What did you expect to happen?

We expect that pods are scheduled quickly, and PVCs are bound to PVs without significant delays, even in large-scale scenarios.

In dynamic provisioning scenarios with WaitForFirstConsumer binding mode, the relationship between PVC and PV is deterministic. Therefore, we propose making the volumeWorker and claimWorker in the PV controller concurrent. This would significantly improve processing efficiency without causing data consistency issues.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a StatefulSet with a large number of replicas (e.g., 50,000)
2. Use volumeTemplate to create a PVC for each pod
3. Use dynamic provisioning with the binding mode set to WaitForFirstConsumer
4. Observe the pod scheduling status and the time taken for PVCs to bind

### Anything else we need to know?

In dynamic provisioning scenarios with WaitForFirstConsumer binding mode, the relationship between PVC and PV is deterministic. Therefore, we propose making the volumeWorker and claimWorker in the PV controller concurrent. This would significantly improve processing efficiency without causing data consistency issues.

title: Add Verbose Logging to net/http for Egress Auditing and Rename probe/http/http.go
body:
### What would you like to be added?

This proposal includes two related changes to improve egress traffic visibility from core Kubernetes components and to refine logging controls:

Add Verbose Logging to staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/net/http.go: Introduce new klog V-level logs to provide visibility into outbound HTTP requests and how they are handled by proxy settings.

A V(5) log will be added to record requests that are proxied (i.e., not matching the NO_PROXY environment variable). This helps identify traffic that would be blocked in a restricted environment.

A V(6) log will be added to record requests that are not proxied (i.e., explicitly allowed via NO_PROXY). This helps verify that allowlist rules are functioning as expected.

Rename pkg/probe/http/http.go to pkg/probe/http/http_prober.go: Rename this file to prevent a logging conflict with the file mentioned above, which is the actual target for our enhanced logging.

### Why is this needed?

Downstream distributions of Kubernetes, such as GKE, are implementing security features to strictly control and block all egress traffic originating from the kube-apiserver. A core part of this mechanism involves using HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY environment variables to route traffic through a controlled gateway or a "blackhole" proxy, while using a NO_PROXY variable to allowlist essential cluster endpoints.

To safely roll out such a feature, it is critical to have a data-driven way to discover and audit all outbound requests made by the kube-apiserver and other components. This allows operators to build a comprehensive NO_PROXY allowlist and ensure no critical functions are broken. The proposed verbose logging in net/http.go provides this essential visibility.

The second change—renaming pkg/probe/http/http.go—is necessary to avoid unintended log spam. The klog output strips the full file path, so both staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/net/http.go (our target) and pkg/probe/http/http.go (an unrelated file) show up in logs simply as http.go.

As a result, setting --vmodule=http*=5 to enable our new logs also enables verbose logging in the probe helpers, flooding the logs with messages from liveness and readiness probes. This makes it extremely difficult to isolate the critical egress traffic data needed for validation. Renaming the probe helper file to http_prober.go cleanly resolves this name collision and allows for precise, targeted logging for this important security use case.

title: DRA: Add support for aggregate/sum-based resource requests (e.g., total GPU memory) in ResourceClaim
body:
### What happened?

The current ResourceClaim/ResourceClass model is designed for requesting discrete, fixed-size units of a resource, or filtering based on properties. It does not support requesting an aggregate total quantity across multiple devices.

Goal: I want to request a total of 128 Gi of GPU memory for a workload.

Context: Our cluster contains heterogeneous GPU devices with varying memory capacities (e.g., some have 16 Gi, others have 32 Gi).

Limitation: A ResourceClaim must specify how many devices (or what properties the individual device must have), not the sum of a device property (like memory) across the final set of allocated devices. This forces me to over-specify the claim (e.g., "I need 8 devices, all with at least 16 Gi memory"), which doesn't allow the scheduler to optimally select 4×32 Gi devices if they are available and sufficient.

### What did you expect to happen?

The scheduler and resource driver should be able to satisfy the 128 Gi request by allocating:

8×16 Gi devices, OR 4×32 Gi devices

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

 devices:
  - requests:
    - name: required-total-vram
      exactly:
        aggregate:
        - cel:
            expression: 'sum(devices.capacity.memory.value) >= resource.quantity("128Gi")'

### Anything else we need to know?

title: Graceful Node Shutdown does not update endpoints for terminating pods
body:
### What happened?

When graceful node shutdown is enabled, I expect that services are drained appropriately during pod shutdown (i.e. the same way that `kubectl delete pod` would work). However this doesn't seem to be the case - the pod never enters the `Terminating` state according to `kubectl` and doesn't get removed from the service endpoints until it enters the `Completed` or `Failed` state. This causes connection errors and lost requests in `Cluster`-routed services.

### What did you expect to happen?

After pod termination starts, the EndpointSlice should be updated to have the pod that is terminating removed or marked terminating, even before the pod is fully shut down. This is what happens when a pod gets removed for any other reason (e.g. `kubectl delete pod`).

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

You can see the repro at https://github.com/mikekap/vagrant-kubeadm-kubernetes/tree/graceful-shutdown-repro . The repro sets up a 2 node cluster with graceful shutdown enabled and a simple deployment/service.

<details>
<summary>Here is the deployment/service yaml pasted again</summary>

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: echo-deployment
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: echo
  replicas: 2
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: echo
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: echo
        image: mendhak/http-https-echo
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
        lifecycle:
          preStop:
            exec:
              command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "echo 'Begin shutdown' > /proc/1/fd/1; sleep 20; echo 'End shutdown' > /proc/1/fd/1; exit 0"]
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: my-service
spec:
  selector:
    app: echo
  ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 80
      targetPort: 8080
```
</details>

To reproduce:
 * Run the deployment, preferably one pod on each node.
 * Run `watch -n 1 'kubectl  describe endpointslice my-service-5j2nw'` in a separate terminal (you'll need to figure out the right name unfortunately)
 * Use the virtualbox UI to send an ACPI shutdown to one of the nodes.

Within 20 seconds (the preStop hook duration), the EndpointSlice should be updated to have the pod that is terminating removed. This is what happens when a pod gets removed for any other reason (e.g. `kubectl delete pod`).

To ensure that everything else worked, you can reboot the node and see the journal logs (via something like `journalctl -b -1`) of the shutdown sequence triggering the kubelet graceful shutdown logic.

title: Cronjob controller try to get existed job without namespace
body:
### What happened?

We're seeing when the senario in [cronjob_controllerv2.go#L615-L637](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/65f09e605cb206b2e5fcff4d69a4ae8acf62dbc3/pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controllerv2.go#L615-L637) happened (Cronjob Controller found an existed job), Cronjob controller will try to get the job without specifying `namespace` value and get HTTP 404:


#### kube-controller-manager log:
```
E0210 18:47:10.835604       1 cronjob_controllerv2.go:179] "Unhandled Error" err="error syncing CronJobController default/sleep-300-job, requeuing: the server could not find the requested resource" logger="UnhandledError"
```

#### API Server log:
```
{
    "kind": "Event",
    "apiVersion": "audit.k8s.io/v1",
    "level": "RequestResponse",
    "auditID": "db48fd5c-6a37-4639-a6f0-2fcfeb0b5e8b",

    =====================

            ]

        "192.168.130.2"
    ],

    "objectRef": {
        "resource": "jobs",

    },
    "responseStatus": {
        "metadata": {},
        "status": "Failure",
        "message": "the server could not find the requested resource",
        "reason": "NotFound",
        "details": {},
        "code": 404
    },
    "responseObject": {
        "kind": "Status",
        "apiVersion": "v1",
        "metadata": {},
        "status": "Failure",
        "message": "the server could not find the requested resource",
        "reason": "NotFound",
        "details": {},
        "code": 404
    },
    "requestReceivedTimestamp": "2026-02-10T18:47:10.834353Z",
    "stageTimestamp": "2026-02-10T18:47:10.835086Z",
    "annotations": {
        "authorization.k8s.io/decision": "allow",
        "authorization.k8s.io/reason": "RBAC: allowed by ClusterRoleBinding \"system:controller:cronjob-controller\" of ClusterRole \"system:controller:cronjob-controller\" to ServiceAccount \"cronjob-controller/kube-system\""
    }
}
```

The issue was the "requestURI": `/apis/batch/v1/jobs/sleep-300-job-29512485` is correct, it should contain `namespace` e.g.:
```
❯ kubectl get job sleep-300-job-29512485 -v 9                                      
...
I0210 18:52:07.314585   31290 round_trippers.go:632] "Response" verb="GET" url="https://192.168.130.2:8443/apis/batch/v1/namespaces/default/jobs/sleep-300-job-29512485" status="200 OK" headers=<
```

And the API Server's 404 indicated there's no `/apis/batch/v1/jobs/` API.

### What did you expect to happen?

Cronjob controller should query the job `with namespace`:

Incorrect URI (current):
```
/apis/batch/v1/jobs/<JOB_NAME>
```

Correct URI:
```
/apis/batch/v1/namespaces/<NAMESPACE>/jobs/<JOB_NAME>
```

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a cronjob to create a job every 5 minutes:
```
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: sleep-300-job
spec:
  schedule: "*/5 * * * *"
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
            - name: echo-sleep
              image: ubuntu
              command:
                - /bin/bash
                - -c
                - echo start && sleep 180 && echo end
          restartPolicy: Never
```

Once the first job was created, create another job manually with the next expected job name (id + 5):
```
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: sleep-300-job-29512465
  namespace: default
  ownerReferences:
  - apiVersion: batch/v1
    blockOwnerDeletion: true
    controller: true
    kind: CronJob
    name: sleep-300-job
    uid: d10ff40f-be9d-47d2-aa67-7a376f054ed2
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - command:
        - /bin/bash
        - -c
        - echo start && sleep 180 && echo end
        image: ubuntu
        name: echo-sleep
      restartPolicy: Never
```

Check the kube-controller-manager and API Server audit log for the result.

### Anything else we need to know?

The issue seems to be when Cronjob controller trying to get job, it used the `jobReq` from `getJobFromTemplate2()` function, however, `getJobFromTemplate2()` won't set the job Namespace:
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/65f09e605cb206b2e5fcff4d69a4ae8acf62dbc3/pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controllerv2.go#L621
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/65f09e605cb206b2e5fcff4d69a4ae8acf62dbc3/pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controllerv2.go#L604
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/cronjob/utils.go#L256-L263

Seems we're not relying on the `namespace` from `getJobFromTemplate2()`, it seems the correct way to specify `namespace` should be the same as:
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/65f09e605cb206b2e5fcff4d69a4ae8acf62dbc3/pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controllerv2.go#L609

title: Set memory.min or memory.low, without memory.high
body:
**Problem**

In kubernetes, the container memory requests aren't propagated to the container runtime. This makes sense because they're not *directly* meaningful to any runtime setting (unlike e.g. container memory limits which translate to `memory.max` on cgroupv2).

[KEP-2570: Memory QoS](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/2570-memory-qos) aims to change this by setting `memory.min` on relevant cgroups based on the corresponding k8s memory requests. This KEP has stalled out due to also tweaking `memory.high`, which has undesirable effects. 

**Question**

Can we start passing container memory requests to the container runtime?

I see two potential paths:

* Path 1: Begin setting `memory.min` on relevant cgroups based on memory requests. This is a part of KEP-2570. Critically, we wouldn't set `memory.high` ever. This alone appears to achieves the goals of the KEP. It's unclear to me if or why we must set `memory.high` together with `memory.min`. Must we?
* Path 2: Begin setting `memory.low` on relevant cgroups based on memory requests. Don't set `memory.min` or `memory.high` at all. Less guarantees than with `memory.min`, but also should be less disruptive from today's behavior, and still a behavior improvement. I believe this should be completely backwards compatible to when if/we support `memory.min` in the future. 

Is there any appetite for this? Am I missing some nuance that makes these paths non-starters? KEP-2570 goes far, and it feels like we can get partial benefit more easily by reducing the ambition.

**Why?**

1. Achieve partial or even full benefits that KEP-2570 aims to achieve by de-coupling some parts of the KEP from others, and tweaking others.
2. I have an on-node plugin which tracks CPU and memory requests of containers on the node, which it uses as input to actuate changes elsewhere on-node. This plugin primarily uses a combination of NRI and directly querying CRI to achieve this. However, it needs to know memory requests, which it has to fetch either from kube-api (external to node), or the local authenticated /pods endpoint (unreliable, security implications). Would be great to just get all needed info from NRI/CRI directly.

title: +k8s:zeroValueAllowed  proposal
body:
### **Introduction**
The `+k8s:required` tag in Declarative Validation (DV) enforces both the presence of a field and its content, rejecting zero values like `0` or `""`. For specific fields, Kubernetes requires that a client explicitly provide the key in the request, yet the zero value of the type remains valid. The `+k8s:zeroValueAllowed` tag allows these fields to converge with standard OpenAPI `required` semantics while maintaining strict server-side presence checks.

### **Reasoning and Motivation**
Focusing on `int` and `string` types covers the majority of legacy "required-but-zero-allowed" cases encountered in the Kubernetes core APIs.

1.  **Meaningful Zero Integers**: 
    *   The `exitCode` in `ContainerStateTerminated` is frequently `0` (indicating success) and must be explicitly representable even when the field is marked as required.
2.  **Required but Non-Empty Strings**:
    *   Many `Node` status identifiers (such as `machineID`, `systemUUID`, and `bootID`) are marked as required in OpenAPI to ensure they are always present in the object, but server-side validation does not currently enforce that they be non-empty strings. 
    *   `status.conditions[].type` fields in several workload APIs (`DaemonSet`, `Deployment`) are required, but validation does not always check for emptiness.
3.  **Migration Path**: Supporting these types enables the migration of fields that currently use "required" OpenAPI metadata without introducing new, breaking server-side validation rules.

### **Expected Behavior in `validation-gen`**
For the initial implementation, `validation-gen` will only support `+k8s:zeroValueAllowed` on fields of type `int` (and its variants) or `string`.

| Type | Behavioral Change with `+k8s:required` + `+k8s:zeroValueAllowed` |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Integer** | The field **must** be present in the request. The value `0` is accepted as valid. |
| **String** | The field **must** be present in the request. The empty string `""` is accepted as valid. |

#### **Implementation Details**
*   **Generator Modification**: When generating code for a field marked with both tags, the generator will omit the content-based "is zero" check.

### What happened?

The apiserver removes all managedFields of an object under the following circumstances:
* object has managedField entries of multiple apiVersions
* conversion webhook is (potentially temporarily) not available/reachable
* there's a write on the object (via label, or client-side apply, SSA just returns an appropriate error, more details below)

### What did you expect to happen?

I would expect to get an error back from the apiserver in cases like this.
Removing all managedFields can have a big impact on the results of subsequent writes.

title: K8s breaks CSI idempotency requirement: NodePublishVolume() passes same target_path for all block mode consumers
body:
For filesystem volumes, NodePublishVolume receives, e.g., 
```
GRPC request: {"target_path":"/var/lib/kubelet/pods/eda0c617-a1ca-4260-a6cd-3cc1dca8560a/volumes/kubernetes.io~csi/<PV-NAME>/mount" ...
```
which is different for every pod. However, for block mode volumes, it is like
```
GRPC request: {"target_path":"/var/lib/kubelet/plugins/kubernetes.io/csi/volumeDevices/publish/<PV_NAME>" ...
```
regardless of the pod to which the device is being attached, and the same is true for NodeUnpublishVolume.

It appears that there is no way for a CSI driver to distinguish between a repeated NodePublishVolume() for the same pod (to which the CSI spec requires it to respond positively for idempotency) and a request for a different pod on the same node.

But it needs to know: in the latter case, it needs to track how many pods still have the device attached, so that it knows what to do when it receives a NodeUnpublishVolume(), including whether or not to unmount the bind mount. Put another way: if the path differed for every consumer then it could simply umount and delete.

The context is a CSI driver providing only NodePublishVolume/NodeUnpublishVolume

/sig storage

title: [Bug] kube-apiserver: `--audit-log-maxsize=0` does not disable rotation as documented, but defaults to 100MB via lumberjack**
body:
### What happened?

When configuring `kube-apiserver` with audit logging enabled, setting `--audit-log-maxsize=0` results in audit logs being rotated when they reach **100MB**, instead of growing indefinitely (or not rotating based on size) as implied by the documentation.

Since default values for `--audit-log-maxbackup` and `--audit-log-maxage` are also `0` (meaning "retain all" and "retain forever"), the result is not a single large file, but an accumulation of many 100MB log files until disk exhaustion.

### What did you expect to happen?

According to the `kube-apiserver` help text and documentation:

> `--audit-log-maxsize`: The maximum size in megabytes of the audit log file before it gets rotated. **If this is 0, the log file is not rotated.**

I expected the `audit.log` file to grow indefinitely without rotation when `maxsize` is set to `0`.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Start `kube-apiserver` with the following flags:
```bash
--audit-log-path=/tmp/k8s-audit.log
--audit-log-maxsize=0

```
2. Generate audit events sufficient to exceed 100MB (e.g., using a load testing tool or simply `dd` appending if testing the library directly, or heavy API usage).
3. Observe that the log file is rotated (renamed with a timestamp) once it hits approximately 100MB.

### Anything else we need to know?

The issue lies in the interaction between `k8s.io/apiserver` and the underlying logging library `gopkg.in/natefinch/lumberjack.v2`.

1. **Kubernetes Implementation**:
In `staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/plugin/pkg/audit/log/backend.go`, the backend is initialized with the user-provided `MaxSize`:
```go
func NewBackend(filename string, maxBackup, maxAge, maxSize int) audit.Backend {
    writer := &lumberjack.Logger{
        Filename:   filename,
        MaxSize:    maxSize,    // Passed as 0
        // ...
    }
    return backend.NewBackend(writer)
}

```


2. **Lumberjack Implementation**:
The `lumberjack` library treats `MaxSize: 0` not as "unlimited", but as "use default".
Reference: `lumberjack.go` in `natefinch/lumberjack`:
```go
const defaultMaxSize = 100 // megabytes

func (l *Logger) max() int64 {
    if l.MaxSize == 0 {
        return int64(defaultMaxSize * megabyte)
    }
    return int64(l.MaxSize) * int64(megabyte)
}

```
Consequently, passing `0` effectively sets the rotation threshold to 100MB.

title: Documentation of pod selection for node-pressure eviction is confusing regarding QoS
body:
In [the Node-pressure doc explaining the ranking of pods for eviction](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/node-pressure-eviction/#pod-selection-for-kubelet-eviction), there is a note saying that QoS are not used for this ranking (which appears to be correct, AFAICT from the code).
However, this section still mentions QoS extensively, and it reads a bit ambiguous. In particular, this section:

>As a result, kubelet ranks and evicts pods in the following order:
>
>   1. BestEffort or Burstable pods where the usage exceeds requests. These pods are evicted based on their Priority and then by how much their usage level exceeds the request.
>   2. Guaranteed pods and Burstable pods where the usage is less than requests are evicted last, based on their Priority.
>
> Note:
> The kubelet does not use the pod's [QoS class](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-qos/) to determine the eviction order. You can use the QoS class to estimate the most likely pod eviction order when reclaiming resources like memory. QoS classification does not apply to EphemeralStorage requests, so the above scenario will not apply if the node is, for example, under DiskPressure.

The first half directly mention the QoS in relation to the eviction order, while the note specifically say they are not used. While I suppose the note is intended as disambiguation, it's not explicitly said.

Furthermore, the [documentation on QoS](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-qos/) says that kubelet use the QoS to determine which pods to evict, which seems a contradiction to the above.

/kind documentation
/sig docs

Users often type "kubectl get ...", so it is natural to try "kubectl get logs". Today that fails or behaves differently than "kubectl logs", which is a small UX papercut for both new and experienced users.

Accept "kubectl get logs" and route it to "kubectl logs", matching flags, behavior, and output.

This only adds a new accepted invocation and does not change existing command behavior.

- Would you prefer a simple alias, a "get" subcommand hook, or command routing in kubectl?

title: [sig-cloud-provider] Hybrid cloud native support.
body:
### What would you like to be added?

CLI global flag `--hybrid-cloud=true`

### Why is this needed?

It's possible to run multiple CCMs in one cluster, but it requires a deep understanding of how the cloud provider works. In some cases, we need to add a few checks or extra logic on the CCM side.

The `node-controller` functions properly; only one CCM can find and initialize the node, while others skip it with an error or log message.

With the node-lifecycle-controller, we need to incorporate more checks into each CCM because we cannot determine if an instance exists or not. For instance, Azure-CCM always responds that the instance exists and is not switched off if the ProviderID is not Azure. The CCM responsible for this cloud can make the correct decision. I believe these checks are better made on the cloud provider side.


When a CCM starts, it registers the name of the cloud using 'cloudprovider.RegisterCloudProvider'. This name usually exists in the ProviderID `cloud-provider-name://`. For example, we can add the CLI global flag `--hybrid-cloud=true`, which will use this name from `RegisterCloudProvider` to check the prefix in the ProviderID. If it does not match, the functions `InstanceExists` and `InstanceShutdown` will not be called.

/sig cloud-provider

title: Controller backoff grows superexponentially due to spurious triggers
body:
### What happened?

Consider an admission webhook that handles all pod deletion events with `failurePolicy: Fail`. It should allow all pod deletion events under normal circumstances. Due to a network issue, this admission webhook is unreachable to kube-apiserver for one minute, thus all ReplicaSet reconciles attempting to scale down (delete pods) during this one-minute window fail.

During this one-minute window, the ReplicaSet attempts to delete the excess pods, but fails at `t0`, triggering an exponential backoff at `t0 + 5ms * Pow(2.0, n)` intervals where [`n` is the number of failured reconciliations](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/6c24674413b0d16f5c5a9628d9f1b75fd5a44f1e/util/workqueue/default_rate_limiters.go#L121). However, the other pods of this ReplicaSet simultaneously transition between `Ready`/`Unready` state. These pod events spuriously triggers ReplicaSet controller to *prematurely reconcile* before `5ms * Pow(2, n)` has elapsed. Since we are still in the time window of the failing window, all these reconciliations fail, **contributing to the failure counter in the rate limiter without actually waiting for the backoff**, quickly escalating to the maximum backoff period ([1000 seconds](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/6c24674413b0d16f5c5a9628d9f1b75fd5a44f1e/util/workqueue/default_rate_limiters.go#L113)) quickly.

Externally, the following pattern was observed:

<details>
<summary>Failed pod deletion event timestamps from audit log</summary>

In anti-chronological order. The webhook is unavailable during the period from 15:12:25 to 15:13:49.

This only includes pod deletion events on a single pod. There might be other pod deletion events on the same replicaset between 15:12:25 and 15:13:48, which I have not carefully classified whether they were independent reconciles (since pods are deleted concurrently), but there are **no other pod deletion events between 15:13:48.466 and 15:38:28.552** related to this ReplicaSet.

```
15:30:28.552
15:13:48.466
15:13:42.757
15:13:42.681
15:13:37.327
15:13:29.396
15:13:07.224
15:12:46.656
15:12:36.335
15:12:31.115
15:12:28.455
15:12:27.039
15:12:26.158
15:12:25.975
15:12:25.865
15:12:25.675
```
</details>


<details>
<summary>Interval in seconds between successive pod deletion events</summary>

In anti-chronological order
```
1000.0859999999999
5.70900000000006     <-- spurious trigger
0.07599999999990814  <-- spurious trigger
5.354000000000042    <-- spurious trigger
7.93100000000004     <-- spurious trigger
22.171999999999912   <-- spurious trigger
20.568000000000097   <--{
10.320999999999913
5.220000000000027
2.659999999999968
1.4160000000000537
0.8809999999999718   <--} these intervals approximately exhibit exponential pattern
0.18299999999999272  <-- exponential pattern not obvious, possibly network latency jitter
0.11000000000001364
0.19000000000005457
```
</details>

The time from the 1st event to the 15th event was only about 83 seconds, but the time from the 15th event to the 16th event is 1000 seconds (maximum backoff). In other words, the apparent behavior is an exponential backoff with a factor much higher than 2.

### What did you expect to happen?

Exponential backoff should be based on the actual elapsed time, not merely by counting the number of failures, in order to tolerate spurious triggers. It is recommended to change the backoff formula from

```
baseDelay * pow(2, numFailures)
```

to

```go
// considering that AddRateLimited is called immediately after a failure that occurred negligibly long ago
target := time.Since(r.lastFailure) * 2
result := min(max(r.longestReturnedBackoff, 2 * min(target, longestReturnedBackoff)), maxBackoff)
r.lastFailure, r.longestReturnedBackoff = time.Now(), result
return result
```


### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a ReplicaSet with 20 pods
2. Scale down the ReplicaSet to 5
3. Immediately after step 2, add an admission webhook that always fails
4. Immediately after step 3, scale down the ReplicaSet to 0.
5. Observe audit logs. Pod deletion attempts grows at an uneven pattern that reaches the maximum ([1000 seconds](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/6c24674413b0d16f5c5a9628d9f1b75fd5a44f1e/util/workqueue/default_rate_limiters.go#L113)) quickly.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

<details>

The kube-controller-manager version is 1.18.10. I have not tested the behavior on newer versions, but I expect the issue to persist considering that the `NewTypedItemExponentialFailureRateLimiter` implementation logic has not been changed.
</details>

title: WaitForCacheSync without polling
body:
### What would you like to be added?

- Add an alternative to `HasSynced` which returns a channel to check, potentially in combination with a name.
- Add an alternative to `WaitForCacheSync` which uses that.


### Why is this needed?

1. A process waiting will react more quickly, with less wasted CPU cycles.
2. The name makes it possible to fail with a more informative message in case of a timeout.
3. In a `synctest`, time currently moves forward randomly when using polling. Channels establish a clear causal relationship between goroutines. The expectation is that the alternative `WaitForCacheSync` will not move time forward. It might even be possible to use `synctest.Wait` instead in the test itself.

The last point is the main motivation for this issue. This was encountered while using `synctest` in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/devicetainteviction/device_taint_eviction_test.go and currently [prevents simplifying some time-based assertions](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8d450ef773127374148abad4daaf28dac6cb2625/pkg/controller/devicetainteviction/device_taint_eviction_test.go#L2110).

title: Migrate 'Good First Migration' Immutable Fields to Declarative Validation
body:
### What would you like to be added?

This issue tracks a number of identified "good first migration" cases from handwritten Go code to Declarative Validation tags (`+k8s:immutable` or `+k8s:update=NoModify`) as part of KEP-5073. This issue aims to be a more narrowed down list with specific fields and validation tags than the general tracking issues. The goal is to have users more easily able to aid in the migration by first having a set of "Good First Migration" cases with minimal migration friction and build from there.

For more information on the tasks here, the Declarative Validation work group (guiding this and similar issues) has open discussion in kubernetes Slack channel: `#sig-api-machinery-dev-tools`

We are targeting fields that meet the "Good First Migration" criteria:
1.  **Validation Logic:** Simple immutability checks (typically using `apivalidation.ValidateImmutableField` or direct equality checks between `new` and `old` objects).
2.  **Versioning:** The field exists at the same path across all API versions.
3.  **Status:** The field has not yet been migrated (does not currently have a `+k8s:immutable` or `+k8s:update` tag).

### IMPORTANT! - PR Structure
The ideal PR structure for a PR contributing a DV tag migration is:

*   **Commit # 1:** IF NOT ALREADY WIRED UP FOR DV - Wire up the apigroup, add empty test and empty generated file.
*   **Commit # 2:** Use a single DV tag on a single field. E.g. Add `+k8s:immutable` to an immutable field. Includes generated code and robust test cases. Emphasis on test-cases -- we want enough to prove that a field is correct, but we don't want to duplicate all the per-tag tests.
*   **Commits # 3...N:** Use DV tags on the same field, one per commit; repeat until that field is done or all that is left is not handled by DV yet.
*   **Commits N+1...M:** Repeat the above for more fields.

The emphasis is on lots of small commits. Maintaining commit discipline is hard but worthwhile.

### Resources

*   **KEP:** [KEP-5073: Declarative Validation](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-api-machinery/5073-declarative-validation)
*   **Migration Guide:** [Review the "Migrating Handwritten Validation" section in the README](https://github.com/jpbetz/validation-gen/blob/main/staging/src/k8s.io/code-generator/cmd/validation-gen/README.md#2-migrating-handwritten-validation-to-declarative-validation)

### Understanding `+k8s:update` Options

When migrating immutable fields, you will primarily use `+k8s:immutable` or `+k8s:update=NoModify`. Here is when to use which:

*   **`+k8s:immutable`**: Use this for fields that, once set (during creation or update), can never be changed. It is the most common tag for "immutable" fields. It is equivalent to `+k8s:update=NoModify` but conveys the intent of "immutability" more clearly for the entire lifecycle.
*   **`+k8s:update=NoModify`**: Use this if you specifically want to enforce that the value cannot change during updates.
*   **`+k8s:update=NoSet`**: Use this if a field cannot be set (transition from nil to non-nil) during an update if it was previously unset.
*   **`+k8s:update=NoUnset`**: Use this if a field cannot be unset (transition from non-nil to nil) during an update if it was previously set.

For the purpose of this "Good First Migration" issue, most fields listed are strictly immutable, so `+k8s:immutable` is the preferred choice unless the existing validation logic explicitly allows transitions (e.g., allow setting once but not modifying afterwards).

### How to Migrate a Field

1.  **Locate the Versioned Type:** Find the `types.go` file for the versioned API.
2.  **Add the Tag:** Add `// +k8s:immutable` (or `// +k8s:update=NoModify`) above the field definition.
3.  **Generate:** Run `hack/update-codegen.sh validation`.
4.  **Update Strategy:** In the resource's `strategy.go` (usually in `pkg/registry/<group>/<resource>/`), update the `ValidateUpdate` function to use `rest.ValidateUpdateDeclarativelyWithMigrationChecks` (if available/applicable for update validation).
5.  **Verify:**
    *   Ensure unit tests pass.
    *   Run `declarative_validation_test.go` (add one if missing) to prove equivalence.
6.  **Mark Covered:** In the original `validation.go`, find the manual check (typically `apivalidation.ValidateImmutableField`) and append `.MarkCoveredByDeclarative()`.

Example of marking hand-written validation code:
```go
allErrs = append(allErrs, apivalidation.ValidateImmutableField(newObj.Spec.Selector, oldObj.Spec.Selector, fldPath.Child("spec", "selector")).MarkCoveredByDeclarative()...)
```

### Why is this needed?

This helps onboard the community to DV, improves the APIs touched, and helps in the process of getting Declarative Validation to its stated goal of migrating ~50% of existing hand-written code to DV over 5 releases -> improved API readability and more declarative APIs.

title: fake.NewClientset should track status and spec independently
body:
### Description

The generated client-go fake clientset (e.g., k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes/fake) does not correctly model the separation between spec and status when using server-side apply.

When the same manager performs:

1. Apply() to update spec-owned fields
2. ApplyStatus() to update status-owned fields

the second call overwrites fields from the first call. This diverges from real apiserver behavior, where spec and status are separate subresources and are merged independently.

### Reproducer

````go
client := NewClientset()
namespace := "default"

pod, err := client.CoreV1().Pods(namespace).Apply(context.Background(),
	v1ac.Pod("foo", namespace).WithFinalizers("foo-finalizer"),
	meta_v1.ApplyOptions{FieldManager: "test-manager"})
require.NoError(t, err)
require.Equal(t, pod.Finalizers, []string{"foo-finalizer"})

pod, err = client.CoreV1().Pods(namespace).ApplyStatus(context.Background(),
	v1ac.Pod("foo", namespace).WithStatus(v1ac.PodStatus().WithPhase(v1.PodPending)),
	meta_v1.ApplyOptions{FieldManager: "test-manager"})
require.NoError(t, err)
require.Equal(t, pod.Status.Phase, v1.PodPending)
require.Equal(t, pod.Finalizers, []string{"foo-finalizer"})
````

### Actual behavior

The second call (ApplyStatus) overwrites the object stored in the fake tracker, causing fields set via Apply() (e.g. metadata.finalizers) to be lost.

This indicates that:

- Apply() and ApplyStatus() are not tracked independently
- The fake client does not model the /status subresource
- Server-side apply merge semantics are not respected

### Expected behavior

The fake client should behave like a real apiserver:

- Apply() updates spec/metadata fields
- ApplyStatus() updates only the status subresource
- Fields written by Apply() must remain intact after ApplyStatus()

This behavior is correctly observed when running the same code against a real API server (e.g. via envtest or a real cluster).

### Why this matters

- Controllers commonly update spec and status in separate calls
- Unit tests using fake.NewClientset produces false failures
- This encourages incorrect controller patterns (single combined updates) to work around fake behavior
- The divergence is subtle and easy to miss

### Notes

The root cause appears to be that the fake client’s ObjectTracker does not implement subresource semantics for /status, even for built-in types that support it.

Should probably be considered as a feature request, as the general advice is to write envtest when real apiserver behavior is required. At the same time, many developers prefer to use fake clients - even for more than just simple unit tests, mainly because a fake client is faster and easier to use/bootstrap.

Follow-up after https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/125560.

For inspiration, this has been "solved" when using the controller-runtime fake client: https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/controller-runtime/pull/2259.

### What happened?

I am working on an extension apiservers and a library helping to create those, upgrading k8s depdendencies to 0.35.0 breaks code generation.

The `kube::codegen::gen_openapi` command from `kube_codegen.sh` reports several permission denied errors, e.g.:

```
2026/01/17 17:40:09 Model name code generation error: failed executing generator: some targets had errors: errors in target "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/resource": open /home/nik/Development/ace/apiserver-kit/.devenv/state/go/pkg/mod/k8s.io/apimachinery@v0.35.0/pkg/api/resource/zz_generated.model_name.go: permission denied
errors in target "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1": open /home/nik/Development/ace/apiserver-kit/.devenv/state/go/pkg/mod/k8s.io/apimachinery@v0.35.0/pkg/apis/meta/v1/zz_generated.model_name.go: permission denied
errors in target "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/runtime": open /home/nik/Development/ace/apiserver-kit/.devenv/state/go/pkg/mod/k8s.io/apimachinery@v0.35.0/pkg/runtime/zz_generated.model_name.go: permission denied
...
```

It is possible to work around these issues by setting the permissions in go modules to non-readonly:
```
declare -a GOMODS=(
  "k8s.io/apimachinery"
  "k8s.io/api"
)
echo "Setting permissions for files of relevant go modules to 644"
for MOD in "${GOMODS[@]}"; do
  find "$(go list -json -m -u "${MOD}" | jq -r '.Dir')" -type f -exec chmod 644 -- {} +
done
```
However tampering with the go modules will make `go mod verify` fail and changing the permissions back will not solve this as the computed hashes differ, so the relevant modules have to be force deleted afterwards to fix this.

### What did you expect to happen?

No errors were expected to occur.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

An easy way to reproduce this is to:
```
git@github.com:kubernetes/sample-apiserver.git
cd sample-apiserver
vim hack/update-codegen.sh # update L22 to: 'CODEGEN_PKG=$(go list -m -f '{{.Dir}}' k8s.io/code-generator)'
go mod download
./hack/update-codegen.sh
```

### Anything else we need to know?

This worked in prior versions, so I am wondering if the files are not opened as read-only.

title: Support TLS Server Name overrides in EgressSelectorConfiguration
body:
## What would you like to be added?

Add a `tlsServerName` field to the `TLSConfig` structure in `EgressSelectorConfiguration` to allow overriding the hostname used for TLS certificate verification, similar to the existing `tls-server-name` field in kubeconfig (added in[ #88769](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/88769)).

## Precedent

This functionality already exists in:
- **kubeconfig files**: The `tls-server-name` field was added in #88769 for similar use cases
- **kubectl**: The `--tls-server-name` flag provides command-line access
- **Go's `tls.Config`**: The underlying `ServerName` field supports this

The egress selector `TLSConfig` would benefit from the same capability for consistency.

## Why is this needed?

### Use Case

This addresses scenarios where components using EgressSelectorConfiguration connect through Kubernetes Service DNS names (e.g., proxy.svc.cluster.local) but that hostname is not included in the server certificate's Subject Alternative Names (SANs), which define which hostnames a certificate is valid for.

**Example scenario:**
- Egress selector is configured to connect to: `https://konnectivity-service.example.svc.cluster.local:8443`
- The proxy's TLS certificate contains SANs for: `proxy.example.com`
- Connection fails because `konnectivity-service.example.svc.cluster.local` is not in the certificate SANs

### Current Workaround Limitations

The current workaround of updating certificates to include all possible service DNS names has significant drawbacks:
- Requires certificate regeneration and rotation across many clusters
- Service names may vary across environments (dev, staging, prod)
- Certificate management becomes complex in multi-tenant environments
- May require coordination with external PKI infrastructure

### Proposed Solution

Add an optional `tlsServerName` field to override the hostname used for certificate verification:

```yaml
apiVersion: apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: EgressSelectorConfiguration
egressSelections:
- name: cluster
  connection:
    proxyProtocol: HTTPConnect
    transport:
      tcp:
        url: "https://proxy-service.example.svc.cluster.local:8443"
        tlsConfig:
          caBundle: /etc/kubernetes/pki/ca.crt
          clientCert: /etc/kubernetes/pki/client.crt
          clientKey: /etc/kubernetes/pki/client.key
          tlsServerName: "proxy.example.com"  # <-- New field
```
This would allow connecting via the service DNS name while verifying the certificate against the actual hostname in the SANs.

title: Allow APIs and feature gates to depend on each other
body:
Some APIs are tightly paired with a feature gate.  For these cases, having the API enabled and the feature gate disabled (or vis-versa) is not a useful state and allowing this state to exist makes developing and testing such features more complicated without any clear benefit.

Providing a way for API authors to express enforced dependencies between the API and feature gate (and allowing them to be mutually dependent) is one possible way to address, although I am interested in hearing other alternatives.

title: [kube-api-linter] Enable the `maxlength` linter
body:
Spun out from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/134671 for tracking purposes.

The `maxlength` lint check will check strings for MaxLength, arrays for MaxItems, and reports when those are missing.

This linter is not ready to be enabled yet because the existing check does not have any knowledge of the declarative validation markers associated with maximum length constraints.

Depends on https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kube-api-linter/issues/223.

title: return a bookmark event with bookmarkafterresourceversion immediately to reduce WatchList time cost
body:
### What happened?

the resource version of the bookmark event returned by watchlist maybe larger than bookmarkafterresourceversion. which means there need more 1 ~ 1.25s to return even the event with bookmarkresourceversion already received in cacher.

### What did you expect to happen?

return a bookmark event with bookmarkafterresourceversion immediately when to sendWatchCacheEvent in cacheWatcher if the resource version already not elder than bookmarkafterresourceversion.
DON‘T wait another cycle of bookmark timer.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/cacher.go#L899
there is a bookmark timer triggered every 1 ~ 1.25s.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/cache_watcher.go#L527-L529
```golang
if event.ResourceVersion > resourceVersion || (event.Type == watch.Bookmark && event.ResourceVersion == resourceVersion && !c.wasBookmarkAfterRvSent()) {
    c.sendWatchCacheEvent(event)
}
```
the resourceversion passed to process function is just bookmarkafterresourversion.
consider the following scenario

1. bookmark event come at t1 with resourceversion < bookmarkresourceversion, no action
2. normal event come at t2 with resourceversion = bookmarkresourceversion, no action
3. normal event come at t3 with resourceversion > bookmarkresourceversion, then the event will be send to client
4. bookmark event come at t4 with resourceversion > bookmarkresourceversion, then the bookmark will be set with an special annotation and return to client

t4 - t1 = 1s ~ 1.25s

the final bookmark event can be send back to client at t1. this will reduce one bookmark timer cycle for watchlist request in some scenario. In extreme cases, this time factor may lead to a timeout for the watchlist request.

### Anything else we need to know?

title: A potential goroutine leak in staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/watch/mux.go
body:
### What happened?

A goroutine get blocked due to channel receive. Maybe there are no corresponding channel send operations or channel close operation.
Blocking position is below.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5161bf00587eb36cd3ce64635126f47a98068b5c/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/watch/mux.go#L268

### What did you expect to happen?

There are corresponding channel operations avoiding the goroutine get blocked.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

We can reproduce the bug using goleak `defer goleak.VerifyNone(t)` at the beginning of the test.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5161bf00587eb36cd3ce64635126f47a98068b5c/pkg/controller/job/job_controller_test.go#L2502

title: [NodeDeclaredFeatures] Throw an error if the feature gate being checked is invalid
body: Currently, we assume that the feature gate being looked up in [Discover()](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c245b40b87ed1996282daabb158c2a9080458b53/staging/src/k8s.io/component-helpers/nodedeclaredfeatures/features/inplacepodresize/guaranteed_cpu_resize.go#L49) always exists. While falling back to an 'unset' state for an invalid gate is safe, we should return an explicit error instead of failing silently.

title: kubelet could reject pods with NodeAffinity error due to incomplete informer cache on the node object
body:
### What happened?

In our end (AKS), we observed that there is a case that kubelet could reject pods with NodeAffinty status if the node watch call got closed due to unknown reason during kubelet start up.

An illustrated procedure is (using `Tx` to indicate time):

- T1: kubelet starts, spawns the processes for registering node (create node) and node informer for syncing the node object in parallel
- T2: the node informer successfully listed empty nodes list from kube-apiserver , proceeding to watch call
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6746df77f2376c6bc1fd0de767d2a94e6bd6cec1/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/reflector.go#L401-L409
- T3: the watch call stopped due to unknown issue, for instance network closed. In this case, the watch call would exit with error like: 
  > very short watch: k8s.io/client-go/informers/factory.go:160: Unexpected watch close - watch lasted less than a second and no items received

  In this case, the node informer will back-off and retry with new list-watch steps:
  https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6746df77f2376c6bc1fd0de767d2a94e6bd6cec1/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/reflector.go#L336-L340
- T4: kubelet successfully created the node object in kube-apiserver side. Kube-scheduler kicks in and assigns pods to the node
- T5: because in T3 the list call was succeeded with empty results, the node informer had been marked as synced:
  
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6746df77f2376c6bc1fd0de767d2a94e6bd6cec1/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L442-L444
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6746df77f2376c6bc1fd0de767d2a94e6bd6cec1/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/delta_fifo.go#L308-L316
  In this case, kubelet starts syncing pods and attempts to run. If these pods are set with affinity settings, the kubelet node admission check will fail the pods with "NodeAffinity" status because the node informer cache is empty. Kubelet uses a minimal node object without expected node labels for performing admission check:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6746df77f2376c6bc1fd0de767d2a94e6bd6cec1/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_getters.go#L291-L298
- T6: kubelet node informer retry kicks in, this time it successfully synced the node object from remote. Now retried pods scheduling on this node would succeed as the node labels are expected

In our reproduction, we captured the following logs:

```
T1: kubelet[3538]: I1225 01:02:59.216231    3538 kubelet.go:2346] "Starting kubelet main sync loop"
T2: kubelet[3538]: I1225 01:04:04.030571    3538 reflector.go:359] Caches populated for *v1.Node from k8s.io/client-go/informers/factory.go:160
T3: kubelet[3538]: W1225 01:04:04.170608    3538 reflector.go:470] k8s.io/client-go/informers/factory.go:160: watch of *v1.Node ended with: very short watch: k8s.io/client-go/informers/factory.go:160: Unexpected watch close - watch lasted less than a second and no items received
T4: kubelet[3538]: I1225 01:04:08.309280    3538 kubelet_node_status.go:76] "Successfully registered node" node="<node-name>"
T5 (1): kubelet[3538]: I1225 01:04:29.348027    3538 predicate.go:164] "Predicate failed on Pod" pod="<namespace>/<pod>" err="Predicate NodeAffinity failed"
T5 (2): kubelet[3538]: E1225 01:04:29.351153    3538 kubelet_node_status.go:462] "Error getting the current node from lister" err="node \"<node-name>\" not found"
T6: kubelet[3538]: I1225 01:04:56.591752    3538 reflector.go:359] Caches populated for *v1.Node from k8s.io/client-go/informers/factory.go:160
```

In the normal case, the retry back off (between T6 and T5) should be short and kubelet should not leave many pods failed. However, in rare scenarios that the node lister might be failing for some other reasons before the first successful call (waiting for TLS bootstrapping for example), and increased the back-off (max out to 30s), then in theory, the gap of `T6-T5` could be as long as 30s + jitter, which aligns with the logs timestamps we observed in above.

### What did you expect to happen?

Kubelet should back off the node list-watch calls until the node object has been populated in the node informer cache. Or, we should invalidate the node informer cache after successfully registering the node from kubelet to maintain the correct version of node object in memory.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Simulate the watch closed call like mentioned above.

### Anything else we need to know?

Related issues/PRs:

- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/99336
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/94087

### Kubernetes version

<details>

1.30 - but we believe this behavior is reproducible in all verisons.

</details>

<details>
AKS

title: Tracking Issue: Alpha/Beta Feature Gate CI Coverage
body:
/sig testing

NOTE: This is **NOT** a good first issue!


TODO:
- [x] Implement the e2e framework changes from [Feature Gated Test Labeling Proposal](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1YkU7EusfOZO9jgJbHvCwMCfMZ5CxYMxZHAblpDdKbUQ/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.kvj5zur6ebww) 
   - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130655
   - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130908
   - https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/pull/34541
- [x] PSA dev@kubernetes.io early in 1.34 (since the framework changes landed late in 1.33)
   - https://groups.google.com/a/kubernetes.io/g/dev/c/uVga86nJDuI
- [x] Implement update alpha/beta job split
    - [x] Determine naming for jobs that enable alpha/beta in the cluster vs jobs that *run the test cases* for alpha/beta. The former will exist so we can get release signal that even alphas are safe to enable.
- [x] Drive new alpha/beta jobs to release informing 
  - https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/pull/35797
- [x] Drive subset of alpha/beta jobs to release-blocking
   - https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/pull/35796
- [x] Drive subset of jobs to *PR ~~blocking~~*
  - We opted to move more jobs to *running*, but only on PRs that touch `pkg/features` and not `Required` for now, alongside a PSA to feature approvers both through multiple slack channels and the mailinglists
  - https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/pull/36648
- [ ] Provide more visible docs for how WithFeature and WithFeatureGate should be used

See the [Feature Gated Test Labeling Proposal](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1YkU7EusfOZO9jgJbHvCwMCfMZ5CxYMxZHAblpDdKbUQ/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.kvj5zur6ebww), shared with [dev@kubernetes.io](https://groups.google.com/a/kubernetes.io/g/dev) (open for anyone to join) and kubernetes-sig-testing@googlegroups.com for prior discussion of roughly the changes required

/assign
cc @pohly @aojea @liggitt @dims

title: Make sure that underlying goroutine finishes when requests times out
body:
### What happened?

Spin off from #105611 as requested in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/105734#discussion_r732852756

Currently, timeout filter doesn't force underlying goroutine to finish. This can potentially cause hard to debug race conditions as showed in #105734
