title: Kubelet SyncTerminatedPod times out after 30s due to race with cleanupOrphanedPodCgroups
body:
### What happened?

In this [OpenShift CI run](https://prow.ci.openshift.org/view/gs/test-platform-results/logs/periodic-ci-openshift-multiarch-master-nightly-4.21-ocp-e2e-ovn-remote-s2s-libvirt-ppc64le/1999572809340162048), the upstream `[sig-node] Lifecycle sleep action zero value when create a pod with lifecycle hook using sleep action with a duration of zero seconds prestop hook using sleep action with zero duration` test failed because SyncTerminatedPod timed out. The kubelet logs shows:

```
Dec 12 21:19:08.719197 compute-1 kubenswrapper[7200]: E1212 21:19:08.719175    7200 pod_workers.go:1324] "Error syncing pod, skipping" err="failed to delete cgroup paths for [kubepods besteffort poda4418b44-5c5a-4bd5-b7b3-42860ff00483] : unable to destroy cgroup paths for cgroup [kubepods besteffort poda4418b44-5c5a-4bd5-b7b3-42860ff00483] : Timed out while waiting for systemd to remove kubepods-besteffort-poda4418b44_5c5a_4bd5_b7b3_42860ff00483.slice" pod="e2e-pod-lifecycle-sleep-action-allow-zero-761/pod-with-prestop-sleep-hook-zero-duration" podUID="a4418b44-5c5a-4bd5-b7b3-42860ff00483"
```

The systemd journal reveals that the slice was actually removed successfully ~30 seconds before the kubelet timeout:

```
Dec 12 21:18:39.127974 compute-1 systemd[1]: Removed slice libcontainer container kubepods-besteffort-poda4418b44_5c5a_4bd5_b7b3_42860ff00483.slice.
```

This shows that systemd completed the slice removal at 21:18:39, but kubelet still timed out at 21:19:08 (exactly ~30 seconds later). The timeout occurred because the kubelet goroutine that initiated the removal never received the D-Bus completion signal.

### What did you expect to happen?

Pod deletion should complete promptly after containers terminate, without a 30-second timeout.

### How can we reproduce it? (as minimally and precisely as possible)

1. Create a cluster with cgroupsPerQOS enabled (default)
2. Run a workload that creates and deletes many pods rapidly
3. Observe that some pods take 30+ seconds to fully terminate

The race is more likely to occur when:
- Multiple pods are being terminated simultaneously
- The orphaned pod cgroup cleanup housekeeping runs during pod termination

### Anything else we need to know?

#### Root Cause

There is a race condition between two code paths that call `pcm.Destroy()` on the same pod cgroup:

1. **`SyncTerminatedPod`** - [pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c34c5a5426aeb48c55c40af5c4b016a71c24d2d1/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L2398-L2402):
```go
pcm := kl.containerManager.NewPodContainerManager()
if err := pcm.Destroy(name); err != nil {
    return err
}
```

2. **`cleanupOrphanedPodCgroups`** - [pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c34c5a5426aeb48c55c40af5c4b016a71c24d2d1/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L2835-L2836):
```go
go pcm.Destroy(val)
```

Both paths can run concurrently for the same pod cgroup. The `Destroy()` method calls systemd's `StopUnit` via D-Bus using `go-systemd`.

#### Why the 30-second timeout occurs

When `StopUnitContext` is called, the `go-systemd` library:

1. Sends a D-Bus method call to systemd's `StopUnit`
2. Systemd returns a **job path** (e.g., `/org/freedesktop/systemd1/job/12345`)
3. The library registers the caller's `statusChan` in an internal map keyed by that job path
4. When systemd emits a `JobRemoved` D-Bus signal with that job path, the library sends the result to the registered channel

**The problem:** When two goroutines call `StopUnit` on the same unit concurrently, systemd may return the **same job path** for both requests (since it's already processing a stop for that unit). The `go-systemd` library overwrites the first channel registration:

[go-systemd/dbus/methods.go](https://github.com/coreos/go-systemd/blob/f3c9410fa503128ff5a025265768843eb09815ca/dbus/methods.go#L55-L75
)
```go
// In go-systemd's dbus/methods.go (simplified)
func (c *Conn) startJob(ch chan<- string, job dbus.ObjectPath) {
    c.jobListener.Lock()
    c.jobListener.jobs[job] = ch  // OVERWRITES any existing channel for this job path!
    c.jobListener.Unlock()
}
```

**Timeline of the race:**

1. **T=0ms:** Goroutine A calls `StopUnit`, gets job `/job/100`, registers `chanA`
2. **T=1ms:** Goroutine B calls `StopUnit`, gets job `/job/100`, registers `chanB` (overwrites `chanA`!)
3. **T=50ms:** Systemd finishes, emits `JobRemoved` for `/job/100`
4. **T=50ms:** go-systemd sends result to `chanB` (the only one in the map now)
5. **T=50ms:** Goroutine B completes successfully
6. **T=30s:** Goroutine A times out (`chanA` was orphaned, never receives signal)

#### Relevant code

The 30-second timeout is in [opencontainers/cgroups/systemd/common.go](https://github.com/opencontainers/cgroups/blob/main/systemd/common.go#L184-L210):

```go
func stopUnit(cm *dbusConnManager, unitName string) error {
    statusChan := make(chan string, 1)
    err := cm.retryOnDisconnect(func(c *systemdDbus.Conn) error {
        _, err := c.StopUnitContext(context.TODO(), unitName, "replace", statusChan)
        return err
    })
    if err == nil {
        timeout := time.NewTimer(30 * time.Second)
        defer timeout.Stop()

        select {
        case s := <-statusChan:
            // ...
        case <-timeout.C:
            return errors.New("Timed out while waiting for systemd to remove " + unitName)
        }
    }
    // ...
}
```

#### Proposed Fix

Use `singleflight.Group` in `podContainerManagerImpl.Destroy()` to deduplicate concurrent calls for the same cgroup. This ensures only one D-Bus `StopUnit` call proceeds per cgroup while other callers wait and receive the same result, avoiding the channel overwrite race entirely.

### Environment

- Kubernetes version: v1.34+
- CRI: CRI-O (crun/runc)
- cgroup driver: systemd

How it should work:

title: kube-apiserver crash: concurrent map read and map write in CEL ValidatingAdmissionPolicy evaluation
body:
### What happened?

The kube-apiserver crashed with a fatal error `concurrent map read and map write` during CEL expression evaluation for ValidatingAdmissionPolicy.

The crash occurs in `k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/cel/types.go:463` inside `FindStructFieldType` when reading from a `DeclType.Fields` map that is being concurrently written to.

**Stack trace (reader goroutine):**
```
fatal error: concurrent map read and map write

goroutine 11296835574 [running]:
internal/runtime/maps.fatal({0x3a59a3a?, 0xc633d97608?})
  runtime/panic.go:1058 +0x18
k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/cel.(*DeclTypeProvider).FindStructFieldType(0xc026d9dce0, {0x3a32069, 0x14}, {0xc07763b2e0, 0xc})
  k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/cel/types.go:463 +0x74
k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/cel.(*DeclTypeProvider).FindStructFieldType(0xc045262180, {0x3a32069, 0x14}, {0xc07763b2e0, 0xc})
  k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/cel/types.go:460 +0x21f
github.com/google/cel-go/interpreter.(*attrFactory).NewQualifier(...)
  github.com/google/cel-go@v0.23.2/interpreter/attributes.go:226 +0x9f
...
k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/cel.(*CompositedConditionEvaluator).ForInput(...)
  k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/cel/composition.go:188 +0x189
k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/policy/validating.(*validator).Validate(...)
  k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/policy/validating/validator.go:122 +0x772
...
k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers.(*patcher).patchResource.func2()
  k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/patch.go:704 +0xa7
```

I haven't managed to capture the writer, but I suspect it is the `AddField` method since it writes to `c.MapType.Fields[name]`

**Root Cause guess:**

I'm guessing there is a race condition in `staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/cel/composition.go`. The `NewCompositedCompilerFromTemplate` function shares the same `MapType` (and its `Fields` map) across all `CompositedCompiler` instances:

```go
// composition.go:72-77
func NewCompositedCompilerFromTemplate(context *CompositionEnv) *CompositedCompiler {
  context = &CompositionEnv{
    MapType:           context.MapType,  // SHARED - same pointer!
    EnvSet:            context.EnvSet,
    CompiledVariables: map[string]CompilationResult{},
  }
```

The singleton template is created via `getCompositionEnvTemplateWithStrictCost()` in `plugin.go:49-55`.

When multiple goroutines process admission requests concurrently:
- **Reader**: `FindStructFieldType` at `types.go:463` reads from `st.Fields[fieldName]`
- **Writer**: `AddField` at `composition.go:127` writes to `c.MapType.Fields[name]`

### What did you expect to happen?

No fatal errors

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Sorry to say I don't have a great answer here. My best guess at the root cause points towards:

1. Create a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy with CEL expressions that use variables
2. Generate high concurrent load to the API server (multiple PATCH/UPDATE requests) that trigger that policy while also updating VAPs (triggering further compilation)

### Anything else we need to know?

The crash was observed in a production environment under normal operational load. The error message preceding the crash was:
```
E1212 20:54:45.514642 12 finisher.go:175] "Unhandled Error" err="FinishRequest: post-timeout activity - time-elapsed: 1.691904645s, panicked: false, err: context canceled, panic-reason: <nil>" logger="UnhandledError"
```

title: Ingress TLS with IP certificates
body:
### What happened?

LetsEncrypt now supports IP certs (certificates valid for an IP address rather than a domain name)
The Ingress resource supports the following:
```
spec:
  rules:
  - http:
      paths:
      - backend:
          service:
            name: web
            port:
              number: 3000
        path: /
        pathType: Prefix
  tls:
  - hosts:
    - 170.9.X.X
  - secretName: ssl-certificate-secret
status:
  loadBalancer:
    ingress:
    - ip: 170.9.X.X
```
and cert-manager is able to fetch an IP cert for this ingress from LetsEncrypt but according to the docs:

> Note:
Keep in mind that TLS will not work on the default rule because the certificates would have to be issued for all the possible sub-domains. Therefore, hosts in the tls section need to explicitly match the host in the rules section.

Now, the problem is that when setting the host in the rules like:
```
spec:
  rules:
  - host: 170.9.X.X
     http:
      paths:
      - backend:
          service:
            ...
```
then the validation fails with:

```
# ingresses.networking.k8s.io "my-ingress" was not valid:
# * spec.rules[0].host: Invalid value: "170.9.X.X": must be a DNS name, not an IP address
```
So, the cert is presented to the Ingress, but it is never used to setup TLS because the host is `*` and does not matc the tls host.

That should be a pretty simple change to loosen the validation to include IP address patterns rather than just domain name


### What did you expect to happen?

I expect the TLS cert to be used and to create a listener for port 443 on my LB with TLS enabled.
This does not happen. 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

LetsEncrypt issuer for cert-manager to fetch IP certs (need to use the profile: short-lived:

```
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: ClusterIssuer
metadata: 
  name: letsencrypt-prod
spec:
  acme:
    # profile, shortlived to be able to provision IP certs
    profile: shortlived
    server: https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory
    privateKeySecretRef: 
      name: letsencrypt-issuer-prod-account-key
    solvers: 
    - http01:
        ingress:
          serviceType: ClusterIP
```

then ingress with
```
  tls:
  - hosts:
    - 170.9.X.X
  - secretName: ssl-certificate-secret
```

and try to set the host: <IP address> in the rules section and it fails.

title: Potential goroutines leak in staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/shared_informer.go
body:
### What happened?

Goroutine 1:If the method distribute() is invoked first, a goroutine holds the **RLock()** and calls listener.add(obj).
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f36be36c76192c9ccaf8c22d61ec9ed3c0a2f978/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/shared_informer.go#L863-L874
The goroutine get blocked at the `p.addCh <- notification `
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f36be36c76192c9ccaf8c22d61ec9ed3c0a2f978/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/shared_informer.go#L1015-L1020

Goroutine 2:After that, The method shouldResync() is invoked, and the goroutine get blocked at `p.resyncLock.Lock()` , waiting for the **RLock()** to be released.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f36be36c76192c9ccaf8c22d61ec9ed3c0a2f978/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/shared_informer.go#L1090-L1099

Goroutine 3: Because the goroutine 2 tries to get Lock() and Write lock has a higher priority. So p.listenersLock.RLock() get blocked, which results in p.wg.Start(listener.pop) can't get executed.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f36be36c76192c9ccaf8c22d61ec9ed3c0a2f978/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/shared_informer.go#L881-L890

And the `<-p.addCh` in listener.pop() can't be executed.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f36be36c76192c9ccaf8c22d61ec9ed3c0a2f978/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/shared_informer.go#L1037

In the situation, these three goroutines are all blocked. The interleaving sequence that triggers the bug is as follows:
```
G1                                            G2                             G3
p.resyncLock.RLock()
p.addCh <- notification
```

title: Basing removed APIs on git tag always causes verify failures when the tag is changed to beta
body:
This follows up on https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/128616#issuecomment-2465832999.

Per @liggitt's comment

> the reason we fail on beta and not alpha is that master transitions to 1.$next.0-alpha.0 as soon as we make a release branch and rc.0 for the current minor

When we transition from `1.$x.0-alpha.0` to `1.$x.0-beta.0`, the alpha flag is changed and certain resource are [dropped](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/deleted_kinds.go#L139), causing an OpenAPI diff.

I have a sample PR to force the beta tag to see the OpenAPI diff: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129863#issuecomment-2619604117. 

At the moment, we can't preemptively remove these "removed" APIs from the OpenAPI as the tag as not transitioned to beta. So we have a chicken egg problem that bumping the tag will cause CI failures because of removed types and we cannot preemptively remove the types because the tag is not bumped. With compatibility versions, we also need to keep a beta API around longer in case of emulation to previous versions.

Can we rely on something other than the git tag alpha/beta/etc for determining what APIs to serve? Perhaps a constant in a file?

cc @aojea @BenTheElder @liggitt @deads2k

title: Duplicate ports with different protocols in pod spec get merged after pod spec update
body:
### What happened?

When I add a port with a duplicate port number but different protocol (UDP instead of TCP) to an existing Deployment, one of these two ports get removed.

### What did you expect to happen?

I would expect both to be present.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Apply this:

```
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: test-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: test
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: test
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: test
        image: busybox
        command:
        - sleep
        - infinity
        ports:
        - containerPort: 1000
          protocol: TCP
```

Then `kubectl edit` the `Deployment`, duplicating the containerport, but with UDP, like this:

```
        ports:
        - containerPort: 1000
          protocol: TCP
        - containerPort: 1000
          protocol: UDP
```

And you'll observe that one of the two ports is gone in the `Deployment`.

### Anything else we need to know?

There are no mutating webhooks involved. Even with all hooks removed, I still observ this.

When you `get deploy -o yaml`, edit the yaml, `apply --server-side -f /the/yaml`, it does seem to get applied.

My guess is it is due to (only) `containerPort` being the merge key in types.go.

This is very similar to #105610, but that issue is about `Services`.

### Kubernetes version

I've observed this in 1.34.2, 1.33.6 and 1.32.4

self hosted Talos

### OS version

Talos Linux, various versions

title: Ephemeral-storage data on node status does not reflect actual available storage after disk expansion
body:
### What happened?

When expanding available node disk space (e.g. expanding root disk size on EKS node), the kubelet does not take into account the available filesystem size change and still advertises initial `ephemeral-storage`  `capacity` and `allocatable` values on node status, obtained by the kubelet on startup. **Because of that, both scheduler and kubelet reject pods with ephemeral storage requests, that actually are satisfiable by the current node root disk size.**

The root cause I believe lies in fact, for node status kubelet only ever fetches actual data on startup and then never refreshes it again: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/243d8c000e451da6f0e8f80704db5d5f672d3d18/pkg/kubelet/cm/container_manager_linux.go#L939
 
It is already done properly for node metrics (`/api/v1/nodes/worker-1/proxy/stats/summary`) and for eviction logic, meaning by not setting an ephemeral storage requests or limits I can run a pod on such node, that will effectively use more `ephemeral-storage` than what kubelet advertises (but within the bounds of expanded node disk of course) and it will not get evicted.

### What did you expect to happen?

`ephemeral-storage` capacity (and allocatable) for node status should be dynamically calculated (taken from cadvisor) on each update, without the need to restart kubelet.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create for example an EKS cluster, increase size of an EBS Volume used as root disk on any node, and grow the partition, where `/var/lib/kubelet` is. Now compare `ephemeral-storage` values in node status with actual available storage on the disk (e.g. on `/var/lib/kubelet`, to be precise).

### Anything else we need to know?

Based on the code I assume the issue is vendor-agnostic.

title: kubelet: standardize plugin support
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Here's a straw-man proposal for a future KEP:

* A node is required to support registering a plugin deployed in a pod.
* A new, builtin volume source kubeletRegistrationDir with no parameters mounts the kubelet's registration directory such that the pod has write permission there.
 * A new, builtin volume source pluginDataDir with a plugin name as parameter acts like emptyDir, except that it creates a unique path based on that plugin name.

/sig node

### Why is this needed?

At the moment, device plugins, CSI storage drivers, and DRA drivers cannot be deployed in a portable manner across different Kubernetes distros in a way which is guaranteed to work.

It's quite possible that this is not worth standardizing. In that case we can use this issue to collect arguments against it and then close it.

title: resourceFieldRef.divisor when unspecified is set to 0 (documented is 1)
body:
### What happened?

The divisor key in [ResourceFieldRef](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/kubernetes-api/common-definitions/resource-field-selector/#ResourceFieldSelector) is documented to default to 1.

However, when applying a manifest using a resourceFieldRef without specifying the divisor, then checking the spec, the divisor is set to '0'.

### What did you expect to happen?

The field should either not be present when checking the manifests, or having the correct value.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

On a kubernetes cluster, deploy the following manifest:
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  labels:
    app: test-divisor
  name: test-divisor
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: test-divisor
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: test-divisor
    spec:
      containers:
      - image: invalid-name
        name: test-divisor
        resources:
          limits:
            memory: 30M
        env:
        - name: GOMEMLIMIT
```

body:
The purpose of the `SECURITY_CONTACTS` file for each Kubernetes repository is to provide a list of people who can assist the Kubernetes [Product Security Committe](https://github.com/kubernetes/community/tree/master/committee-product-security) in the event that a security issue related to the repository is discovered or disclosed.  As described in the file, those on the list should agree to our [Embargo Policy](https://git.k8s.io/security/private-distributors-list.md#embargo-policy).

Please update the [`/staging/src/k8s.io/metrics/SECURITY_CONTACTS`](/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/metrics/SECURITY_CONTACTS) file for the metrics repository. After finding people who are willing to work in this capacity, you should add them to the list, then remove PSC members (except any PSC member will be working as a security contact for this repository). The list is GitHub usernames, optionally followed by an email address. If no email address is listed, the PSC will use the email address found on git commits made by the listed user.

The file may already have people listed who are secuirty contacts. In that case, simply remove any PSC members who aren't also security contacts for the repo.

See https://github.com/kubernetes/security/issues/92 for more information

title: Pod phase transition is slower when EventedPLEG is enabled
body:
### What happened?
After #124297, which fixes timestamps set by Evented PLEG, was merged, a pod phase transition is slower especially at deletion when the EventedPLEG is enabled.

EventedPLEG is enabled:
```
$ kubectl create -f simple-pod.yaml; kubectl get pod simple-pod -w & kubectl wait --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Running pod simple-pod; sleep 1; kubectl delete pod simple-pod; kill $!
pod/simple-pod created
NAME     	READY   STATUS          	RESTARTS   AGE
simple-pod   0/1 	ContainerCreating   0      	0s
simple-pod   1/1 	Running         	0      	3s
pod/simple-pod condition met
simple-pod   1/1 	Terminating     	0      	4s
pod "simple-pod" deleted
simple-pod   0/1 	Terminating     	0      	13s
simple-pod   0/1 	Terminating     	0      	18s
simple-pod   0/1 	Terminating     	0      	18s
simple-pod   0/1 	Terminating     	0      	18s
```

EventedPLEG is disabled:
```
$ kubectl create -f simple-pod.yaml; kubectl get pod simple-pod -w & kubectl wait --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Running pod simple-pod; sleep 1; kubectl delete pod simple-pod; kill $!
pod/simple-pod created
NAME     	READY   STATUS          	RESTARTS   AGE
simple-pod   0/1 	ContainerCreating   0      	0s
simple-pod   1/1 	Running         	0      	2s
pod/simple-pod condition met
pod "simple-pod" deleted
simple-pod   1/1 	Terminating     	0      	3s
simple-pod   0/1 	Terminating     	0      	4s
simple-pod   0/1 	Terminating     	0      	5s
simple-pod   0/1 	Terminating     	0      	5s
simple-pod   0/1 	Terminating     	0      	5s
```

As described here, a pod worker is blocked at `cache.GetNewerThan()` when it is woken up by an update without a cache update in a PLEG:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ade0d2140a68a69f5343c865792393a83c76ca6a/pkg/kubelet/pod_workers.go#L1244-L1253

The worker is unblocked when another event is delivered or the PLEG calls `cache.UpdateTime()`. At the latter case, while the genericPLEG calls `cache.UpdateTime()` every one second along with `Relist()`, the EventPLEG calls `cache.UpdateTime()` every five seconds. Because of this difference, the Evented PLEG spends more time to get pods into another phase.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ade0d2140a68a69f5343c865792393a83c76ca6a/pkg/kubelet/pleg/evented.go#L34-L37

Even if there is a cache update, a worker can be blocked when the cache is updated by an asynchronous event before the worker finishes `SyncPod()`. For instance, when a runtime starts a container, the PLEG gets an event and caches the container status(`running`). If this event is received after a pod worker finishes `SyncPod()` to start the container, the worker gets the new status at `GetNewerThan()` soon and runs `SyncPod()` again to update the pod phase to `running`. However, if the event arrives before the worker finishes `SyncPod()` to start the container, the worker is blocked at `GetNewerThan()` because the cached status is older than `lastSyncTime`.

### What did you expect to happen?

The pod phase transition should be as fast as GenericPLEG. It would be better to set `globalCacheUpdatePeriod` to 1 second.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?
This issue can be observed in the `pull-kubernetes-node-crio-cgrpv1-evented-pleg-e2e` job as described in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/124297#issuecomment-2340279198:
```
E2eNode Suite: [It] [sig-node] [NodeFeature:SidecarContainers] Containers Lifecycle [It] should not hang in termination if terminated during initialization [sig-node, NodeFeature:SidecarContainers]
{ failed [FAILED] should delete in < 5 seconds, took 10.071795
Expected
    <float64>: 10.071794756
to be <
    <int64>: 5
In [It] at: k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e_node/container_lifecycle_test.go:3470 @ 09/10/24 08:54:31.819
}
```

This can be also reproduced manually as follows:

Build kubernetes locally with applying PR #124297 and run with enabling `EventedPLEG` feature gate.

Use this simple-pod.yaml
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  labels:
	run: simple-pod
  name: simple-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - command:
	- sh
	- -c
	- trap "exit 0" SIGTERM; while true; do sleep 1; done
	image: busybox
	name: simple-container
```

title: Improve models-schema to accept generated openapi as input
body:
Currently [models-schema](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/generated/openapi/cmd/models-schema/main.go) is written such that the generated openapi is imported directly in the file:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/10f1b287121ef078a0f74d1c148a1cad89cd6926/pkg/generated/openapi/cmd/models-schema/main.go#L26

We currently copy this file into:
- `staging/src/k8s.io/kube-aggregator/pkg/generated/openapi/cmd/models-schema/main.go`
- `staging/src/k8s.io/sample-apiserver/pkg/generated/openapi/cmd/models-schema/main.go`
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/131068 will also add `staging/src/k8s.io/sample-controller/pkg/generated/openapi/cmd/models-schema/main.go`

To protect us from a drift we have a verify script in some of the above places:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/10f1b287121ef078a0f74d1c148a1cad89cd6926/staging/src/k8s.io/kube-aggregator/hack/verify-codegen.sh#L32-L43
which ensures we detect drift.

But the ideal goal is to change models-schema, such that it accepts the appropriate package as input.

This was requested in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136537#discussion_r2732152232

/sig api-machinery
/kind feature

title: client can run into infinite loop when watch ends with  too old resource version
body:
### What happened?

Scenario
1.  Test client built with pod reflector/informer，connected to apiserver A, with last sync rv 100
2.  k/v related to pod has been compacted in etcd, to rv 110
3.  another apiserver B restarts,  later it has pod watchcatch sync with oldest rv 110
4.  Apiserver A restarts, client disconnect from A, and connect to B,  continue watching pod with rv 100, but ended with:
     too old resource version: 100 (110)
5. client try to relist with rv 100 (paginated), but last sync rv will not be reset
6. client continue to watch with rv 100,  start from 4. again, this can not be self-recovered

### What did you expect to happen?

client can be self-healthed in case of watch ends with too old resource 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. build a test client with client-go v0.34.0, make lastSyncRv injectable/replacable, runs it with kube-apiserver 1.34.0
2. after inject a small enough rv, kill the apisrver which the client currently connects
3. the client continue watch with the injected rv on another apiserver, and ends with too old resource version
4. the infinite loop can be observed

### Anything else we need to know?

we found this issue on release 1.20
test shows it can still be reproduced in 1.34.0, with ListFromCacheSnapshot enabled

body:
### What would you like to be added?

[EnvFromSource](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.27/#envfromsource-v1-core) currenty has two important keys:
* `configMapRef` which is [ConfigMapEnvSource](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.27/#configmapenvsource-v1-core)
* `secretRef` which is [SecretEnvSource](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.27/#secretenvsource-v1-core)

Those two mentioned types has `name` and `optional` parameter, but does not have `namespace`. What's more interesting, there is another type: [SecretReference](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.27/#secretreference-v1-core) which has `namespace` but does not have `optional`. There is no such type as `ConfigMapReference`.

I propose the following:
* Add `optional` to `SecretReference`
* Use `SecretReference` as type of `secretRef`
* Remove `SecretEnvSource`
* Create `ConfigMapReference` type
* It should have simmilar fields as `SecretEnvSource`
* Use `ConfigMapReference` as type of `configMapRef`
* Remove `ConfigmMapEnvSource`


### Why is this needed?

This way, we will be one step closer to unified and better developer experience. As an engineer I will not need to wonder why there are so many similar types, but have different fields and purposes. And all secret/configmap references will have namespaces and unified DX across K8s ecosystem.

title: [Scheduler] Add an extension after PostFilter that will always execute
body:
### What would you like to be added?

I am a plugin developer, the plugin will have different actions according to the preemption result. For example, mark the podGorup (API in schedule-plugins) as failed and reject all the pods when failed to preempt, or I will mark the pods as schedulable (I will limit the number of times to schedule any pods in PodGroup for the performance).
But when any of the plugin return code other than fwk.Unschedulable, scheduler will skip all plugins after that. This makes difficult to implement the PostFilter:
- If we run coscheduling before preemption, we can not know the preempt result.
- If we run coscheduling after preemption and preempt return error (for example the pod is deleted when in schedulingCycle), we are not able to reject the podGroup because the scheduling stop the iteration for the PostFilter.

### Why is this needed?

Mentioned above.

title: apiserver: panic from goroutine spun up by request handler should not crash the apiserver
body:
### What happened?

request handler logic spins up goroutine, and most of them has the style: 
```
go dunc() {
     defer utilruntime.HandleCrash()

    ...
}
```

`HandleCrash` will re-raise the panic after handling it, if `ReallyCrash` is true. (`ReallyCrash` is true by default, and to my knowledge it's not overridden to `false`)

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2ab3151936f1df6b3ffb4d49bf9dc90218264545/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/runtime/runtime.go#L54-L57
The re-raised panic will go unhandled and cause the process to crash.

I have found the following code sites:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1f02f43ec6910cbcd46222b16a2f3965458e5e45/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/watch.go#L289

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1f02f43ec6910cbcd46222b16a2f3965458e5e45/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/registry/generic/registry/store.go#L1173-L1175

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1f02f43ec6910cbcd46222b16a2f3965458e5e45/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/registry/generic/registry/store.go#L1192-L1194

Mount the secret to the specified directory in the pod. The startup script of pod will read the value of secret. Our program will update the secret and then upgrade the pod. The probability of the problem is very low, we only encountered it twice in total. title: DRA should sign pods when we can determine the claims are single node
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Today DRA claims will never be signed, which means they can be never be batched and optimized. In the common case where claims are per-node we should allow for a signature.

Per johnbelamaric:
"""
  So, is the primary issue this criterion?
  
  Any two pods with the same signature should get the same feasibility and scoring for the same set of nodes in the same state.
  
  And the issue then is that for multi-node devices, the state would need to expand to include all nodes participating in that multi-node device?
  
  As a first cut, maybe we can add a calculation in the https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134326 that evaluates the pools that are part of the class, and tags them as node local or not. Maybe even better, possibly we could add a field to the DeviceClass to inform us of a few things that can help with scheduler decisions - like, explicitly limiting a device class to one driver, or even having a flag in device class that says "only allow node local" and then in the class match evaluation we exclude anything with a non-node-local. This would mean we don't need to evaluate pools to make this per-deviceclass optimization.
"""
  
See https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-scheduling/5598-opportunistic-batching and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134916

### Why is this needed?

Adoption of DRA claims will remove an important optimization for ML customers.

title: Facilitate ConfigMap rollouts / management
body:
To do a rolling update of a ConfigMap, the user needs to create a new ConfigMap, update a Deployment to refer to it, and delete the old ConfigMap once no pods are using it. This is similar to the orchestration Deployment does for ReplicaSets.

One solution could be to add a ConfigMap template to Deployment and do the management there.

Another could be to support garbage collection of unused ConfigMaps, which is the hard part. That would be useful for Secrets and maybe other objects, also.

cc @kubernetes/sig-apps-feature-requests

title: Timeout-based termination of Pod "stuck" in terminating state
body:
### What would you like to be added?

A k8s-native mechanism to handle Pod stuck in terminating state (with deletionTimestamp, but with phase=Running).

Currently, the core k8s contains a mechanism in the Pod Garbage-collector (PodGC) to mark such pods as "Failed", but it terminates (marks as Failed) only Pods on the [NotReady nodes with OutOfService taint](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7104c1e426b92025aa25083edcd3dac128f3e206/pkg/controller/podgc/gc_controller.go#L154-L160) (part of the [Non-graceful shutdown](https://kubernetes.io/blog/2023/08/16/kubernetes-1-28-non-graceful-node-shutdown-ga/)).

I think we could consider a timeout after which the taint `OutOfService` is added automatically, or timeout after which a Pod is marked as Failed (timeout buffer + spec.terminationGracePeriodSeconds probably), regardless of the Node state.

### Why is this needed?

Pods stuck in the terminating phase are problematic becuase:
- they block workload-level preemptions in Kueue from being finalized
- they don't allow to make progress by Jobs using [podReplacementPolicy: Failed](https://kubernetes.io/blog/2025/09/05/kubernetes-v1-34-pod-replacement-policy-for-jobs-goes-ga/)

The current OutOfService taint requires manual cluster admin intervention, or using some small controller to add the taint, or directly transition the Pod to Failed, or delete.

The lack of the mechanism in k8s core I think results in the ecosystem fragmentation:
- AppWrapper has its own solution based on [forceful Pod deletion](https://github.com/project-codeflare/appwrapper/blob/59ca67156f53bb0ed37dff65389e0eba3f58e12d/pkg/config/config.go#L55)
- there is the [self-node-remediation project](https://github.com/medik8s/self-node-remediation) using the OutOfService taints
- Kueue is considering introducing a similar mechanism in https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue/issues/6757

The issue is that the "fix" is very small, and many users say of Kueue may prefer so that it is fixed inside Kueue, rather than in a new project to deploy, as deploying a new operator increases operational complexity of the cluster (upgrades etc.).

So, ideally it would be done inside the core k8s.

title: Container fail to create when env var contains $ followed by non-ASCII character (invalid UTF-8 gRPC error)
body:
### What happened? After upgrading our Kubernetes cluster from v1.33.5 to v1.34.2 (AWS EKS), pods scheduled on nodes running v1.34.2 fail during container creation with the following error: ```bash grpc: error while marshaling: string field contains invalid UTF-8 ``` The pods are created successfully, but containers fail to create. Important observation: Pods scheduled on nodes still running v1.33.5 continue to work correctly with the same manifests and environment variables. The failure occurs only on nodes upgraded to v1.34.2, strongly indicating a regression. Through isolation and testing, we observed that the failure occurs when an environment variable value contains a $ immediately followed by a non-ASCII character. This behaviour did not occur on v1.33.5 and appears to be a regression introduced in v1.34.x. ### What did you expect to happen? Pods and containers should start successfully when environment variable values contain valid UTF-8 characters, including non-ASCII characters and literal $ characters. This configuration worked as expected on v1.33.5 nodes, even within the same cluster during a rolling upgrade. ### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)? 1. Create a pod (or deployment) with an environment variable containing: - a $ - immediately followed by a non-ASCII UTF-8 character 3. Schedule the pod on a v1.34.2 node 4. Observe container creation failure with: - `grpc: error while marshaling: string field contains invalid UTF-8` Minimal reproducible example: ```yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: utf8-env-repro spec: containers: - name: test image: busybox command: ["sh", "-c", "echo started && sleep 3600"] env: - name: TEST_ENV value: "$£FOO" ``` Observed result: ❌ Fails on v1.34.2 nodes ✅ Works on v1.33.5 nodes Expected result: Container starts normally on all versions. ### Anything else we need to know? - We run a custom CRD/operator that propagates env vars from the CR spec into Deployments and multi-container Pods. - The failure occurs after Pod creation, during container creation / runtime interaction. - This reproduces across all containers in the pod that receive the env var. - This is reproducible in a mixed-version cluster: - Pods on v1.33.5 nodes work - Pods on v1.34.2 nodes fail ### Kubernetes version

title: [KEP-4680] DRA: Health status is not applied to pods that have already terminated
body:
### What happened?

The DRA health status feature introduced by KEP-4680 does not currently work for pods that have already reached a terminal state (Failed or Succeeded).
E2E testing has revealed a race condition in the Kubelet's current implementation. The sequence is as follows:

1.   A pod using a DRA resource runs and its container terminates.
2.  The Kubelet immediately calls NodeUnprepareResources to begin garbage collection.
3.  The DRA manager (pkg/kubelet/cm/dra/manager.go) deletes the ClaimInfo from its cache, severing the link between the pod and the allocated device.
4.  A health update from the DRA plugin arrives after this cleanup.
5.  The Kubelet's health manager receives the update but can no longer find which pod was using the device, so the update is discarded and the PodStatus is never updated.

This prevents the "post-mortem" troubleshooting use case for batch jobs, which was an intended goal of the KEP.



### What did you expect to happen?

The `pod.status.allocatedResourcesStatus` field on the terminated pod object should be updated to reflect the health of the device at the time of failure, even if the health report arrives after the pod has stopped running.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

This was discovered via an e2e test, which can be reproduced with the following logic:

1.  Create a pod with `RestartPolicy: Never` and a command that runs for a short time before exiting, (e.g. sleep 10 && exit 1). Ensure it uses a DRA resource.
2.  Wait for the pod to enter the Running phase to confirm the resource was successfully prepared.
3.  Wait for the pod to enter the Failed phase.
4. After the pod is Failed, send an Unhealthy status update for its device from the DRA plugin.
5. Observe the pod's status. The allocatedResourcesStatus field is never populated with the unhealthy status.

### Anything else we need to know?

This issue is being filed to track a known limitation for [KEP-4680: Add Resource Health Status to the Pod Status](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/4680).

For the initial Alpha release of the DRA portion of the feature (targeting v1.34), this behavior will be documented as a known limitation. **The core value for long-running services (`RestartPolicy: Always`) is unaffected and provides a solid foundation.**

This issue will be used to track the future work required to solve this garbage collection race condition. Fixing this will be a requirement for promoting the feature to Beta or GA.

This will likely require modifying the DRA manager's state handling (`pkg/kubelet/cm/dra/manager.go`) to "tombstone" terminated ClaimInfo entries for a grace period instead of deleting them immediately upon un-preparation.

title: panic: assignment to entry in nil map in pkg/util/resource.maxResourceList when pod container has nil Resources.Requests
Duplicate keys in MatchLabelKeys of PodSpec should be explicitly validated
body:
#### Summary
If `MatchLabelKeys` of `PodSpec` contains duplicate keys, the validation should fail with an explicit error.

#### Details
If `MatchLabelKeys` of `PodSpec` contains duplicate keys, validation will fail as follows.

`sample-affinity.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: sample-affinity
  labels:
    app: sample-affinity
spec:
  containers:
  - image: nginx
    name: nginx
  affinity:
    podAffinity:
      requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      - labelSelector: {}
        topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
        matchLabelKeys:
        - app
        - app
```
 
```console
$ kubectl apply -f sample-affinity.yaml
The Pod "sample-affinity" is invalid: spec.affinity.podAffinity.requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution[0].matchLabelKeys[1]: Invalid value: "app": exists in both matchLabelKeys and labelSelector
```

It is caused by duplication between `matchLabelKeys[1]` and the key added to the `labelSelector` corresponding to `matchLabelKeys[0]`, so strictly speaking, key duplication in `matchLabelKeys` is not validated.
I think it should be explicitly validated.

#### Special notes:
#130534, which adds `matchLabelKeys` validation for `PodTemplateSpec`, is in progress.
In the case of `PodTemplateSpec`, the duplication of keys in `matchLabelKeys` is explicitly validated because the key-values corresponding to `matchLabelKeys` will not be added to the `labelSelector`.
If #130534 is merged and this issue is not addressed, the error message will differ between `PodTemplateSpec` and `PodSpec`.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0ab306a08655c72fe26c01090a154264648fd2ba/pkg/apis/core/validation/validation.go#L8032-L8040

### What would you like to be added?

I wonder if we can make a toy database-like workload that is deliberately intolerant of various snags 

eg:
* workload runners must be upgraded in index order
* if there is at any point no running replica during an upgrade, the upgrade is considered failed
* if there is at any point no quorum during an upgrade, the upgrade is considered failed
* the readiness check takes 30 seconds* 
* the workload balks at being co-hosted (same node) as another replica
* the workload checks that there are at least n÷2 other replicas with storage mounted and (indirectly) writable
* something relating to the workload runs a Job for an upgrade, and the Job that can only succeed if scheduled to a node where the workload is running
* the workload resolves its peers via DNS and is only ready if 100% of replicas are resolvable and reachable
* the workload fails if any replica has index 0

title: Pods rejected by kubelet admission control enter 'ContainerStatusUnknown' state after kubelet restart
body:
### What happened?

In scenarios where kubelet [rejects](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8a28b17c3adab3f0c9ffb8107554b2ed5021fd14/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L2273-L2279) a pod via its own admission control (`canAdmitPod`), for instance-

- When the NodeResourcesFit filter is disabled in kube-scheduler, or when a pod is directly created with a spec.nodeName (ensuring the scheduler does not validate pod resource requests against a node's capacity) AND the pod's requests exceed the node's available capacity. In this case, kubelet will reject the pod, eg. with the reason 'OutOfCpu'.

- When pods are stuck pending due to taints on a node, and the taint is removed, there appears to be a race between kube-scheduler placing the pod on the node and kubelet detecting the updated taints on the node (which makes sense, they are both presumably backed by independent watches). In this case, kubelet will reject the pod with the 'TaintToleration' reason. This is a lot harder to reproduce though, because it's racey.

This leaves the pod with a status that has an overall failed phase but no containerStatuses.
```yaml
...
status:
  message: 'Pod was rejected: Node didn''t have enough resource: cpu, requested: 8000,
    used: 950, capacity: 4000'
  phase: Failed
  qosClass: Guaranteed
  reason: OutOfcpu
  startTime: "2025-08-27T15:47:53Z"

```

After a kubelet restart (Which can be done for a few reasons, eg. handling in-place node resize, or a node reboot.), these pods transition into a ContainerStatusUnknown state.

```bash
$ kubectl get po
NAME      READY   STATUS     RESTARTS   AGE
busybox   0/1     OutOfcpu   0          2s

$ docker exec -it $(docker ps | grep kindest | awk '{print $1}') systemctl restart kubelet

$ kubectl get po
NAME      READY   STATUS                   RESTARTS   AGE
busybox   0/1     ContainerStatusUnknown   0          17s

```

where the overall status now has additional conditions for last probe time, container statuses showing container status unknown, etc.
```
status:
  conditions:
  - lastProbeTime: null
    lastTransitionTime: "2025-08-27T15:48:34Z"
    status: "False"
    type: PodReadyToStartContainers
  - lastProbeTime: null
    lastTransitionTime: "2025-08-27T15:48:34Z"
    status: "True"
    type: Initialized
  - lastProbeTime: null
    lastTransitionTime: "2025-08-27T15:48:34Z"
    reason: PodFailed
    status: "False"
    type: Ready
  - lastProbeTime: null
    lastTransitionTime: "2025-08-27T15:48:34Z"
    reason: PodFailed
    status: "False"
    type: ContainersReady
  - lastProbeTime: null
    lastTransitionTime: "2025-08-27T15:48:34Z"
    status: "True"
    type: PodScheduled
  containerStatuses:
  - image: busybox:1.37.0-glibc
    imageID: ""
    lastState: {}
    name: busybox
    ready: false
    restartCount: 0
    started: false
    state:
      terminated:
        exitCode: 137
        finishedAt: null
        message: The container could not be located when the pod was terminated
        reason: ContainerStatusUnknown
        startedAt: null
    volumeMounts:
    - mountPath: /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount
      name: kube-api-access-79svn
      readOnly: true
      recursiveReadOnly: Disabled
  hostIP: 172.18.0.2
  hostIPs:
  - ip: 172.18.0.2
  message: 'Pod was rejected: Node didn''t have enough resource: cpu, requested: 8000,
    used: 950, capacity: 4000'
  phase: Failed
  qosClass: Guaranteed
  reason: OutOfcpu
  startTime: "2025-08-27T15:47:53Z"
```

A similar issue can also be reproduced when using init containers
```bash
kubectl get po -A
NAMESPACE            NAME                                         READY   STATUS                        RESTARTS   AGE
default              busybox                                      0/1     Init:ContainerStatusUnknown   0          11s
```



### What did you expect to happen?

I'm not sure if this is by design, but I would expect such rejected pods to remain in an OutOfCpu/TaintsToleration failure state. No containers were ever started as the pod was rejected in admission control. The error _sounds_ like something went missing from the container runtime, but that did not happen, of course.

We could work around this by GCing such pods, but I wonder if this could be handled more gracefully at the Kubernetes layer (and I would also hate to mask genuine container runtime issues by clubbing multiple such ContainerStatusUnknown issues together)


### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Using 'kind' for ease of cluster LCM, but this can happen in any vanilla K8s cluster.

- Ensure you have kind installed.
```bash
go install sigs.k8s.io/kind@v0.29.0
```

- Create a massive pod (in terms of container requests) that cannot fit on the node based on node selector. eg. pod.yaml

```yaml
spec:
  containers:
  ...
    resources:
      requests:
        memory: "64000Mi"
        cpu: "8000m"
      limits:
        memory: "64000Mi"
        cpu: "8000m"
```

- Apply the YAML
```bash
kubectl apply -f pod.yaml
```
- Verify pod state

```bash
➜  ContainerStatusUnknown-repro kubectl get po
NAME      READY   STATUS     RESTARTS   AGE
busybox   0/1     OutOfcpu   0          2s
```

- Docker exec into the kind node and restart kubelet
```bash
docker exec -it $(docker ps | grep kindest | awk '{print $1}') systemctl restart kubelet
```

- Verify pod state

```bash
➜  ContainerStatusUnknown-repro kubectl get po
NAME      READY   STATUS                   RESTARTS   AGE
busybox   0/1     ContainerStatusUnknown   0          17s
```


### Anything else we need to know?

Sifting through the kubelet code, I saw a few sites where we seem to iterate over the containers for a pod and if any are missing statuses (eg. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/850bc09e9b78e49ec2459515379ae042a142e5c9/pkg/kubelet/status/status_manager.go#L441-L470) - my guess is post restart there's a full sync being run and kubelet has lost track of the fact that no containers were ever started for that pod. I imagine it's possible to instrument kubelet with targeted logging to see the specific site where this is happening.


### Kubernetes version

1.31.14 (VMware)
1.33.0 (kind)

N/A, reproduced on VMware and kind.

N/A, does not seem OS specific. reproduced on Photon OS and kind.

body:
### What happened?

CRDs that use standard numeric formats for both integer and number types do not actually enforce these constraints during validation. 

This is a follow up issue of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/133880

### What did you expect to happen?

Reject invalid integer/number following the defined formats.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Scenario A (Integer/int32):
1. Create a CRD with a field: type: integer, format: int32.
2. Apply a Custom Resource with the value 2147483648.
3. Observed Behavior: Resource is accepted. Expected Behavior: Rejected (out of range).

Scenario B (Number/float):
1. Create a CRD with a field: type: number, format: float.
2. Apply a Custom Resource with the value 3.5e+38.
3. Observed Behavior: Resource is accepted. Expected Behavior: Rejected (out of range).

### Anything else we need to know?

The lack of enforcement is caused by a combination of two gaps in the validation pipeline:

1. Format Stripping: In pkg/apiserver/validation/formats.go, the StripUnsupportedFormatsPostProcessorForVersion function strips these formats from the schema because they are not explicitly whitelisted for numeric types. This prevents the validator from even knowing a format was requested.
2. Validator Initialization Gap: In k8s.io/kube-openapi/pkg/validation/validate/schema.go, the `numberValidator` is initialized without the Type and Format fields from the schema. Even if the format isn't stripped, the validator lacks the context to call IsValueValidAgainstRange correctly.
```go
func (s *SchemaValidator) numberValidator() ValueValidator {
	return &numberValidator{
		Path:             s.Path,
		In:               s.in,
		Default:          s.Schema.Default,
		MultipleOf:       s.Schema.MultipleOf,
		Maximum:          s.Schema.Maximum,
		ExclusiveMaximum: s.Schema.ExclusiveMaximum,
		Minimum:          s.Schema.Minimum,
		ExclusiveMinimum: s.Schema.ExclusiveMinimum,
	}
}
```

title: [Cleanup] Default KUBE_PROXY_DAEMONSET to true in GCE cluster scripts
body:
### What happened?

While auditing stale TODO comments in the GCE configuration scripts (following my recent merged cleanup PR #136379), I identified a 9-year-old TODO at line 525 of cluster/gce/config-test.sh. The environment variable KUBE_PROXY_DAEMONSET still defaults to false, causing kube-proxy to be deployed as static pods in certain GCE test configurations.

### What did you expect to happen?

I expect GCE cluster configurations to align with modern Kubernetes standards (like kubeadm), where kube-proxy is managed as a DaemonSet by default. This change will allow for the future removal of legacy static-pod logic in cluster/gce/gci/configure-helper.sh, significantly reducing technical debt.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Inspect cluster/gce/config-test.sh at line 527.
2. Observe KUBE_PROXY_DAEMONSET=${KUBE_PROXY_DAEMONSET:-false}.
3. This stems from Commit 1102656 (PR #50705) from 2017, where the variable was introduced as an experimental option but never flipped to the default.

### Anything else we need to know?

I am a DevOps Engineer and am happy to take ownership of this transition. My plan is to:

1. Flip the default to true.
2. Monitor CI signal (pull-kubernetes-e2e-gce) to ensure no regressions.
3. Submit a follow-up PR to deprecate the false code path once verified.

title: Mixing +default with hand-written defaults breaks ordering
Frequent churn between EndpointSlice objects
body:
### What happened?

We are running a single control-plane k3s cluster in our lab. The cluster has about 56 high-power bare metal nodes. The cluster is used primarily by our developers and our CICD. We create kubevirt VMs for dev and testing. 

Recently as our cluster grew to serve a 100+ kubevirt VMs (running in pods), we noticed significant uptick in the number of ssh and nslookup failures by our CICD system when trying to communicate with the VMs. On average, we would see 1 in 100 or so attempts fail to resolve the VMs IP address. The lookups happened based on the VM name. We use a single headless Service for all of our VMs. 

We wrote a small script to see if we could reproduce the issue. The script would send DNS lookups (dig) to all running healthy VMs (VM status = ready). We noticed that coredns would occasionally return NXDOMAIN for perfectly healthy VMs. Importantly, those VMs were not going through any state transition. The NXDOMIANs would be short-lived, usually < 10 seconds and then it go back to resolving correctly. Again, it's important to note that the VMs(and their pods) for which the NXDOMAIN was received were not transitioning states during this period. 

To see why coredns would behave this way, we wrote another program to watch for updates on the EndpointSlice object. What we noticed was that when the number of endpoints per slice grew greater than 100 (the default value), then, as expected, a new slice would be created. However, what would happen next was surprising. The two endpointslices would start to exhibit significant churn, where endpoints would be frequently be removed from one slice and added to the other. Here is a snippet for the two slices: tortuga-4frcm and tortuga-sxqh9. The program logs the type of event (e.g. MODIFIED) and what changed (i.e. it does a diff between the old and new object). Some additional information that may be helpful:
1. We noticed that the control plane was complaining with these errors:

```
Aug 06 22:20:32 node-name-foo k3s[2663]: time="2025-08-06T22:20:32Z" level=warning msg="Proxy error: write failed: io: read/write on closed pipe"
Aug 06 22:20:42node-name-foo k3s[2663]: I0806 22:20:42.363009    2663 endpointslice_controller.go:337] "Error syncing endpoint slices for service, retrying" key="jenkins/tortuga" err="EndpointSlice informer cache is out of date"
```

2. We are running a single control-plane k3s cluster in our lab. It's certainly possible that this node when under load cannot send out events fast enough to all services (like coredns). However, we would expect that the system should continue to resolve valid VMs to their IPs. 

How does this tie into the coredns issue of returning NXDOMAIN for valid VMs?

Coredns also uses endpointslice objects. One theory would be that there is a significant time gap between the slice update events. Using the example above, an update where one slice removes a (valid) VM is received and then after a delay of several seconds, the update for the second slice, which includes the previously removed VM, is received. Between these two updates, coredns returns NXDOMAIN for the valid VM. 

Other thoughts:
1. The moving of endpoints between slices seems racy to me. If there is significant delay between propagating updates of the two slices, then services like coredns will have temporary inconsistencies. 
2. Is there a corner case where the endpointslice controller frequently balances endpoints across slices? Can this balancing be disabled?
3. Should coredns (and other consumers of endpointslice) be enhanced to detect stale cache entries?  
4. Is this expected behavior? I hope not. 

### What did you expect to happen?

We expect that coredns should reliably resolve IPs for VMs/Pods that are healthy.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Unfortunately, this is not easy to produce, primarily because the issue seems to arise when the control-plane is under load and is having a hard time sending updates to all informers. 

### Anything else we need to know?

Our current workaround has been to increase endpoints pers slice from 100 (default) to 200. This has mitigated the issue for the time being, but we would like to scale to 500+ endpoints. Single slice approach may not be appropriate at that point.

title: Temporary volumes (emptyDir, configMap, secrets) created with 0777 permissions – Security concern and compliance question
body:
### What happened?

Hello Kubernetes team,
A vulnerability scan (SHC) has flagged a potential misconfiguration (ID: RIES-693, also known as "Riesgo 55 en Misuri") due to temporary directories being created with 0777 permissions inside Kubernetes pods.

We have observed that:

    The issue affects volumes created from emptyDir, configMap, and secret.

    It is reproducible and not random, and seems to be part of Kubernetes' standard behavior.

    These directories are being created with world-writable (0777) permissions, which conflicts with various internal security and hardening policies.

    This behavior is not caused by the container runtime. We use CRI-O (Kubernetes v1.32.7), which is the recommended runtime, and the issue appears to originate in Kubernetes core.

We have reviewed the following related issue:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/125876

In that thread, it is acknowledged that Kubernetes is assigning these permissions, and there's a TODO in the codebase suggesting it is known but not yet addressed. However, it's still unclear whether:

    This behavior is intentional and accepted, or

    It is a pending security enhancement or known issue under consideration.
Request:
Due to compliance requirements, we kindly request one of the following:

    Confirmation that this behavior is expected and accepted by the Kubernetes project, ideally with links to relevant documentation or design decisions.

    OR, confirmation that this is a known issue, and any information about plans to address it or a suggested mitigation.

We need this as evidence that the issue has been escalated to the Kubernetes maintainers.
🔧 Environment:

    Kubernetes version: v1.32.7

    Container runtime: CRI-O

  Thank you

Thank you in advance for your time and guidance. We understand this may be a deeply technical or legacy-driven decision, but any clarification or support you can provide will be extremely helpful to us and likely to others in regulated industries.

Kind regards,

### What did you expect to happen?

We expected the temporary directories created by Kubernetes for emptyDir, configMap, and secret volumes to have more restrictive default permissions — for example, 0755 or 0700 — instead of 0777, which grants world-writable access.

This expectation is based on common security hardening practices and compliance standards, which typically discourage the use of world-writable permissions (0777) in production environments, especially for sensitive volumes managed by the container orchestration platform.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

title: Scheduler does not consider pod-deletion-cost during rollout, leading to pod imbalance
body:
### What happened?

During rollout of a Deployment with a `rollingUpdate` strategy (`maxSurge: 3`, `maxUnavailable: 0`) and `podAntiAffinity` based on `pod-template-hash`, the Kubernetes Scheduler does not take the `pod-deletion-cost` annotation into account. This leads to an imbalance where two pods with different `pod-template-hash` values are scheduled on the same node for an extended period. Specifically, the Scheduler should prioritize scheduling on nodes with existing pods of lower-cost pods in a manner that maintains a balanced distribution across nodes.

For example, in a setup with 6 replicas across 6 nodes, when a rollout begins, new pods are scheduled alongside existing ones without considering their deletion costs, resulting in a situation with two pods on one node and none on others, thus leading to an undesired imbalance throughout the rollout.


### What did you expect to happen?

I expected that the Scheduler would take `pod-deletion-cost` into account when scheduling new replicas during a rollout, ensuring that it removes lower-cost pods first and maintains balanced distribution across nodes to comply with `podAntiAffinity` rules.


### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a Deployment with the following configuration:
    ```yaml
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    metadata:
      name: foo
    spec:
      replicas: 6
      selector:
        matchLabels:
          app: foo
      template:
        metadata:
          labels:
            app: foo
        spec:
          affinity:
            podAntiAffinity:
              requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
              - labelSelector:
                  matchExpressions:
                  - key: app.kubernetes.io/name
                    operator: In
                    values:
                    - foo
                matchLabelKeys:
                - pod-template-hash
                topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
          containers:
          - name: foo
            image: foo:latest
    ```
2. Annotate the pods with pod-deletion-cost as shown below:
```
| node   | pod  | pod-template-hash | pod-deletion-cost | Zone       |
| NodeA1 | pod1 | foo-123           | 999               | us-west-2a | 
| NodeB1 | pod2 | foo-123           | 999               | us-west-2b |
| NodeC1 | pod3 | foo-123           | 999               | us-west-2c |
| NodeA2 | pod4 | foo-123           | 998               | us-west-2a | 
| NodeB2 | pod5 | foo-123           | 998               | us-west-2b |
| NodeC2 | pod6 | foo-123           | 998               | us-west-2c |
```

3. Do a rollout restart, it surges and it could do the following:
```
| node   | pod  | pod-template-hash | pod-deletion-cost | Zone       |
| NodeA1 | pod1 | foo-123           | 999               | us-west-2a | 
| NodeA1 | pod7 | foo-124           | <not-set-yet>     | us-west-2a | 
| NodeB1 | pod2 | foo-123           | 999               | us-west-2b |
| NodeB1 | pod8 | foo-124           | <not-set-yet>     | us-west-2b |
| NodeC1 | pod3 | foo-123           | 999               | us-west-2c |
| NodeA2 | pod4 | foo-123           | 998               | us-west-2a | 
| NodeB2 | pod5 | foo-123           | 998               | us-west-2b |
| NodeC2 | pod6 | foo-123           | 998               | us-west-2c |
| NodeC2 | pod9 | foo-124           | <not-set-yet>     | us-west-2c |
```

This will put two pods (with different pod-template-hash) onto the same node, but take down the pods with lower cost, leading to:

```
| node   | pod  | pod-template-hash | pod-deletion-cost | Zone       |
| NodeA1 | pod1 | foo-123           | 999               | us-west-2a |
```

title: When the API server calls multiple validating webhooks, it should surface all errors to the client, not just the first error returned by a webhook
body:
### What would you like to be added?

When the API server calls multiple validating webhooks, it should surface all errors to the client, not just the first error returned by a webhook.

The validating webhook dispatcher was implemented in [#58381](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/58381). It calls multiple webhooks in parallel. When more than one webhook returns an error, the dispatcher only surfaces the first error to the API client. It [logs](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/24877f96fbb60f34c1c808e7ac76870019eee86b/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/webhook/validating/dispatcher.go#L242) the remaining errors.

The original commit included a [TODO](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/24877f96fbb60f34c1c808e7ac76870019eee86b/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/webhook/validating/dispatcher.go#L241) to merge the errors, presumably because all errors should be surfaced to the API client.


### Why is this needed?

As a user of a resource that associated with more than one validating webhook, I know that all these webhooks are called in parallel when I try to create the resource. If more than one webhook rejects my create request, I want to know the reasons behind all of the rejections. That is, I the API server to surface the errors returned by all the webhooks.

title: watchlist request will be closed abnormally when cacheInterval contains a large amount of watchEvents
body:
### What happened?

I'm conducting an investigation into watchList benchmark in 1.30 Kubernetes cluster. I found that using `watchList` request to make the reflector become synced takes longer than using `list` request. 

Then, I found that the apiserver always prints `Forcing %s watcher close due to unresponsiveness: key.... ` log.  I realized that if `cacheInterval ` containes lots of watchEvents, then cacheWatcher.Process will not be invoked until all watchEvents in `cacheInterval` have been sent. As a result, the `input` channel in `cacheWatcher` may become full, leading to the abnormal closure of the watchlist request.

Therefore, are there any solutions to address this issue? Perhaps we need a new watchList request handler to process watchList requests instead of reusing the original watch request handler's logic. 

If there isn't a similar issue in this problem, we can use the current issue to track it. :)

### What did you expect to happen?

Using watchList request to make the reflector become synced takes approximately the same amount of time as using list request.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. create 5K Pods
2. use watchlist request to make reflector become synced. At the same time, start many client to update pods
3. watchlist request will be close and apiserver prints `Forcing %s watcher close due to unresponsiveness: key.... ` log

title: Kubelet CSI init backoff too short when DNS is unreachable; kubelet restarts before NSS falls back to `myhostname`
body:
### What happened?

## Problem origin (ARO/OCP bugs)
- OCPBUGS-64883 and OCPBUGS-67200: on ARO with UDR and a non-responsive DNS, new workers never register Node/CSINode. Kubelet restarts during CSI init.

## Root cause
- NSS `hosts:` ordering on RHEL/RHCOS/Fedora is typically `files dns myhostname`. With blackholed DNS, glibc waits for DNS timeouts before reaching `myhostname`.
- Default resolver budget can be ~20–60s (A+AAAA, up to 3 nameservers, attempts=2, timeout=5s), longer if `timeout`/`attempts` are higher.
- Kubelet’s CSI init backoff in `pkg/volume/csi/csi_plugin.go` is ~23s total, despite the comment claiming ~140s. It exits before DNS fallback completes, so kubelet restarts and never initializes `CSINode`.

## Why increase the timeout
- To survive realistic DNS timeouts and let `myhostname` succeed, the backoff should exceed the DNS worst case. Raising it toward the documented ~140s (or at least >60–90s) aligns behavior with the comment and prevents restart loops when DNS is slow/unreachable.

## OS/NSS considerations
- Reordering NSS to place `myhostname` before `dns` would avoid the wait, but distro defaults/operator preferences differ; consensus is hard. Increasing kubelet’s backoff is a practical, compatible mitigation.

## Proposed backoff
```
New exponential backoff steps:
  sleep 1:  32.55437ms
  sleep 2:  254.104702ms
  sleep 3:  2.059965819s
  sleep 4:  16.567802964s
  sleep 5:  2m14.365124124s  <-- roughly 140 seconds
```

## Request
- Update CSI init backoff parameters so the actual cap matches the intended ~140s (or another explicit target ≥ DNS timeout budget), and fix the comment to reflect the real value. This allows kubelet to complete CSI/CSINode initialization even when DNS is slow or unreachable.

### What did you expect to happen?

Exponential backoff should be roughly 140 seconds.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

    1. Create a new worker node whose DNS server will time out
    2. Observe that kubelet will never create the Node object

### Anything else we need to know?

NOTE: I assume that the original backoff values assumed there will be 6 sleep cycles. However, the `ExponentialBackoff` skips the last sleep iteration: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9f6977db54084d766c1fec19f383bf509d7e8610/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/wait/backoff.go#L480-L481

Feature requests: Support adding label based indexes to apiserver cache
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Support adding label based indexes to apiserver cacher to speed up list and watch requests by labels. 

### Why is this needed?

Background: Each job of the big data computing engine spark/flink will start a master pod to create/list/watch/delete worker pods, namely the Driver pod of spark and the JobManager pod of flink.
spark:
list: https://github.com/apache/spark/blob/branch-3.5/resource-managers/kubernetes/core/src/main/scala/org/apache/spark/scheduler/cluster/k8s/ExecutorPodsPollingSnapshotSource.scala#L77-L92
watch: https://github.com/apache/spark/blob/branch-3.5/resource-managers/kubernetes/core/src/main/scala/org/apache/spark/scheduler/cluster/k8s/ExecutorPodsWatchSnapshotSource.scala#L63-L67

flink:
list: https://github.com/apache/flink/blob/master/flink-kubernetes/src/main/java/org/apache/flink/kubernetes/kubeclient/Fabric8FlinkKubeClient.java#L207-L215
watch: https://github.com/apache/flink/blob/master/flink-kubernetes/src/main/java/org/apache/flink/kubernetes/kubeclient/Fabric8FlinkKubeClient.java#L251-L257

In our production k8s cluster, each cluster may run thousands of spark or flink jobs in parallel (the number of jobs may be roughly the same as the number of nodes, or even higher). We found that this will cause great pressure on the apiserver. The number of pod add events sent by the apiserver to the scheduler per second will not keep up with the speed of pod creation per second, resulting in the scheduling speed not matching the speed of pod creation, resulting in resource waste.

Although https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/115918 has added namespace indexes to the cacher's watch function, this function is not so useful in scenarios where a large number of jobs are running in a small number of namespaces. Most events are still sent to each cacheWatcher through the cacher first and then filtered, causing high CPU usage on the apiserver and delays in event delivery.

In fact, each spark and flink job only lists and watches the worker pods of each job through the applicationId label of the job, and does not list and watch the worker pods of other jobs (as we can see from the list/watch code of spark and flink above). This is very similar to the way each pod of daemonsets watches the pod of each node according to spec.nodeName. The number of watchers for these jobs is also comparable to the number of watchers for daemonsets.

Since the apiserver has a watch index of spec.nodeName by default, we also want to add an applicationId index, considering that different scenarios may use different label names. Therefore, we optimized the apiserver to build an index based on certain configurable labels, such as `metadata.labels.app` or `metadata.labels.spark-app-selector`, so that the pod event of each job can query the matching watchers in the cacher's dispatchEvent, without having to broadcast to a large number of unmatched cacheWatchers first and then filter them out by cacheWatcher.

Before implementing this feature, we could only isolate an apiserver for the scheduler to use, and big data jobs or daemonsets would not access this apiserver, so that the number of events received by the scheduler per second could keep up with the number of pods created per second. With this feature, we no longer need to isolate the apiserver separately, and the CPU of the apiserver is also reduced a lot.

title: Support async moveAllToActiveOrBackoffQueue in scheduler
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Kube-Scheduler uses scheduling hint to determine whether the pods should be moved to ActiveQ. Scheduler will lock and traverse all pods in unschedulableQ to find which pods might become schedulable due to the incoming event. Many operation on SchedulingQueue will be blocked if the events come too frequently.

For example, if someone updates assigned pod in a high frequency, the SchedulingQueue will be blocked by assignedPodUpdate() and new pods can not be added into the activeQ, result in scheduler hang.

I want to make moveAllToActiveOrBackoffQueue run in a background goroutine, check multi cluster events once a time, and limit its frequency to avoid influencing other SchedulingQueue operation.

### Why is this needed?

If someone updates assigned pod in a high frequency, the SchedulingQueue will be blocked by assignedPodUpdate() and new pods can not be added into the activeQ, result in scheduler hang.

title: A potential data conflict occurs in cert_rotation.go
body:
clientCert is read/written 4 times in cert_rotation.go; 3 out of 4 times it is protected by c.certMtx.RLock()/Lock(),which is in L76、L77、L84; 1 out of 4 times it is read without a Lock, which is in [L97](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/transport/cert_rotation.go#L79)

> 	c.certMtx.RLock()
	haveCert := c.clientCert != nil
	if certsEqual(c.clientCert, cert) {
		c.certMtx.RUnlock()
		return c.clientCert, nil
	}
	c.certMtx.RUnlock()

In the above code, I think it would be better to first store c.clientCert in a temporary variable and then return it.

> 	c.certMtx.RLock()
	haveCert := c.clientCert != nil
	if certsEqual(c.clientCert, cert) {
                temp:=c.clientCert
		c.certMtx.RUnlock()
		return temp, nil
	}
	c.certMtx.RUnlock()

Excuse me, how do you view this issue? I'm looking forward to your reply.

title: Watches are not drained during graceful termination when feature gate APIServingWithRoutine is on
body:
### What happened?

I tried to observe the graceful termination of kube-apiserver, in particular, how watches are drained.
1) I created a cluster in 1.30 with kube-apiserver flags
```
--shutdown-delay-duration=10s --shutdown-send-retry-after=true --shutdown-watch-termination-grace-period=60s 
```

```
"terminationGracePeriodSeconds"=60,
```

```
"[graceful-termination] active watch request(s) have drained" duration="1m0s" activeWatchesBefore=0 activeWatchesAfter=0 error=null
```

Also, I do not observe any logs of watches being closed.

When I do the same procedure as above but for cluster 1.29.6 (or a cluster with feature gate `APIServingWithRoutine` off) I see a log similar to this one
```
"[graceful-termination] active watch request(s) have drained" duration="1m0s" activeWatchesBefore=623 activeWatchesAfter=0 error=null"
```

Create clusters in 1.30 with provided kube-apiserver flags and with feature gate `APIServingWithRoutine` on and off, respectively.
