title: [Failing Test] user namespaces kubeconfig tests [LinuxOnly] [Feature:UserNamespacesSupport] [Serial]  Kubelet crashes on restart when idsPerPod changes with existing userns pods on disk
body:
### Which jobs are failing?

`ci-node-crio-swap-serial`

### Which tests are failing?

```
[sig-node] user namespaces kubeconfig tests [LinuxOnly] [Feature:UserNamespacesSupport] [Serial] test config using userNamespaces.idsPerPod honors idsPerPod in userns pods
```

`k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e_node/user_namespaces_test.go:71`

### Since when has it been failing?

Observed in job run [2034607623600345088](https://gcsweb.k8s.io/gcs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-node-crio-swap-serial/2034607623600345088/artifacts/e2-standard-2-fedora-coreos-43-20260301-3-1-gcp-x86-64-117cbc54/).

### Testgrid link

N/A

### Reason for failure (if possible)

> **Note:** The following analysis is AI-summarized from the linked CI logs and source code.

The kubelet fatally crashes during restart when `userNamespaces.idsPerPod` is changed and a pod created with the previous `idsPerPod` value still has its directory on disk.

**Failing log line** (from [kubelet.log](https://gcsweb.k8s.io/gcs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-node-crio-swap-serial/2034607623600345088/artifacts/e2-standard-2-fedora-coreos-43-20260301-3-1-gcp-x86-64-117cbc54/kubelet.log)):
```
E0319 12:51:56.731779  8547 run.go:72] "command failed" err="failed to run Kubelet: failed to create kubelet:
  create user namespace manager: record pod mappings for existing pod \"5982517a-d29a-4eae-887d-773f1f8a0548\":
  wrong user namespace length 131072"
```

**Sequence of events:**

1. The test sets `userNamespaces.idsPerPod = 131072` (65536 × 2) and restarts the kubelet.
2. A pod with `hostUsers: false` is created. The kubelet allocates a user namespace mapping with `length = 131072` and persists it to the pod's `userns` file on disk.
3. The pod succeeds and the test deletes it.
4. The AfterEach restores the original kubelet config (default `idsPerPod = 65536`) and restarts the kubelet.
5. During initialization, `MakeUserNsManager()` scans existing pod directories on disk (`pkg/kubelet/userns/userns_manager.go:185-190`). It finds the not-yet-cleaned-up pod directory, reads its `userns` file (which has `length = 131072`), and calls `record()`.
6. `record()` (`pkg/kubelet/userns/userns_manager.go:242-243`) performs a strict equality check:
   ```go
   if length != m.userNsLength {
       return fmt.Errorf("wrong user namespace length %v", length)
   }
   ```
   This fails because `131072 != 65536`, and the error is fatal — the kubelet never starts.
7. The AfterEach times out after 120s waiting for the kubelet health check, and the test is marked as FAILED.

**Impact:** This also means that outside of tests, changing `idsPerPod` in a kubelet config and restarting the kubelet will crash the kubelet if any pods using the old value still have directories on disk. The strict check in `record()` does not account for pods that were created with a different `idsPerPod`.

### Additional context

- [Full CI job logs](https://gcsweb.k8s.io/gcs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-node-crio-swap-serial/2034607623600345088/artifacts/e2-standard-2-fedora-coreos-43-20260301-3-1-gcp-x86-64-117cbc54/)

title: Deployment controller: Inconsistency of deletePod pod update handler and oldPodsRunning condition
body:
### What happened?

We observed that in cluster with phase=Failed pods present, the update of the deployment using Recreate strategy was stalling for ~10 minutes (ProgressDeadlineSeconds period).

After a log analysis and code, I think this is caused by the fact that [deletePod handler](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/74e84a90c725047b1328ff3d589fedb1cb7a120e/pkg/controller/deployment/deployment_controller.go#L385-L391) (the handler attached to pod informer), for Recreate case is enqueuing the deployment only if the number of pods equals zero. OTOH if the loop triggers, the different condition is checked: [oldPodsRunning](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/74e84a90c725047b1328ff3d589fedb1cb7a120e/pkg/controller/deployment/recreate.go#L48-L51) ignores the terminal state pods such as Failed/Succeeded.

In effect, we may not enqueue deployment at the time when oldPodsRunning becomes true in a case when e.g. Succeeded pod is present.

### What did you expect to happen?

That the deployment is enqueued at the time when oldPodsRunning becomes true -- the last pod is deleted.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

* Create a deployment with a pod in Failed state (we used a deployment with image that OOMs quite often)
* Try to update deployment few times
* You will observe that the updates starts to be delayed by ~10m at some point.

### Anything else we need to know?

A proposed fix is to change the deletePod to exclude the Final/Succeed state or even better share the logic with the oldPodsRunning condition (maybe even call it from there).

title: client-go v1.32/v1.33 WatchList is incompatible with kube-apiserver v1.34
body:
### What happened?

When using `client-go` `v1.32.x` against a Kubernetes `v1.34.x` API server, informers/reflectors may log:
> The watchlist request for nodes ended with an error, falling back to the standard LIST semantics, err = "kubernetes.io/initial-events-list-blueprint" annotation is missing content

The client then falls back to standard `LIST/WATCH`, so this is not always a fatal failure, but the WatchList path itself is not compatible.

### What did you expect to happen?
`client-go v1.32.x` should either:
1. remain compatible with a `v1.34.x` API server for WatchList, or
2. cleanly avoid using the incompatible WatchList path.


### How can we reproduce it?

Use:

- `client-go`: `v1.32.x` (same applies to `v1.33.x`)
- `kube-apiserver`: `v1.34.x`



Enable the client WatchList path (`WatchListClient`) and start an informer/reflector against a `v1.34` apiserver.

The reflector will attempt WatchList and then log:

> The watchlist request ended with an error, falling back to the standard LIST/WATCH semantics ...

with the specific error:

> `"kubernetes.io/initial-events-list-blueprint" annotation is missing content`

### What do you see in the code?

In `client-go v1.32.x`, the WatchList client logic still expects the bookmark event to contain:

`kubernetes.io/initial-events-list-blueprint`

The old code path is in `staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/rest/request.go`:

- `WatchListResult`
- `WatchListResult.Into()`
- `Request.handleWatchList()`

That code explicitly reads `metav1.InitialEventsListBlueprintAnnotationKey` from the bookmark and returns an error if the annotation is empty/missing.

In Kubernetes `v1.34`, the API server removed that annotation from the synthetic bookmark event. The 1.34 changelog explicitly says:

> Removes the `kubernetes.io/initial-events-list-blueprint` annotation from the synthetic "Bookmark" event for the watch stream requests.

Also, newer reflector code no longer reconstructs a typed `List` from the watch stream. Instead it uses:

- `Watch + SendInitialEvents=true`
- writes initial `Added` events into a temporary store
- waits for the `k8s.io/initial-events-end=true` bookmark
- `Replace()`s the main store
- reuses the same watch stream for incremental events


So the old blueprint-based WatchList client protocol and the new server behavior no longer match.

### Is this a supported skew?
`client-go` compatibility matrix marks `v0.32.0` vs Kubernetes `1.34` as `+-`, not `✓`, so some incompatibility is allowed. However, this specific WatchList protocol break is concrete and user-visible.


### Impact

- WatchList path in old clients (`v1.32.x`, `v1.33.x`) is incompatible with `kube-apiserver v1.34.x`
- Reflectors typically recover by falling back to standard `LIST/WATCH`
- Users may see noisy logs and lose the WatchList optimization



### Environment

- client-go version: `v1.32.x`
- Kubernetes server version: `v1.34.x`


### Relevant references

- old client WatchList path in `client-go v1.32`
- removal of `kubernetes.io/initial-events-list-blueprint` in Kubernetes `v1.34`
- reflector WatchList flow in newer `client-go` using `temporaryStore` + `initial-events-end` bookmark

### Related PR

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/127587
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/132326

title: User Namespace: Allow simultaneous use of hostNetwork and userns
body:
This appears to be a legacy issue. Based on our [historical discussions](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/111090#discussion_r936033887), there is no inherent problem with using `hostNetwork` and userns simultaneously. The restriction exists primarily because certain underlying container runtimes, like runc, lack support for this combination. However, other runtimes, such as crun, do support this functionality.

The static pods for Kubernetes control plane components require the use of hostNetwork. However, due to security requirements, they also need to utilize user namespaces. To enable these control plane static pods to use the user namespace feature, we propose lifting this restriction.

title: apimachinery: Quantity.String() skips canonicalization for inputs with 3n decimal places
body:
### What happened?

`ParseQuantity("1.001").String()` returns `"1.001"` instead of the canonical form `"1001m"`.
This affects any decimal input where the number of decimal places is a multiple of 3 (3, 6, 9).

### Root cause

In 
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/eb8032bb8313640f57d32560b90269618524e9c6/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/resource/quantity.go#L278
 the fast-path caching check:
    `if scale%3 == 0 && !strings.HasSuffix(shifted, "000") && shifted[0] != '0'`
incorrectly caches the raw input string as canonical when the input contains a decimal point.
The fix is to add `len(denom) == 0` to ensure only inputs without a decimal point are cached.

**Kubernetes version:** v1.35.x


### What did you expect to happen?

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/eb8032bb8313640f57d32560b90269618524e9c6/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/resource/quantity.go#L278

`ParseQuantity("1.001").String()` should return `"1001m"`, consistent with how other decimal inputs are canonicalized (e.g. `"1.44"` → `"1440m"`).
Inputs with 1, 2, or 4 decimal places canonicalize correctly. Only multiples of 3 are affected.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Under

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/eb8032bb8313640f57d32560b90269618524e9c6/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/resource/quantity_test.go#L789

Add follow testing cases
```
		{"1.001", "1001m"},
		{"1.0001", "1000100u"},
		{"1.00001", "1000010u"},
		{"1.000001", "1000001u"},
		{"1.0000001", "1000000100n"},
		{"1.00000001", "1000000010n"},
		{"1.000000001", "1000000001n"},
```
Then the error messages are expected to see here whose decimal places is a multiple of 3 (3, 6, 9).
```
"1.001": expected 1001m, got 1.001
"1.000001": expected 1000001u, got 1.000001
"1.000000001": expected 1000000001n, got 1.000000001
```

title: [Declarative Validation] Enable `k8s-ip` format in `+k8s:format` declarative validation tag
body:
Enable the `k8s-ip` format value in the existing `+k8s:format` declarative validation (DV) tag and potentially add `k8s-ipv4` / `k8s-ipv6` family-specific variants. This corresponds to the OpenAPI `format: ipv4` and `format: ipv6` keywords.

**Current status:** `k8s-ip` is already **documented** in the `Docs()` function of `validators/format.go` (line 133) and the validator variable `ipSloppyValidator` referencing `strfmt.IPSloppy()` exists (commented out, line 54). The switch case is **commented out** (lines 93-98) with a TODO:

```go
// TODO: uncomment the following when we've done the homework
// to be sure it works the current state of IP manual-ratcheting
/*
    case "k8s-ip":
        return Function(formatTagName, DefaultFlags, ipSloppyValidator), nil
*/
```

## Motivation

IP address validation is one of the most common string validations in Kubernetes, used extensively across networking, service, and node APIs. OpenAPI supports `format: ipv4` and `format: ipv6` as standard formats. The infrastructure is already in place — this issue tracks resolving the ratcheting concern and enabling it.

## Kubernetes API Example

**`PodStatus.PodIP`** and IP validation across `pkg/apis/core/validation/validation.go`:

```go
// IP address validation pattern used in many places:
if net.ParseIP(value) == nil {
    allErrs = append(allErrs, field.Invalid(fldPath, value, "must be a valid IP address"))
}
```

With the format enabled:

```go
type PodStatus struct {
    // +k8s:format=k8s-ip
    PodIP string
}
```

## OpenAPI Semantics

- **OpenAPI formats:** `ipv4` (RFC 2673 dotted-quad), `ipv6` (RFC 5954)
- **kube-openapi strfmt:** registered in `strfmt/default.go` with `net.ParseIP()`

## DV Design Considerations

- **Ratcheting concern (the blocker):** The TODO mentions "IP manual-ratcheting." Some existing IP fields in Kubernetes have historically accepted slightly malformed IPs (e.g., leading zeros in IPv4 octets like `192.168.01.1`). The `IPSloppy()` validator already accounts for this by using `netutils.ParseIPSloppy()`. The concern is whether DV's automatic ratcheting (skip re-validation of unchanged fields on update) interacts correctly with the sloppy parsing, especially for fields that were previously validated with different strictness levels.
- **Sloppy vs. strict:** The validator references `IPSloppy` which uses `netutils.ParseIPSloppy()`. This is intentional — it matches the historical leniency of Kubernetes IP validation. New strict-only IP fields might want a `k8s-ip-strict` variant in the future.
- **IPv4/IPv6 variants:** Consider whether to add `k8s-ipv4` and `k8s-ipv6` for fields that must be a specific IP family (e.g., `ClusterIP` when dual-stack is not enabled).
- **Naming convention:** Follows existing `k8s-` prefix pattern used by all other DV formats.

## Implementation Notes

- Primary work: resolve the ratcheting concern documented in the TODO, then uncomment lines 54 and 93-98 in `validators/format.go`
- Runtime function already exists: `strfmt.IPSloppy()` in `k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/validate`
- Very high priority — IP validation is extremely common across the Kubernetes API surface
- Validator file: `staging/src/k8s.io/code-generator/cmd/validation-gen/validators/format.go`

/sig api-machinery
/triage accepted
/area api-validation

title: VolumeRestrictions RemovePod assumes prefilter state exists even when PreFilter returned Skip
body:
### What happened?

VolumeRestrictions seems to have an inconsistent preemption contract.

  PreFilter() may return Skip without writing PreFilterVolumeRestrictions into CycleState, but during preemption simulation the framework may still call RunPreFilterExtensionRemovePod(), which reaches VolumeRestrictions.RemovePod(). RemovePod() then unconditionally reads the prefilter state and fails with:

  running RemovePod on PreFilter plugin "VolumeRestrictions": cannot read "PreFilterVolumeRestrictions" from cycleState

  This looks like a framework/plugin contract bug in the interaction between PreFilter, PreFilterExtensions, and RemovePod during preemption.

### What did you expect to happen?

Expected behavior would be one of:
  - RemovePod() treats missing state as a no-op,
  - the framework avoids calling RemovePod() for skipped prefilter paths, or
  - PreFilter() always initializes state even when returning Skip.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

A likely minimal reproducer is a scheduler/framework test with the following steps:

  1. Create a pod that will go through preemption handling.
  2. Run VolumeRestrictions.PreFilter() in a case where it returns Skip.
  3. Verify that PreFilterVolumeRestrictions is not written into CycleState.
  4. Simulate victim removal by calling RunPreFilterExtensionRemovePod().
  5. Observe that the framework still dispatches to VolumeRestrictions.RemovePod().
  6. Observe that RemovePod() fails because it unconditionally reads missing state from CycleState.

  Observed error:

  running RemovePod on PreFilter plugin "VolumeRestrictions": cannot read "PreFilterVolumeRestrictions" from cycleState

  This suggests the bug is reproducible entirely within scheduler preemption/framework tests, without relying on cluster-specific behavior.

title: kubelet: SyncPod kills liveness-failed containers sequentially, blocking replacement starts
body:
## What happened?

When multiple containers in a pod fail liveness probes, kubelet's `SyncPod()` kills them sequentially in Step 3 — each `killContainer()` call blocks for up to `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` before moving to the next container. Step 8 (start replacements) only runs after the entire Step 3 kill loop finishes.

A container killed early in the loop cannot get its replacement until all sibling kills in the same cycle complete.

Reproduced with 4 containers, `terminationGracePeriodSeconds=30`, and a `preStop` hook that sleeps 25s. All 4 containers shared one liveness file; removing it caused all 4 to fail simultaneously.

Container restart timestamps from `kubectl logs` and `kubectl logs --previous`:

```
07:08:43  Liveness file removed — all 4 containers fail

Cycle A: kubelet picks up app-a (1 container in this SyncPod cycle)
  07:09:15  app-a STARTED (new container) ← ~30s to restart, expected

Cycle B: kubelet picks up app-b, app-c, app-d (3 containers in one cycle)
  Kill events spaced ~30s apart (= preStop duration), confirming sequential:
    Killing app-b
    Killing app-c  (31s after app-b)
    Killing app-d  (38s after app-c)
  07:10:54  app-b STARTED ← 68 seconds dead, waited for app-c + app-d kills
  07:10:55  app-c STARTED ← 39 seconds dead, waited for app-d kill
  07:10:55  app-d STARTED ← immediate after its own kill
```

app-b was killed at 07:09:46 but could not restart until 07:10:54 because kubelet was still sequentially killing app-c and app-d in the same Step 3 loop. With longer `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` (e.g., 300s for connection draining), the first-killed container in a 4-container cycle would wait **15 minutes** instead of 5.

Additional observations:
- The kill order within a cycle is non-deterministic (`ContainersToKill` is a Go map)
- How many containers end up in each cycle is timing-dependent: `computePodActions()` snapshots the liveness cache; only containers that have already crossed `failureThreshold` at that instant are included

## What did you expect to happen?

A container's replacement should start as soon as its own kill completes, without waiting for sibling container kills to finish.

The whole-pod kill path (`killContainersWithSyncResult` at `kuberuntime_container.go:886-921`) already kills containers in parallel using goroutines + `sync.WaitGroup`. The per-container liveness restart path should either:
1. Parallelize kills using the same pattern, or
2. Start each replacement immediately after its specific kill completes

## How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: sequential-kill-repro
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: repro
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: repro
    spec:
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
      volumes:
      - name: shared-health
        emptyDir:
          medium: Memory
      initContainers:
      - name: init-health
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["touch", "/shared/healthy"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: shared-health
          mountPath: /shared
      containers:
      - name: app-a
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "echo \"$(date -u +%H:%M:%S) [app-a] STARTED\"; sleep infinity"]
        livenessProbe:
          exec:
            command: ["cat", "/shared/healthy"]
          periodSeconds: 1
          failureThreshold: 1
        volumeMounts:
        - name: shared-health
          mountPath: /shared
        lifecycle:
          preStop:
            exec:
              command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 25"]
      - name: app-b
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "echo \"$(date -u +%H:%M:%S) [app-b] STARTED\"; sleep infinity"]
        livenessProbe:
          exec:
            command: ["cat", "/shared/healthy"]
          periodSeconds: 1
          failureThreshold: 1
        volumeMounts:
        - name: shared-health
          mountPath: /shared
        lifecycle:
          preStop:
            exec:
              command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 25"]
      - name: app-c
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "echo \"$(date -u +%H:%M:%S) [app-c] STARTED\"; sleep infinity"]
        livenessProbe:
          exec:
            command: ["cat", "/shared/healthy"]
          periodSeconds: 1
          failureThreshold: 1
        volumeMounts:
        - name: shared-health
          mountPath: /shared
        lifecycle:
          preStop:
            exec:
              command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 25"]
      - name: app-d
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "echo \"$(date -u +%H:%M:%S) [app-d] STARTED\"; sleep infinity"]
        livenessProbe:
          exec:
            command: ["cat", "/shared/healthy"]
          periodSeconds: 1
          failureThreshold: 1
        volumeMounts:
        - name: shared-health
          mountPath: /shared
        lifecycle:
          preStop:
            exec:
              command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 25"]
```

Steps:
1. `kubectl apply -f repro.yaml` — wait for 4/4 Running
2. `kubectl exec <pod> -c app-a -- rm /shared/healthy` — all 4 fail at once
3. Wait ~2 minutes, then check start times:
   ```
   for c in app-a app-b app-c app-d; do
     echo "=== $c ==="
     kubectl logs <pod> -c $c
     kubectl logs <pod> -c $c --previous
   done
   ```
4. Observe: containers killed later in the Step 3 loop restart at the same time as the last-killed container. Containers killed early waited much longer than their own preStop duration.
5. Check `kubectl describe pod <pod>` — Killing events are spaced ~30s apart (= preStop duration), confirming sequential blocking.

## Anything else we need to know?

Source code references (v1.34.0):

| Code | Location |
|------|----------|
| Step 3 sequential kill loop | `pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/kuberuntime_manager.go:1241-1251` |
| `killContainer()` blocks synchronously | `pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/kuberuntime_container.go:818-882` |
| Step 8 start loop (only after all kills) | `pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/kuberuntime_manager.go:1489-1492` |
| Parallel kill pattern (whole-pod only) | `pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/kuberuntime_container.go:886-921` |
| Pod worker serialization | `pkg/kubelet/pod_workers.go:980-990` |
| `ContainersToKill` is a Go map | `pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/kuberuntime_manager.go:1007-1008` |

`killContainersWithSyncResult()` at `kuberuntime_container.go:886-921` already implements parallel container kills with goroutines + WaitGroup, but is only used for the whole-pod teardown path. The per-container restart path in Step 3 uses a simple sequential `for range` over the map.

Suggested fix directions:
1. Parallelize Step 3 kills for regular container restarts using the same goroutine + `sync.WaitGroup` pattern from `killContainersWithSyncResult()`
2. Or better: a kill-start pipeline where each container's replacement starts immediately after its own kill completes, without waiting for siblings

Either fix should be scoped to regular container restarts in an unchanged sandbox (not init containers, not sandbox recreation, not resize).

Related: #131690 — liveness failure does not mark container not-ready, so during the sequential kill wait, containers in preStop still pass readiness probes and receive traffic. Distinct but compounding issue.

title: Node reboot leaving existing pod using resources stuck with error UnexpectedAdmissionError
body:
### What happened?

When a node is rebooted, pod using resources allocated by device plugin will encounter UnexpectedAdmissionError error as below:

```
  Warning  UnexpectedAdmissionError  84s                kubelet            Allocate failed due to no healthy devices present; cannot allocate unhealthy devices xxx, which is unexpected
```

What makes it really bad is if it's a raw pod, it stucks in such state and never recover.

### What did you expect to happen?

The pod should be retried until device plugin is ready

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. create a pod requesting any resources allocated via a device plugin
2. reboot the node
3. observe pod failure


### Anything else we need to know?

The behavior is introduced with #116376

And there are various issues opened around kubelet restart #118559 #124345

But this issue is about node restart. When node is restarted, kubelet started to rerun existing pods in random order. So a pod can run into this issue before device plugin pod is healthy on the node

title: Add multiply/divide to the CEL resource library in kubernetes
body:
### What would you like to be added?

There's currently no support for multiplication and division for the kubernetes `resource.Quantity` type in CEL. Ideally, the two operations should be added as `resource.quantity(10).mul(2)`, `resource.quantity(10).div(2)` and a `resource.quantity(10).div(3, 4)` for specifying decimal rounding

### Why is this needed?

CEL expressions used to generate kubernetes resources can benefit from referencing existing resources and perform such mathematical operations on existing resources to calculate another desired value from them

title: CRD validation uses separate CRD->OpenAPI conversion from SSA
body:
### What happened?

We appear to have two methods for creating kube-openapi's spec.Schema type being employed today.

For validation, there is a direct conversion `CustomResourceValidation -> spec.Schema` written in an ad-hoc function for validation. This schema is used to perform validation of CRs against the schema.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/694698ca3801fe5aa258d58c1e27ac7f88c29d35/staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apiserver/validation/validation.go#L145-L306

For SSA, a separate path is used: `CustomResourceValidation -> StructuralSchema -> ToKubeOpenAPI` 

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/694698ca3801fe5aa258d58c1e27ac7f88c29d35/staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apiserver/schema/kubeopenapi.go#L23-L45

There is an old comment with a TODO to replace the validator's usage of `ConvertJSONSchemaPropsWithPostProcess` with StructuralSchemas -> ToKubeOpenAPI

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/694698ca3801fe5aa258d58c1e27ac7f88c29d35/staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apiserver/validation/validation.go#L32-L43

### What did you expect to happen?

I think it is an important property to have CRD validation use the same schema as SSA, and go through the same conversion steps. Combining these two Willa also save memory and allow CRDs to scale better.

title: `wait.PollImmediate` timeout not respected when `ConditionFunc` takes a long time to execute
body:
### What happened?

https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/wait#PollImmediate method has a timeout parameter, and is documented as:

> PollImmediate tries a condition func until it returns true, an error, or the timeout is reached. 

Under certain (realistic, non-artificial) conditions, the timeout is not respected and the method continues polling even after the timeout, only terminating much later. This happens when the `ConditionFunc` callback duration is close-ish to the timeout. We saw this happening when `ConditionFunc` contained network calls that were hitting multi-second timeouts:

```
$ cat poll-timeout.go
...
        wait.PollImmediate(3*time.Second, 4*time.Second, func() (bool, error) {
                fmt.Printf("Iteration at %fs\n", time.Since(start).Seconds())
                time.Sleep(5 * time.Second)
                return false, nil
        })
        fmt.Printf("Finished at: %f\n", time.Since(start).Seconds())
...
}

$ go run poll-timeout.go 
Iteration at 0.000000s
Iteration at 8.005522s << expected PollImmediate to terminate here
Iteration at 13.008506s
Finished at: 18.012517
```

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected `PollIteration` to terminate after `ConditionFunc` terminated for the first time after the timeout

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```console
$ cd $(mktemp -d)
$ go mod init test
go: creating new go.mod: module test
$ cat << EOF > poll-timeout.go
package main

import (
        "fmt"
        "time"
        "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/wait"
)

func main() {
        start := time.Now()
        wait.PollImmediate(3*time.Second, 4*time.Second, func() (bool, error) {
                fmt.Printf("Iteration at %fs\n", time.Since(start).Seconds())
                time.Sleep(5 * time.Second)
                return false, nil
        })
        fmt.Printf("Finished at: %f\n", time.Since(start).Seconds())
}
EOF
$ go get k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/wait
go: downloading k8s.io/apimachinery v0.25.4
...
$ go run poll-timeout.go 
Iteration at 0.000000s
Iteration at 8.005522s
Iteration at 13.008506s
Finished at: 18.012517
```

title: DRA: scheduler performance issue with ResourceClaim event handling
body:
## Problem

When a ResourceClaim is created or updated, the scheduler's event handler calls `MoveAllToActiveOrBackoffQueue`, which iterates **every pod** in the unschedulable queue under an exclusive lock to determine which pods should be requeued. At scale, this becomes a  bottleneck.

On a 10,000-node KWOK cluster scheduling DRA pods, `MoveAllToActiveOrBackoffQueue` and its callees consume **~9% of total scheduler CPU** in a 30-second profile window:

```
                                          cum   cum%
  MoveAllToActiveOrBackoffQueue          9.24%
    moveAllToActiveOrBackoffQueue        9.15%
      movePodsToActiveOrBackoffQueue     9.05%
        isPodWorthRequeuing              6.82%
```

The call chain is:

```
informer callback (ResourceClaim Add/Update)
  → MoveAllToActiveOrBackoffQueue()     // acquires exclusive lock
    → moveAllToActiveOrBackoffQueue()   // iterates ALL unschedulable pods
      → movePodsToActiveOrBackoffQueue()
        → isPodWorthRequeuing()         // per-pod hint evaluation
```

Every ResourceClaim event triggers a full scan of the unschedulable pod pool. With N pending pods and M claim events, this is O(N×M) work under the scheduling queue lock, blocking `Pop()` and all other queue operations.

### Observation

ResourceClaims created from a `ResourceClaimTemplate` have an `OwnerReference` pointing to the pod that triggered their creation. For these per-pod claims, only the owning pod needs to be requeued — not every pod in the unschedulable pool.

### Profiling environment

- Kubernetes v1.34.5 (stock scheduler, no modifications)
- 10,000 KWOK nodes, each with one ResourceSlice (1 device per pool)
- DRA pods each with one per-pod ResourceClaim (AllocationMode=All)
- 30-second CPU profile captured during active scheduling

Opening this issue to start the discussion and explore a fix. One possible
approach is to leverage the pod OwnerReference on per-pod claims to requeue
only the affected pod instead of scanning the entire unschedulable pool.

Document the Job positive and negative criteria evaluation orders
body:
### What would you like to be added?

I would like to document the Job positive and negative criteria evaluation orders in the following 3 levels:

- [x] [JobController (KubeControllerManager)](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/bc79d3ba87b8b3c4b7c68f26cdfcaa35654d96ac/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go) Comments: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128569
- [ ] [Job API](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/bc79d3ba87b8b3c4b7c68f26cdfcaa35654d96ac/pkg/apis/batch/types.go) Comments
- [ ] [Job API Documents](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/job/)

/sig apps

### Why is this needed?

As reported in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/117303 and discussed in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121863#issuecomment-2447872050, when the Job meets both the positive (`.spec.completions`, `.spec.successPolicy`, and some else) and negative (`.spec.backoffLimit`, `.spec.activeDeadlineSeconds`, and some else) criteria at the same time, the negative ones are respected, then the Job status looks weird. However, the evaluation orders and status are Job specifications, not any bugs.

It would be better to document the criteria evaluation steps to clarify this behavior. Additionally, users should rely on the `.status.completionTime` instead of `.status.succeeded` to verify if the Job has been succeeded since the `.status.succeeded` is not a terminal state, that is just intermediate state for the JobController.

title: APIServer ends watches way too early, defeating the purpose of sendInitialEvents
body:
### What happened?

We have several large kube clusters with 60,000 to 100,000 pods. This makes the list-then-watch strategy painful because fetching the initial list of pods will frequently take over 3 minutes, and by the time the initial list call completes, you get a "TOO OLD" error when you start the watch after it.

So we're very excited to begin using sendInitialEvents instead, which is supposed to solve this problem. However, in our largest clusters, the API server always closes the watch almost immediately after receiving the initial-events-end BOOKMARK (like under a second).

Because of this, sendInitialEvents does not serve its intended purpose and has the exact same problem as list-then-watch: the resourceVersion for the BOOKMARK end of the initial events is the version at the time the watch started, which is 2-3 minutes before the watch ended, so even if you re-watch after that, you still get a TOO OLD error just like with list-then-watch.

### What did you expect to happen?

I expect the watch to continue until the timeoutSeconds, or at least much longer than 1s after the initial-events-end bookmark is received.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

In a cluster with 80k pods, I dumped the watch stream to a file with curl:
```sh
$ time curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN" -H "Accept: application/json" 'https://YOURSERVER/api/v1/pods?allowWatchBookmarks=true&watch=true&timeoutseconds=3600&sendInitialEvents=true&resourceVersionMatch=NotOlderThan' | ts '[%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S]' > /tmp/watchdata 

real	3m6.176s
user	0m3.732s
sys	0m7.982s
```
You can see that the request runs for a total of 3m6s despite `timeoutSeconds=3600`.


You can then see that there are only 58 events in the file after the BOOKMARK:
```sh
$ grep BOOKMARK /tmp/watchdata -A 99999 | wc -l
58
```
Timestamp of the bookmark:
```
$ grep BOOKMARK /tmp/watchdata -A 99999  | head -n1
[2025-10-23 20:43:52] {"type":"BOOKMARK","object":{"kind":"Pod","apiVersion":"v1","metadata":{"resourceVersion":"46574078021","creationTimestamp":null,"annotations":{"k8s.io/initial-events-end":"true"}},"spec":{"containers":null},"status":{}}}
```
Timestamp of the final event:
```
$ grep BOOKMARK /tmp/watchdata -A 99999  | tail -n1 | head -c 100
[2025-10-23 20:43:52] {"type":"MODIFIED","object":{"kind":"Pod","apiVersion":"v1","metadata":{"name"
```
So the watch ended less than 1s after the bookmark.

### Anything else we need to know?

title: Implement Quota Scope for Label Resource Exclusion
body:
#### What would you like to be added

Extend the ResourceQuota quota scopes mechanism to support excluding Pods and PVCs from quota accounting based on specific labels.
This would enable workloads to mark resources that should not consume quota (e.g., temporary resources during migration or import operations).

Implement [new Quota Scope](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/apis/core/types.go#L6447): `ObjectLabel` managed by resources.k8s.io/ignore annotation on pod/pvc
#### Why is this needed:

Current ResourceQuota scopes [provide](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/policy/resource-quotas/#quota-scopes) limited filtering capabilities. Many use cases require the ability to temporarily exclude resources from quota without modifying application code or resource definitions:
1. **VM/Pod Migration Workflows**: When migrating VMs(pods as virtual machines), a second Pod is created during the migration process. This temporary Pod should not be counted toward the namespace quota until the migration is complete.
2. **Storage Import Operations**: Temporary PVCs created during disk import should not count against storage quotas.
3. **Ephemeral Resources**: Controllers managing temporary resources need a way to mark them as exempt from quota accounting dynamically, even after the resource is created.

It's also worth mentioning #77508 and #110065 with a similar request, here we complement the user case and are ready to help with its implementation.

We can offer several options for implementation for scope usage:

Filter directly by labels:
```yaml
scopeSelector: 
  matchExpressions: 
  - operator: NotIn 
     scopeName: ObjectLabel 
     values: ["workload-type=migration"]
```
We are open to discussion

title: Declarative Validation: Add `+k8s:exclusiveMaximum` declarative validation tag
body:
# Add `+k8s:exclusiveMaximum` declarative validation tag

## Summary

Add a new `+k8s:exclusiveMaximum=<int>` declarative validation (DV) tag that enforces a strict upper bound on numeric fields (value must be strictly less than the specified bound). This corresponds to the OpenAPI/JSON Schema `exclusiveMaximum` keyword.

## Motivation

OpenAPI/JSON Schema supports `exclusiveMaximum` for strict upper bounds. DV currently supports `+k8s:maximum` (inclusive) but has no way to express strict less-than constraints. Several Kubernetes API fields use strict upper bounds in handwritten validation.

## Kubernetes API Example

**`ServiceAccountTokenProjection.ExpirationSeconds`** in `pkg/apis/core/validation/validation.go`:

```go
// Handwritten validation today:
if source.ServiceAccountToken.ExpirationSeconds > 1<<32 {
    allErrs = append(allErrs, field.Invalid(projPath.Child("expirationSeconds"),
        source.ServiceAccountToken.ExpirationSeconds,
        "may not specify a duration larger than 2^32 seconds"))
}
```

With the proposed tag, the strict `< 2^32` bound could be expressed declaratively:

```go
type ServiceAccountTokenProjection struct {
    // +k8s:minimum=600
    // +k8s:exclusiveMaximum=4294967296
    ExpirationSeconds *int64
}
```

## OpenAPI Semantics

- **OpenAPI keyword:** `exclusiveMaximum`
- **JSON Schema Draft-04 (which Kubernetes uses):** `exclusiveMaximum` is a **boolean** that modifies the adjacent `maximum` field. When `true`, the `maximum` value becomes exclusive (`value < maximum` instead of `value <= maximum`).
- **JSON Schema Draft-06+:** `exclusiveMaximum` is a standalone **number** (the exclusive bound itself).

## DV Design Considerations

- **Standalone value vs. boolean modifier:** Same as `+k8s:exclusiveMinimum` — DV should use a standalone value (Draft-06+ style) since it's cleaner for comment tags. The generated OpenAPI schema can emit Draft-04 form (`maximum: 4294967296, exclusiveMaximum: true`).
- **Integer-only types:** The existing `+k8s:maximum` tag only accepts Go integer types — **not floats** (checked via `types.IsInteger(t)` in `limits.go`, value parsed via `util.ParseInt()`). This tag should follow the same constraint.
- **Relationship to `+k8s:maximum`:** Using both `+k8s:maximum` and `+k8s:exclusiveMaximum` on the same field should be an error (mutually exclusive constraints on the upper bound).
- **Large values:** The example uses `4294967296` (2^32). Ensure `util.ParseInt()` handles values that fit in int64 but not int32.

## Implementation Notes

- Should be implemented in `validators/limits.go` alongside existing `minimum`/`maximum` tags
- Should generate a call to a validation function in `k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/validate`
- Validator file: `staging/src/k8s.io/code-generator/cmd/validation-gen/validators/limits.go`

/sig api-machinery
/triage accepted
/area api-validation

title: OpenAPI spec (swagger.json) integer type valid ranges not specified
body:
In the generated [OpenAPI swagger.json](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/api/openapi-spec/swagger.json), integer types such as `ContainerPort` have clearly documented valid ranges in the human-readable comments, but these are not actually specified in the API JSON using [the minimum/maximum/exclusiveMinimum/exclusiveMaximum](https://swagger.io/docs/specification/data-models/data-types/) keywords. This creates problems for statically-typed languages used to generate for the API because they cannot perform this type checking. They can't even make a choice as to whether to represent a given integer quantity as a "natural" or "unsigned" type or a signed one.

I assume the range information is available in some form within the API server that generates the swagger, so would it be possible to include it?

title: [declarative validation] Framework/CI-level checks to prevent merging ineffective or inconsistent Declarative Validation (DV) markers
body:
### What would you like to be added?
CI checks for DV to ensure that DV tags are wired up properly and are used correctly, consistently, and effectively.  Currently this is not the case and incorrect DV tag wiring through strategy, missing DV tags on additional API versions, and lack of associated DV tests etc. passes with CI green.

Example of the Gap:
[PR #138004](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138004) serves as an example of this issue. In this PR, DV tags are added without proper wiring or testing yet CI passes completely green.

Required CI Checks Identified:
1. **API Version Consistency:** If a DV tag is added to a `v1` type, it must also be added to the corresponding `v1beta1`, `v1alpha1`, etc., types (or flagged if intentionally omitted).
2. **Strategy Wiring Verification:** DV added to Go types must actually be wired up to be called by the strategy. 
   - It must be called by all relevant subresource strategies.
3. **Test Coverage Enforcement:** Adding DV markers to a type must require corresponding test coverage. If a tag is added without a test, CI should fail.

### Why is this needed?
This is needed so that it is ~impossible to accidentally merge misleading, ineffective, untested, or inconsistent DV markers** without explicitly acknowledging it via an intentional allowlist.

For API reviewers to be confident in DV when reviewing, they need to be able to trust that a green CI run means the DV wiring and tests are correct. They should only need to spot-check the `types.go` tags and the `_test.go` file. If a contributor forgets to wire up DV, add tests, or apply tags to all API versions, CI should go red and guide the contributor on what to fix (similar to `kube-api-linter`).

/area api-validation
/sig api-machinery
/kind feature

* audit annotations (I think we can detect the problem early enough, but I haven't thought about it to check)
* logging
* metrics, eg a counter of requests that are rejected for this reason. Could have the targeted API as a label dimension (eg `group=authentication.k8s.io` / `api=subjectaccessreviews`)

What do you think about this? I could implement this if you're willing to accept a PR. Please also let me know which option would be the preferred one to take.

### Why is this needed?

Certain API kinds are (by design) exempt from being targeted by ValidatingAdmissionPolicy and MutatingAdmissionPolicy. Unfortunately there is no clear documentation in the [KEP-3488](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-api-machinery/3488-cel-admission-control). Nor was there any documentation in the official Kubernetes docs which resources are affected by this exemption until https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/49520 was merged.

As a user it is still hard to find out if a created VAP/MAP policy targets an exempt API kind because there are no longs, metrics or anything else from the API server side of things.

See also [discussion in Slack](https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C0EG7JC6T/p1738233413818159)

title: PodTopologySpread DoNotSchedule-to-ScheduleAnyway fallback mode
body:
### What would you like to be added?

A mode of operation for PodTopologySpread that allows users to express the flexibility to fallback from DoNotSchedule to ScheduleAnyway after a specific condition is met (e.g., after a defined period of time).

### Why is this needed?

This is needed to force the cluster autoscaler to bring up new nodes in under scaled zones, but fallback to schedule anyway if CA can't because of zonal failure or more commonly stockouts.

/sig scheduling

title: Warnings on missing pull secrets can be confusing
body:
### What happened?

A previous enhancement has added a warning event when a pull secret is missing: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/117927

If the image has pulled successfully because either another pull secret did the job, or the image doesn't need auth, the warning is distracting.

As an example, this pod is running perfectly fine and has no problems, and yet when described, has had 11k warning events emitted over the last 9 days.
```
  Warning  FailedToRetrieveImagePullSecret  114s (x11399 over 9d)  kubelet  Unable to retrieve some image pull secrets (sa-integration); attempting to pull the image may not succeed.
```

We have been including multiple pull secrets in our pulls because it's more flexible to point to a few that may exist than to have to very exactly map each pod to a pull secret. This change means we will get warnings even when everything is working exactly as we wanted it to.

### What did you expect to happen?

No warnings if an image is pulled successfully.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a pod or service account that references a missing pull secret that is not required to pull the image.

### Anything else we need to know?

My suggestion would be to only emit that warning if the image cannot be pulled (for example, reaches ImagePullBackOff), or to include the detail about the missing secret in the existing image pull failure events.

[Declarative Validation] Add `+k8s:minProperties` declarative validation tag
body:
Add a new `+k8s:minProperties=<int>` declarative validation (DV) tag that enforces a minimum number of keys in a map field. This corresponds to the OpenAPI/JSON Schema `minProperties` keyword.

## Motivation

OpenAPI/JSON Schema supports `minProperties` as a standard validation keyword. DV currently has no equivalent. Several Kubernetes API map fields require at least one entry, currently enforced with handwritten validation.

## Kubernetes API Example

**`StorageClass.Parameters`** in `pkg/apis/storage/validation/validation.go`:

```go
// Handwritten validation today:
if !allowEmpty && len(params) == 0 {
    allErrs = append(allErrs, field.Required(fldPath, "must contain at least one key/value pair"))
}
```

With the proposed tag:

```go
type StorageClass struct {
    // +k8s:minProperties=1
    Parameters map[string]string
}
```

## OpenAPI Semantics

- **OpenAPI keyword:** `minProperties`
- **Go type in JSONSchemaProps:** `*int64`
- **Spec behavior:** The object (map) must have at least the specified number of properties/keys. Counts **actually present keys**, not schema-defined fields.

## DV Design Considerations

- **Map types only:** In Go, struct fields are fixed at compile time, so `minProperties` is only meaningful for `map` types. The type check should restrict to `types.Map` kind, unlike `+k8s:minItems` which restricts to `types.Slice`.
- **Relationship to `+k8s:minItems`:** `+k8s:minItems` validates slice/array length. `+k8s:minProperties` validates map key count. They are analogous but for different Go kinds. The implementation pattern in `limits.go` should be similar (parse int value, check type kind, generate validation call).
- **Relationship to `+k8s:required`:** A map field with `+k8s:required` ensures the map itself is non-nil, but doesn't enforce minimum entries. `+k8s:minProperties=1` ensures at least one key exists (a non-nil empty map would fail).
- **Value parsing:** Should use `util.ParseInt()` like other limit tags. Value must be non-negative.

## Implementation Notes

- Should be implemented in `validators/limits.go` alongside existing min/max tags
- Should generate a call to a validation function in `k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/validate`
- Validator file: `staging/src/k8s.io/code-generator/cmd/validation-gen/validators/limits.go`

/sig api-machinery
/triage accepted
/area api-validation

title: Declarative Validation: Add `+k8s:exclusiveMaximum` declarative validation tag
body:
# Add `+k8s:exclusiveMaximum` declarative validation tag

## Summary

Add a new `+k8s:exclusiveMaximum=<int>` declarative validation (DV) tag that enforces a strict upper bound on numeric fields (value must be strictly less than the specified bound). This corresponds to the OpenAPI/JSON Schema `exclusiveMaximum` keyword.

## Motivation

OpenAPI/JSON Schema supports `exclusiveMaximum` for strict upper bounds. DV currently supports `+k8s:maximum` (inclusive) but has no way to express strict less-than constraints. Several Kubernetes API fields use strict upper bounds in handwritten validation.

## Kubernetes API Example

**`ServiceAccountTokenProjection.ExpirationSeconds`** in `pkg/apis/core/validation/validation.go`:

```go
// Handwritten validation today:
if source.ServiceAccountToken.ExpirationSeconds > 1<<32 {
    allErrs = append(allErrs, field.Invalid(projPath.Child("expirationSeconds"),
        source.ServiceAccountToken.ExpirationSeconds,
        "may not specify a duration larger than 2^32 seconds"))
}
```

With the proposed tag, the strict `< 2^32` bound could be expressed declaratively:

```go
type ServiceAccountTokenProjection struct {
    // +k8s:minimum=600
    // +k8s:exclusiveMaximum=4294967296
    ExpirationSeconds *int64
}
```

## OpenAPI Semantics

- **OpenAPI keyword:** `exclusiveMaximum`
- **JSON Schema Draft-04 (which Kubernetes uses):** `exclusiveMaximum` is a **boolean** that modifies the adjacent `maximum` field. When `true`, the `maximum` value becomes exclusive (`value < maximum` instead of `value <= maximum`).
- **JSON Schema Draft-06+:** `exclusiveMaximum` is a standalone **number** (the exclusive bound itself).

## DV Design Considerations

- **Standalone value vs. boolean modifier:** Same as `+k8s:exclusiveMinimum` — DV should use a standalone value (Draft-06+ style) since it's cleaner for comment tags. The generated OpenAPI schema can emit Draft-04 form (`maximum: 4294967296, exclusiveMaximum: true`).
- **Integer-only types:** The existing `+k8s:maximum` tag only accepts Go integer types — **not floats** (checked via `types.IsInteger(t)` in `limits.go`, value parsed via `util.ParseInt()`). This tag should follow the same constraint.
- **Relationship to `+k8s:maximum`:** Using both `+k8s:maximum` and `+k8s:exclusiveMaximum` on the same field should be an error (mutually exclusive constraints on the upper bound).
- **Large values:** The example uses `4294967296` (2^32). Ensure `util.ParseInt()` handles values that fit in int64 but not int32.

## Implementation Notes

- Should be implemented in `validators/limits.go` alongside existing `minimum`/`maximum` tags
- Should generate a call to a validation function in `k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/validate`
- Validator file: `staging/src/k8s.io/code-generator/cmd/validation-gen/validators/limits.go`

/sig api-machinery
/triage accepted
/area api-validation

title: Declarative Validation: Add `+k8s:exclusiveMinimum` declarative validation tag

# Add `+k8s:exclusiveMinimum` declarative validation tag

## Summary

Add a new `+k8s:exclusiveMinimum=<int>` declarative validation (DV) tag that enforces a strict lower bound on numeric fields (value must be strictly greater than the specified bound). This corresponds to the OpenAPI/JSON Schema `exclusiveMinimum` keyword.

## Motivation

OpenAPI/JSON Schema supports `exclusiveMinimum` for strict lower bounds. DV currently supports `+k8s:minimum` (inclusive) but has no way to express strict greater-than constraints. Several Kubernetes API fields use strict bounds in handwritten validation.

## Kubernetes API Example

**`ClientIPConfig.TimeoutSeconds`** in `pkg/apis/core/validation/validation.go`:

```go
// Handwritten validation today:
func validateAffinityTimeout(timeout *int32, fldPath *field.Path) field.ErrorList {
    allErrs := field.ErrorList{}
    if *timeout <= 0 || *timeout > core.MaxClientIPServiceAffinitySeconds {
        allErrs = append(allErrs, field.Invalid(fldPath, timeout,
            fmt.Sprintf("must be greater than 0 and less than %d", core.MaxClientIPServiceAffinitySeconds)))
    }
    return allErrs
}
```

With the proposed tag, the strict `> 0` bound could be expressed declaratively:

```go
type ClientIPConfig struct {
    // +k8s:exclusiveMinimum=0
    // +k8s:maximum=10800
    TimeoutSeconds *int32
}
```

## OpenAPI Semantics

- **OpenAPI keyword:** `exclusiveMinimum`
- **JSON Schema Draft-04 (which Kubernetes uses):** `exclusiveMinimum` is a **boolean** that modifies the adjacent `minimum` field. When `true`, the `minimum` value becomes exclusive (`value > minimum` instead of `value >= minimum`).
- **JSON Schema Draft-06+:** `exclusiveMinimum` is a standalone **number** (the exclusive bound itself).

## DV Design Considerations

- **Standalone value vs. boolean modifier:** The existing `+k8s:minimum` tag is a standalone value. For DV, a standalone `+k8s:exclusiveMinimum=<int>` (Draft-06+ style) is cleaner than a boolean modifier, since comment tags don't compose the same way JSON Schema fields do. The generated OpenAPI schema can still emit Draft-04 form (`minimum: 0, exclusiveMinimum: true`).
- **Integer-only types:** The existing `+k8s:minimum` tag only accepts Go integer types (`int`, `int8`, `int16`, `int32`, `int64`, `uint8`–`uint64`) — **not floats** (checked via `types.IsInteger(t)` in `limits.go`). The tag value is parsed via `util.ParseInt()`. This tag should follow the same constraint unless float support is added to DV limits broadly.
- **Relationship to `+k8s:minimum`:** Using both `+k8s:minimum` and `+k8s:exclusiveMinimum` on the same field should be an error (they are mutually exclusive constraints on the lower bound).

## Implementation Notes

- Should be implemented in `validators/limits.go` alongside existing `minimum`/`maximum` tags
- Should generate a call to a validation function in `k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/validate`
- Validator file: `staging/src/k8s.io/code-generator/cmd/validation-gen/validators/limits.go`

/sig api-machinery
/triage accepted
/area api-validation

title: Declarative Validation: Add `k8s-duration` format to `+k8s:format` declarative validation tag
body:
# Add `k8s-duration` format to `+k8s:format` declarative validation tag

## Summary

Add support for a `k8s-duration` format value in the existing `+k8s:format` declarative validation (DV) tag to validate that a string field contains a valid duration. This corresponds to the OpenAPI `format: duration` keyword.

## Motivation

OpenAPI supports `format: duration` as a standard format. Kubernetes uses duration values in various APIs. While most use typed `metav1.Duration` or integer seconds fields, some string fields hold duration values. Adding this format provides OpenAPI parity.

## Kubernetes API Example

**`metav1.Duration`** wraps Go's `time.Duration` and serializes as a string:

```go
// In staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/duration.go:
type Duration struct {
    time.Duration  // Marshals as e.g., "30s", "5m", "1h30m"
}
```

For string-typed duration fields:

```go
type RetryPolicy struct {
    // +k8s:format=k8s-duration
    BackoffDelay string  // e.g., "30s", "5m"
}
```

Note: Integer-second duration fields like `CertificateSigningRequest.ExpirationSeconds` (`int32`) are handled by `+k8s:minimum`/`+k8s:maximum` instead — format validation only applies to string types.

## OpenAPI Semantics

- **OpenAPI format:** `duration`
- **kube-openapi strfmt:** registered in `strfmt/duration.go`, supports both Go duration format (`30s`, `5m`) and Scala-style durations

## DV Design Considerations

- **Go duration vs. ISO 8601:** Two competing formats exist:
  - **Go style:** `time.ParseDuration()` — `30s`, `5m`, `1h30m` — this is what Kubernetes uses natively via `metav1.Duration`
  - **ISO 8601:** `P1DT12H30M` — used in some external standards
  - DV should use **Go style** since that's what `metav1.Duration` and the Kubernetes ecosystem already use.
- **`+k8s:format` only applies to string types:** Same constraint as all format validators — checked via `t != types.String` in `format.go` line 70. `metav1.Duration` is a struct (not a string), so this format would only apply to raw string fields.
- **Naming convention:** Follows existing `k8s-` prefix pattern.
- **Lower priority** — most k8s durations use typed `metav1.Duration` or integer seconds fields.

## Implementation Notes

- Should be added to the format switch in `validators/format.go`
- Runtime validation should use `time.ParseDuration()`
- Validator file: `staging/src/k8s.io/code-generator/cmd/validation-gen/validators/format.go`

/sig api-machinery
/triage accepted
/area api-validation

title: Declarative Validation: Add `k8s-date` format to `+k8s:format` declarative validation tag
body:
# Add `k8s-date` format to `+k8s:format` declarative validation tag

## Summary

Add support for a `k8s-date` format value in the existing `+k8s:format` declarative validation (DV) tag to validate that a string field contains a valid date in RFC3339 full-date format (`YYYY-MM-DD`). This corresponds to the OpenAPI `format: date` keyword.

## Motivation

OpenAPI supports `format: date` as a standard format. While less common than datetime in core Kubernetes APIs, date-only fields appear in certificate management, scheduling, and lifecycle contexts. Adding this format provides OpenAPI parity.

## Kubernetes API Example

Certificate-related APIs and annotation values sometimes use date-only strings:

```go
// Expiry dates, scheduled maintenance windows, etc.
type MaintenanceWindow struct {
    // +k8s:format=k8s-date
    ScheduledDate string  // e.g., "2025-03-15"
}
```

## OpenAPI Semantics

- **OpenAPI format:** `date`
- **JSON Schema spec:** RFC 3339, section 5.6 full-date (`YYYY-MM-DD`)
- **kube-openapi strfmt:** registered in `strfmt/date.go`

## DV Design Considerations

- **`+k8s:format` only applies to string types:** Same constraint as all format validators — checked via `t != types.String` in `format.go` line 70.
- **Relationship to `k8s-date-time`:** `k8s-date` validates date-only (`2025-03-15`), while `k8s-date-time` validates full timestamp (`2025-03-15T12:00:00Z`). These are independent formats, not hierarchical.
- **Naming convention:** Follows existing `k8s-` prefix pattern and JSON Schema style (lowercase, hyphenated).
- **Lower priority** — most k8s date/time fields use `metav1.Time`, but useful for OpenAPI completeness.

## Implementation Notes

- Should be added to the format switch in `validators/format.go`
- Runtime validation should parse as `YYYY-MM-DD` (e.g., `time.Parse("2006-01-02", ...)`)
- Validator file: `staging/src/k8s.io/code-generator/cmd/validation-gen/validators/format.go`

/sig api-machinery
/triage accepted
/area api-validation

# Add `k8s-date-time` format to `+k8s:format` declarative validation tag

## Summary

Add support for a `k8s-date-time` format value in the existing `+k8s:format` declarative validation (DV) tag to validate that a string field contains a valid RFC3339 datetime with timezone (e.g., `2023-01-15T12:00:00Z`). This corresponds to the OpenAPI `format: date-time` keyword.

## Motivation

OpenAPI supports `format: date-time` as a standard format. While most Kubernetes timestamp fields use the typed `metav1.Time` (which handles serialization/validation via its Go type), some string fields hold datetime values. Adding this format provides OpenAPI parity.

## Kubernetes API Example

Most k8s timestamps use `metav1.Time` (a Go struct wrapping `time.Time`), which serializes as RFC3339:

```go
// In staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/time.go:
type Time struct {
    time.Time  // Marshals to RFC3339 format
}
```

For string-typed timestamp fields (e.g., annotation values, CRD-adjacent types):

```go
type AuditAnnotation struct {
    // +k8s:format=k8s-date-time
    Timestamp string
}
```

## OpenAPI Semantics

- **OpenAPI format:** `date-time`
- **JSON Schema spec:** RFC 3339, section 5.6 (e.g., `2023-01-15T12:00:00Z`)
- **kube-openapi strfmt:** registered in `strfmt/time.go`, validated with multiple RFC3339 variants

## DV Design Considerations

- **`+k8s:format` only applies to string types:** The existing format validator checks `t != types.String` (line 70 of `format.go`). This format would only apply to raw string fields holding datetime values, NOT to `metav1.Time` fields (which are structs, not strings). This is appropriate — `metav1.Time` already handles its own validation via marshaling.
- **Naming convention:** Follows existing `k8s-` prefix pattern. Use `k8s-date-time` (hyphenated, matching JSON Schema style referenced in `format.go` line 84-86).
- **Lower priority** for core k8s APIs since most use typed `metav1.Time`, but useful for OpenAPI completeness and edge cases with raw string timestamps.

## Implementation Notes

- Should be added to the format switch in `validators/format.go`
- Runtime validation should use `time.Parse(time.RFC3339, ...)`
- Validator file: `staging/src/k8s.io/code-generator/cmd/validation-gen/validators/format.go`

/sig api-machinery
/triage accepted
/area api-validation

title: RFE: Policy on versioning e2e tests
body:
**FEATURE REQUEST**:
Objective: Ensure a newer build of e2e tests can run a the tests on older clusters without having failures, and ensure upgrade tests don't test deprecated features.

Currently if a new feature adds coverage to the e2es there is no version information that denotes that this feature is new and may not work on an older version.  We should ensure that the e2es in question check the server version and make certain >= to the version it was introduced in.  

Also on a similar note we should cherry-pick a check of <= on issues where we know features are going to be deprecated.  

This has caused a bunch of consternation on upgrade tests and has wasted copious amounts of time.  It should be the sig-leads responsibility to ensure that the tests are in order prior to code freeze for a given cycle.    

/kind feature 
/cc @kubernetes/sig-testing-feature-requests @kubernetes/sig-release-feature-requests

title: Feature gates to bypass in-tree plugin registration dropped without first graduating
body:
### What happened?

In the upcoming v1.31 release, we plan to drop some alpha feature gates; see 
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/126406#issuecomment-2255700515
However, people may have been setting these feature gates (even thought they have no effect).

Per https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/feature-gates.md, we should lock them to true for at least one release before removal.



### What did you expect to happen?

[For each feature gate] the feature gate cannot actually be disabled, but is documented as locked to true. Specifiying the feature gate on the command line does not cause component failure.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Read the code / try explicitly disabling these feature gates.

### Anything else we need to know?

I think this is a release blocker until we decide how we'll handle it.

If we leave things as they are, we should clearly call out the snag in the release notes.

title: Unable to verify cosign signature for kubectl 1.35.0 on amd64
body:
### What happened?

After downloading kubectl 1.35.0, I attempted to verify the cosign keyless signature. This failed for amd64 but succeeds for arm64.

I used the following command:

```bash
# amd64
cosign verify-blob https://dl.k8s.io/release/v1.35.0/bin/linux/amd64/kubectl \
    --signature https://dl.k8s.io/release/v1.35.0/bin/linux/amd64/kubectl.sig \
    --certificate https://dl.k8s.io/release/v1.35.0/bin/linux/amd64/kubectl.cert \
    --certificate-oidc-issuer https://accounts.google.com \
    --certificate-identity krel-staging@k8s-releng-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com

# arm64
cosign verify-blob https://dl.k8s.io/release/v1.35.0/bin/linux/arm64/kubectl \
    --signature https://dl.k8s.io/release/v1.35.0/bin/linux/arm64/kubectl.sig \
    --certificate https://dl.k8s.io/release/v1.35.0/bin/linux/arm64/kubectl.cert \
    --certificate-oidc-issuer https://accounts.google.com \
    --certificate-identity krel-staging@k8s-releng-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```

### What did you expect to happen?

The command should have printed:

```plaintext
Verified OK
```

But the error message was:

```plaintext
Error: searching log query: [POST /api/v1/log/entries/retrieve][400] searchLogQueryBadRequest {"code":400,"message":"verifying signature: invalid signature when validating ASN.1 encoded signature"}
error during command execution: searching log query: [POST /api/v1/log/entries/retrieve][400] searchLogQueryBadRequest {"code":400,"message":"verifying signature: invalid signature when validating ASN.1 encoded signature"}
```

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```bash
# amd64
cosign verify-blob https://dl.k8s.io/release/v1.35.0/bin/linux/amd64/kubectl \
    --signature https://dl.k8s.io/release/v1.35.0/bin/linux/amd64/kubectl.sig \
    --certificate https://dl.k8s.io/release/v1.35.0/bin/linux/amd64/kubectl.cert \
    --certificate-oidc-issuer https://accounts.google.com \
    --certificate-identity krel-staging@k8s-releng-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com

# arm64
cosign verify-blob https://dl.k8s.io/release/v1.35.0/bin/linux/arm64/kubectl \
    --signature https://dl.k8s.io/release/v1.35.0/bin/linux/arm64/kubectl.sig \
    --certificate https://dl.k8s.io/release/v1.35.0/bin/linux/arm64/kubectl.cert \
    --certificate-oidc-issuer https://accounts.google.com \
    --certificate-identity krel-staging@k8s-releng-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```

### Anything else we need to know?

The SHA256 of kubectl 1.35.0 for amd64 is a2e984a18a0c063279d692533031c1eff93a262afcc0afdc517375432d060989.

The corresponding Rekor UUID is https://search.sigstore.dev/?uuid=108e9186e8c5677a0d75f1d86fbb64dd10a3e796fe62fa95e6b4707ceec7e91cfe741ba456a23bc0

The Rekor entry shows that for amd64 the signature matches but the certificate does not.

title: Unable to SSA remove array entry containing nested field with "foreign" owner
body:
### What happened?

We are in the process of removing a long-time deprecated API version in one of our internal operators. We have done this process before, and are familiar with how it should be done. But since then, we have migrated all our code to use SSA. While this in general has been a pleasant experience, we hit a major issue when our CI/CD pipeline attempted to delete obsolete webhooks from our webhook configuration resources (using SSA). We have both validating and mutating webhooks. The same error was reported for both, and I will use the validating webhook in the following description.

When the pipeline attempts to SSA the webhook configuration, we got the following error:

````
Error from server (Invalid): ValidatingWebhookConfiguration.admissionregistration.k8s.io "application-operator-validating-webhook-configuration" is invalid: [webhooks[2].sideEffects: Required value: must specify one of None, NoneOnDryRun, webhooks[2].clientConfig: Required value: exactly one of url or service is required, webhooks[2].admissionReviewVersions: Required value: must specify one of v1, v1beta1]
````

Pretty cryptic error message, but I am pretty sure this is caused by "foreign" ownership to selected nested fields in the array item that the pipeline is trying to remove, making the item retain with invalid configuration and thus rejected by the SSA. Looking at the managed fields confirms my suspicion:

````yaml
managedFields:
    - manager: cert-manager-cainjector
      operation: Apply
      apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
      time: '2024-09-03T08:00:49Z'
      fieldsType: FieldsV1
      fieldsV1:
        'f:webhooks':
          'k:{"name":"v1alpha1-stasjob-validator.stas.statnett.no"}':
            .: {}
            'f:clientConfig':
              'f:caBundle': {}
            'f:name': {}
          'k:{"name":"v1beta2-application-validator.stas.statnett.no"}':
            .: {}
            'f:clientConfig':
              'f:caBundle': {}
            'f:name': {}
          'k:{"name":"v1beta2-stasjob-validator.stas.statnett.no"}':
            .: {}
            'f:clientConfig':
              'f:caBundle': {}
            'f:name': {}
````

As we use cert-manager to inject the webhook CA bundle, it owns a single nested field in each array item as expected. Note: We have enabled the ServerSideApply feature gate in cert-manager, if that matters.

### What did you expect to happen?

I would expect the obsolete/removed webhook to be removed without error from the array of webhooks in the webhook configuration resource.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

There are probably many ways to reproduce this issue. But to reproduce the issue in the same context as us, I would suggest the following:

1. Install cert-manager with mostly default options. We have enabled the c-m ServerSideApply feature gate, but I don't think it matters.
2. Add/update a ValidatingWebhookConfiguration containing at least two webhooks **using SSA**.
3. Create a cert-manager `Certificate` for your webhook.
4. Request injection of webhook CA bundle by cert-manager ca-injector adding an annotation to the VWC: `cert-manager.io/inject-ca-from: $(CERTIFICATE_NAMESPACE)/$(CERTIFICATE_NAME)`
5. Wait for cert-manager to reconcile the VWC (`caBundle` should be injected)
6. Attempt to remove one of the webhooks from the VMC, still **using SSA**:

### Anything else we need to know?

This issue was initially raised on sig-api-machinery Slack: https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C0EG7JC6T/p1728996348284339

It is also worth mentioning that a temporary rollback to use client-side apply (a.k.a. Update) in our pipeline appears as a workaround for this issue. We successfully used this approach to finalize our removal of the obsolete API version.

$ kubectl version

title: `iptables.minSyncPeriod` working on iptables-restore start, rather than completion
body:
### What happened?

Was looking into the use/adjustment of minSyncPeriod of `kube-proxy` in my clusters and have seen that `minSyncPeriod` is measured based off of sync-start to sync-start, rather than completion of last sync to the start of the next sync.

See an example below, where my `minSyncPeriod` is set to 14s, and the time between completion of last sync, and start of next sync, is only 12 seconds. BUT, the time between sync-start to sync-start, is the actual 14s minSyncPeriod time.
```
I0327 21:36:58.067431       1 proxier.go:815] "Syncing iptables rules" ipFamily="IPv4" fullSync=false
I0327 21:36:59.360840       1 proxier.go:1536] "Reloading service iptables data" ipFamily="IPv4" numServices=3595 numEndpoints=138792 numFilterChains=6 numFilterRules=46 numNATChains=12044 numNATRules=38841
I0327 21:37:00.882055       1 proxier.go:809] "SyncProxyRules complete" ipFamily="IPv4" elapsed="2.837692607s"
I0327 21:37:12.067991       1 proxier.go:815] "Syncing iptables rules" ipFamily="IPv4" fullSync=false
```



### What did you expect to happen?

Doing some checking of the KP code, I came across the [boundedFrequencyRunner](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/16c5a6be07bb2eab06b6e7732eb1cb759a7fe61c/pkg/proxy/runner/bounded_frequency_runner.go#L44-L62) code comments which mention the below, **seemingly contradicting what sounds like is supposed to happen.**
```
// The runner guarantees two properties:
//  1. Minimum Interval (`minInterval`): At least `minInterval` must pass between
//     the *completion* of one execution and the *start* of the next. Calls to
//     `Run()` during this cooldown period are coalesced and deferred until the
//     interval expires. This prevents burst executions.
```

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

  replicas: 50

      role: backend

    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 25%
      maxUnavailable: 25%
    type: RollingUpdate

    metadata:
      creationTimestamp: null
      labels:
        app: nginx
        role: backend
    spec:
      containers:
      - image: nginx:stable
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        name: nginx
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
          protocol: TCP
```

MIN=50
MAX=100

while true; do
  echo "$(date) - Scaling up to $MAX"

title: Daemonset Status is not updated when Pod create fails
body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


#### What happened:
A Daemonset's status field was not updated following its failure to create Pods.


#### What you expected to happen:
A Daemonset's `.status.desiredNumberScheduled` should be set to match the number of matched nodes and `.status.numberUnavailable` should be set to reflect any failures where the daemon pods are not running or available even when a Pod cannot be created (i.e. due to lack of pod quota).

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):
```
$ kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: quota
spec:
  hard:
    pods: '0'
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  labels:
    app: kuard
  name: kuard
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: kuard
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: kuard
    spec:
      containers:
      - image: gcr.io/kuar-demo/kuard-amd64:1
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        name: kuard
        resources: {}
EOF
```

```
$ kubectl get ds kuard -o json | jq .status
{
  "currentNumberScheduled": 0,
  "desiredNumberScheduled": 0,
  "numberMisscheduled": 0,
  "numberReady": 0
}
```

The above should have `numberUnavailable` set to `1` and `desiredNumberScheduled` set to 1.


```
$ kubectl get events
20s         Warning   FailedCreate             daemonset/kuard              Error creating: pods "kuard-hdpxb" is forbidden: exceeded quota: compute-resources, requested: pods=1, used: pods=0, limited: pods=0
1s          Warning   FailedCreate             daemonset/kuard              (combined from similar events): Error creating: pods "kuard-xcpgm" is forbidden: exceeded quota: compute-resources, requested: pods=1, used: pods=0, limited: pods=0
```

It is only after the pod creation is unblocked does status get updated:
```
$ kubectl delete quota quota
resourcequota "quota" deleted
$ # Wait some time for retry
$ kubectl get ds kuard -o json | jq .status
{
  "currentNumberScheduled": 1,
  "desiredNumberScheduled": 1,
  "numberAvailable": 1,
  "numberMisscheduled": 0,
  "numberReady": 1,
  "observedGeneration": 1,
  "updatedNumberScheduled": 1
}
```

#### Anything else we need to know?:
Just some conjecturing but it seems that `updateDaemonSetStatus` should be
called even in the event of a pod error during `dsc.manage` in a similar way
that the replica set controller calls `updateReplicaSetStatus` when there is an
error from `rsc.manageReplicas`.

#### Environment:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
```
$ kubectl version
Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"20", GitVersion:"v1.20.2", GitCommit:"faecb196815e248d3ecfb03c680a4507229c2a56", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2021-01-13T13:28:09Z", GoVersion:"go1.15.5", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}
